`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

If you don't want to use the docker image as above, you can also build all from source:

Install `vllm-ascend` from source, refer to [installation](../../getting_started/installation.html).

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to set up the environment on each node.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Run the following script to execute PD-colocated online inference.

```shell
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=CCU_SCHED
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1

vllm serve /root/.cache/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731  \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --data-parallel-size 8 \
    --prefill-context-parallel-size 1 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --block-size 32 \
    --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}' \
    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":"True","multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true}' \
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

Service Verification: Use the API port configured for the selected deployment. For the 950DT example, use port `8000`.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "dsv4",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 256,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected Result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON response containing the `choices` field.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

single-node PD separation on 950DT products (96GB × 8).

#### 950DT products PD Separation Deployment with DSpark[](#524-950dt-series-pd-separation-deployment)

This section describes PD separation on a single 950DT products node (96GB × 8). The Prefill instance uses DP1/TP1 with PCP4 on NPUs 0–3, while the Decode instances use DP4/TP1 with PCP1 on NPUs 4–7. KV Cache is transferred from Prefill to Decode using MooncakeConnectorV2.

You can adjust the Prefill and Decode parallelism according to your workload and service requirements. The prefill and decode parallelism settings in --kv-transfer-config must match the actual engine configurations.

Before starting the services, set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 in both templates to enable Model Runner V2. Replace nic_name, local_ip,the model path with the appropriate values for your environment.

Both Prefill and Decode use the same node IP (`<node_ip>`). The Prefill DP group uses RPC port `12321`, while the Decode DP group uses RPC port `12325`.

Before you start, please:

1. Prepare one shared `launch_online_dp.py` launcher for Prefill and Decode. `import argparse import multiprocessing import os import subprocess import sys parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--script", required=True, help="Prefill or Decode startup script.") parser.add_argument("--dp-size", type=int, required=True) parser.add_argument("--tp-size", type=int, default=1) parser.add_argument("--pcp-size", type=int, default=1) parser.add_argument("--dp-size-local", type=int, default=-1) parser.add_argument("--dp-rank-start", type=int, default=0) parser.add_argument("--dp-address", required=True) parser.add_argument("--dp-rpc-port", default="12345") parser.add_argument("--vllm-start-port", type=int, default=9000) args = parser.parse_args() if args.dp_size_local == -1: args.dp_size_local = args.dp_size def run_command(visible_devices, dp_rank, port): script_args = [ visible_devices, str(port), str(args.dp_size), str(dp_rank), args.dp_address, args.dp_rpc_port, str(args.tp_size), str(args.pcp_size), ] if args.dp_size == 1: with open(args.script, encoding="utf-8") as f: script = f.read() script = "\n".join( line for line in script.splitlines() if "--data-parallel-rank" not in line and "--data-parallel-external-lb" not in line ) command = ["bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c", script, args.script, *script_args] else: command = ["bash", "-o", "pipefail", args.script, *script_args] subprocess.run(command, check=True) if __name__ == "__main__": if not os.path.isfile(args.script): sys.exit(f"Cannot find {args.script}") processes = [] devices_per_rank = args.tp_size * args.pcp_size for i in range(args.dp_size_local): visible_devices = ",".join( str(x) for x in range(i * devices_per_rank, (i + 1) * devices_per_rank) ) process = multiprocessing.Process( target=run_command, args=( visible_devices, args.dp_rank_start + i, args.vllm_start_port + i, ), ) processes.append(process) process.start() for process in processes: process.join() sys.exit(1 if any(p.exitcode != 0 for p in processes) else 0) ` Select the startup script with `--script`. When `--dp-size` is `1`, the launcher filters DP rank and external/hybrid load-balancing flags before running the script. It also propagates pipeline failures through `pipefail`. Parameter descriptions: Parameter Type Required Default Description `--script` str Yes — Path to the Prefill or Decode startup script. `--dp-size` int Yes — Total number of DP ranks across all nodes. `--tp-size` int No `1` Tensor parallel size for each DP rank. `--pcp-size` int No `1` Prefill context parallel size. Each local DP rank is assigned `--tp-size` × `--pcp-size` devices. `--dp-size-local` int No `--dp-size` Number of DP ranks launched on the current node. `--dp-rank-start` int No `0` Starting DP rank for the current node. `--dp-address` str Yes — IP address of the DP master node. `--dp-rpc-port` str No `12345` RPC port for DP coordination. `--vllm-start-port` int No `9000` Starting API port for local vLLM instances. Each subsequent instance uses the next port.
2. Prepare the P/D startup scripts. Save the following templates as `run_prefill.sh` and `run_decode.sh` in the same directory as `launch_online_dp.py`. If you use different filenames or directories, pass their paths through `--script` no launcher changes are required. With --pcp-size 4, the launcher passes 0,1,2,3 for this Prefill instance. export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1" export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.3"}' vllm serve /root/.cache/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host "$local_ip" \ --port "$2" \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --data-parallel-size "$3" \ --data-parallel-rank "$4" \ --data-parallel-address "$5" \ --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \ --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \ --prefill-context-parallel-size "$8" \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --seed 1024 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}' \ --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","enforce_eager":true}' \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 32 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --enforce-eager \ --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_fused_mc2":0, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "enable_shared_expert_dp":true}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_port": "30000", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "prefill": { "dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1 }, "decode": { "dp_size": 4, "tp_size": 1 } } }' \ 2>&1 | tee v4_flash_p.log ` Decode script: `run_decode.sh` `nic_name="xxxx" # change to your own nic name local_ip=xx.xx.xx.1 # change to your own ip export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000 export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=204 export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 export OMP_PROC_BIND=false export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024 export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1 # 3. Start the services. Open separate terminals in the same container and run the commands from the directory containing `launch_online_dp.py` and the startup scripts. Start Prefill and Decode in separate terminals. The startup sequence is Prefill and Decode → Proxy. Both roles use the same node IP but different DP RPC ports. Decode (NPUs 4–7) `# Change the IP address to your own. python ./launch_online_dp.py --script ./run_decode.sh --dp-size 4 --tp-size 1 --pcp-size 1 --dp-size-local 4 --dp-rank-start 0 --dp-address xx.xx.xx.1 --dp-rpc-port 12325 --vllm-start-port 7200 ` Prefill (NPUs 0–3) `# Change the IP address to your own. python ./launch_online_dp.py --script ./run_prefill.sh --dp-size 1 --tp-size 1 --pcp-size 4 --dp-size-local 1 --dp-rank-start 0 --dp-address xx.xx.xx.1 --dp-rpc-port 12321 --vllm-start-port 7100 `
4. Deploy the P-D disaggregation proxy. Wait until the Prefill API endpoint and all four Decode API endpoints are healthy, then deploy the P-D disaggregation proxy as described in [Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

Key Parameter Descriptions:

- `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` keeps the hybrid KV cache manager enabled. DeepSeek-V4 KV Pool deployments require this flag otherwise, the service may OOM during startup.
- `--enforce-eager` forces eager execution on Prefill nodes instead of graph compilation.
- `--async-scheduling` enables asynchronous scheduling to overlap CPU scheduling work with model execution.
- `--trust-remote-code` allows the model repository's custom code to be loaded. Only use trusted model repositories.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`: Keep this environment variable exported in both the Prefill and Decode pooling scripts. PCP requires Model Runner V2, which does not support DSA-CP. Therefore, do not set `enable_dsa_cp` in `--additional-config`.
- `--prefill-context-parallel-size` configures prefill context parallelism (PCP) on Model Runner V2 (MRv2), replacing the DSA-CP configuration used on MRv1. Besides speeding up long-context prefill, enabling PCP also shards the `o_proj` weights across the PCP group, providing partial tensor parallelism even when `--tensor-parallel-size` is `1` and relieving memory pressure.
- `--kv-transfer-config` configures KV cache transfer between the Prefill producer and Decode consumer in PD separation.
- `MooncakeConnectorV2` transfers KV cache from Prefill to Decode in PD separation. Configure Prefill with `kv_role: kv_producer` and Decode with `kv_role: kv_consumer`, allowing Decode to reuse the KV cache computed by Prefill for subsequent token generation.
- `kv_connector_extra_config.prefill.dp_size/tp_size` and `decode.dp_size/tp_size` must match the actual global DP and TP layout on the Prefill and Decode sides, respectively.
- `scheduler_config.recompute_scheduler_enable: true` enables the recomputation scheduler. When the Decode node has insufficient KV cache space, requests are sent to Prefill for KV cache recomputation. Enable it only on PD Decode nodes the legacy top-level key is deprecated.
- `--speculative-config`: Prefill and Decode must use the same DSpark `num_speculative_tokens` value. Use the value declared by the checkpoint this example uses `5`. The nested `enforce_eager` applies to DSpark draft execution, while the top-level `--enforce-eager` keeps the Prefill target model in eager mode.
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and `--attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8` use FP8 KV cache. The P and D sides must use the same KV data types so that the transferred KV cache is directly reusable.
- `enable_fused_mc2: 0` disables the Fused MC2 fusion operator on Prefill `multistream_overlap_shared_expert: true` overlaps shared-expert computation with MoE communication instead,`enable_shared_expert_dp: true` places shared experts on DP ranks.
- `ascend_compilation_config.enable_npugraph_ex: true` enables the extended NPU graph mode on Decode for graph compilation, while Prefill runs in eager mode. `enable_static_kernel: false` uses dynamic-shape kernels instead of static-shape kernels for ACL Graph execution.
- `combine_quant_mode: 4` forces the MoE MC2 combine stage on Decode nodes to use FP8 (MXFP float8_e4m3) communication quantization.

### KV Cache Pool Deployment

This section provides PD separation deployment examples with a KV Cache Pool for cross-engine KV cache reuse. The 950DT and MemCache. Each hardware tab describes backend and storage configuration, Prefill and Decode startup steps,KV cache reuse verification.

#### 950DT Single-Node PD Separation Deployment with Memcache KV Cache Pool[](#54-950dt-single-node-pd-separation-deployment)

This section extends [the 950DT PD deployment example](#524-950dt-series-pd-separation-deployment) with a Memcache-backed KV Cache Pool on a single 950DT products node. Prefill uses NPUs `0,1,2,3`, while Decode uses NPUs `4,5,6,7`. The existing external DP load balancing, API ports, DP RPC ports,proxy configuration remain unchanged.

Reuse the shared `launch_online_dp.py` from [the 950DT PD deployment example](#524-950dt-series-pd-separation-deployment). Save the pooled templates below as `run_prefill_memcache.sh` and `run_decode_memcache.sh`,select them with `--script`. These templates use `MultiConnector` and the required Memcache environment variables.

For backend configuration and parameter descriptions, refer to [KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store)](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend).

1. **Prerequisites and MemCache Configuration** Configure the Memcache environment and configuration files inside the container where both Prefill and Decode run. Then, open separate terminals in the same container to launch Prefill on NPUs 0–3 and Decode on NPUs 4–7. Replace the paths below with the actual values in your environment. `INSTALL_PATH` is the `Location` reported by `pip show memcache_hybrid`. Set `MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH` to the absolute path of `mmc-local.conf`. Export the environment variables so they are inherited by the launcher and its child processes. Run these exports in each Prefill and Decode terminal before starting the corresponding launcher. `# Set these variables to the actual paths in your environment. export MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR="/absolute/path/to/memcache-config" export INSTALL_PATH="<Location from pip show memcache_hybrid>" export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="${MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR}/mmc-local.conf" export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 ` Configure one `mmc-meta.conf` for the MetaService: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<metaservice_ip>:5000 ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<metaservice_ip>:6000 ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<metaservice_ip>:8000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ` Configure `mmc-local.conf` for both roles on this node: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<metaservice_ip>:5000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<metaservice_ip>:6000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_urma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 40GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 2048GB ` Use `device_urma` for 950DT products Device UB. For UBOE, replace it with `device_uboe`. Both roles must connect to the same MetaService and ConfigStore. `world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices supported by the pool it is not the number of NPUs used by this example. This example uses the embedded LocalService mode. Each vLLM process initializes a LocalService by loading `mmc-local.conf` from `MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH`. Therefore, `ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size` must be greater than `0GB`. Do not start a separate standalone LocalService when using this configuration. In this example, the Prefill instance uses PCP4 together with `AscendStoreConnector` in layerwise mode. This example sets `use_layerwise` to `true` and `layerwise_prefetch_layers` to `3`.
2. **Prepare the Prefill Startup Script** Save the following template as `run_prefill_memcache.sh` in the same directory as the shared `launch_online_dp.py`. `#!/usr/bin/env bash source /root/.bashrc nic_name="xxxx" # change to your own nic name local_ip=xx.xx.xx.1 # change to your own ip : "${MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR:?Set MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR before starting the launcher}" export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="${MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR}/mmc-local.conf" export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000 export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=204 export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 export OMP_PROC_BIND=false export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024 export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=CCU_SCHED export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1 # With --pcp-size 4, the launcher passes 0,1,2,3 for this Prefill instance. export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1" export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.3"}' vllm serve /root/.cache/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host "$local_ip" \ --port "$2" \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --data-parallel-size "$3" \ --data-parallel-rank "$4" \ --data-parallel-address "$5" \ --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \ --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \ --prefill-context-parallel-size "$8" \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --seed 1024 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}' \ --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","enforce_eager":true}' \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 32 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --enforce-eager \ --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_fused_mc2":0, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "enable_shared_expert_dp":true}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_port": "30000", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "prefill": { "dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1 }, "decode": { "dp_size": 4, "tp_size": 1 } } }, { "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "backend": "memcache", "use_layerwise": true, "layerwise_prefetch_layers": 3 } } ] } }' \ 2>&1 | tee v4_flash_p_memcache.log `
3. **Prepare the Decode Startup Script** Save the following template as `run_decode_memcache.sh` in the same directory as the shared `launch_online_dp.py`. It accepts the same eight arguments, maps device indices to NPUs `4`–`7`,writes a separate log for each DP rank. `#!/usr/bin/env bash source /root/.bashrc nic_name="xxxx" # change to your own nic name local_ip=xx.xx.xx.1 # change to your own ip : "${MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR:?Set MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR before starting the launcher}" export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="${MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR}/mmc-local.conf" export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3000 export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=204 export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 export OMP_PROC_BIND=false export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024 export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1 # The Decode group uses NPUs 4-7 each DP rank sees one of those NPUs. export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$(( $1 + 4 ))" export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.3"}' vllm serve /root/.cache/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --host "$local_ip" \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --port "$2" \ --data-parallel-size "$3" \ --data-parallel-rank "$4" \ --data-parallel-address "$5" \ --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \ --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \ --prefill-context-parallel-size "$8" \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --seed 1024 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \ --max-num-seqs 56 \ --async-scheduling \ --block-size 32 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":128}' \ --trust-remote-code \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark","enforce_eager":false}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_port": "30100", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "prefill": { "dp_size": 1, "tp_size": 1 }, "decode": { "dp_size": 4, "tp_size": 1 } } }, { "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "backend": "memcache" } } ] } }' \ --additional-config '{ "ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": true,"enable_static_kernel": false}, "enable_cpu_binding": true,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true,"recompute_scheduler_enable": true,"enable_shared_expert_dp": true,"combine_quant_mode": 4 }' \ 2>&1 | tee "v4_flash_d_memcache_dp${4}.log" `
4. **Startup and Verification** Start one MetaService on the node containing `mmc-meta.conf`: `export MMC_META_CONFIG_PATH="<directory containing mmc-meta.conf>/mmc-meta.conf" python -c "from memcache_hybrid import MetaService MetaService.main()" ` After the MetaService is ready, start Prefill and Decode in separate terminals in the same container. The startup sequence is MetaService → Prefill and Decode → Proxy. Start Prefill and Decode in separate terminals in the same container. Run both commands from the directory containing the shared launcher and the pooled scripts. Replace `MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR` with the directory prepared above. Both roles use the same node IP but different DP RPC ports. Decode (NPUs 4–7) `# Change the IP address to your own. python ./launch_online_dp.py --script ./run_decode_memcache.sh --dp-size 4 --tp-size 1 --pcp-size 1 --dp-size-local 4 --dp-rank-start 0 --dp-address xx.xx.xx.1 --dp-rpc-port 12325 --vllm-start-port 7200 ` Prefill (NPUs 0–3) `# Change the IP address to your own. python ./launch_online_dp.py --script ./run_prefill_memcache.sh --dp-size 1 --tp-size 1 --pcp-size 4 --dp-size-local 1 --dp-rank-start 0 --dp-address xx.xx.xx.1 --dp-rpc-port 12321 --vllm-start-port 7100 ` Start the Proxy and Verify KV Cache Pool Reuse Wait until the Prefill API endpoint and all four Decode API endpoints are healthy, then start the proxy using the configuration from [the 950DT PD deployment example](#524-950dt-series-pd-separation-deployment). Send a generation request to `<proxy_ip>:1999` as described in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification). Confirm that the response contains generated text. To verify KV Cache Pool reuse, send an initial request to warm up the cache, then send another request with the same identical token prefix. Check the Prefill logs for KV Pool lookup/get/put operations and cache-hit information. An HTTP 200 response alone does not confirm KV Cache Pool reuse. For details,refer to [KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store)](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend).

Key pooling parameters:

- `AscendStoreConnector` integrates with the MemCache KV Cache Pool to support external KV cache storage and reuse. In this example, Prefill handles pool lookups, loading,storage, while Decode receives KV cache from Prefill.
- `backend: "memcache"` selects MemCache as the pool storage backend. On Prefill, `use_layerwise: true` enables layer-by-layer KV cache storage and loading, while `layerwise_prefetch_layers: 3` configures prefetching to load KV cache ahead of layer execution.

## Verification

This section verifies basic inference functionality for all deployment modes. For Memcache pooled PD deployments,verification steps](#534-startup-and-verification) or the “Start the Proxy and Verify KV Cache Pool Reuse” step in the [950DT example](#54-950dt-single-node-pd-separation-deployment).

Once your server is started, you can query the model with input prompts:

3, use the proxy's IP address and port, since requests are routed through the proxy to the Prefill and Decode instances.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:<port>/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "dsv4",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 256,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected Result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON response containing the `choices` field.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8) node | ModelScope |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 |  | Hugging Face |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8 |  | Quantize locally with msmodelslim |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select an image based on your machine type and start the docker image on your node, refer to [using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Start the docker image on each node.

```bash

export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main

docker run --rm \
    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=512g \
    --net=host \
    --privileged=true \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

After a successful docker run, you can verify the running container service by executing the `docker ps` command.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8).

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

# during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8) node | ModelScope |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 |  | Hugging Face |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8 |  | Quantize locally with msmodelslim |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select an image based on your machine type and start the docker image on your node, refer to [using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Start the docker image on each node.

```bash

export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main

docker run --rm \
    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=512g \
    --net=host \
    --privileged=true \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

After a successful docker run, you can verify the running container service by executing the `docker ps` command.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8).

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

# during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 800000 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 128 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "enforce_eager": true}'  \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "dsv4",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 256,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected Result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON response containing the `choices` field.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8)

#### A2 Series PD Separation Deployment with DSpark (2P2D, 32 cards)[](#525-a2-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark-2p2d-32-cards)

Use `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on four Atlas 800I A2 servers (8 NPUs per server). Choose the workload settings from the table before starting either role. The settings below retain the configurations selected in completed A2 measurements they are starting points for the listed workloads, not a universal optimum across workloads or software versions.

| Role | Nodes / NPUs | Parallelism | HTTP endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 / 16 | ExternalDP2 × TP1 × PP1 × PCP8 | node A:7100, node B:7101 |
| Decode | 2 / 16 | DP16 × TP1, eight processes per node | 7100–7107 on each node |

Measurement and version scope

The measured setup used the A2 `dev-26.2.0.day20261021` image, MRv2, P eager and D target/draft graph mode. It also included runtime changes for UVA dirty tracking, exact request-hash reuse and RoPE capacity those changes are not delivered by this documentation update. Pin the image, model and loaded code when reproducing measurements.

Topology and dispatch limits

Keep `PP1 × PCP8` with `MooncakeHybridConnector`. The validated implementation rejects simultaneous PP>1 and PCP>1. Its A2 dispatch path also requires `D max-num-seqs × (1 + draft tokens) <= 256`: the measured pairs are 5/42, 2/85 and 1/128. A different draft length changes the legal request capacity 42 is not a universal maximum.

**Choose the server settings and client load.** D uses `--max-num-batched-tokens 720` and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97` in every configuration. P uses `--max-num-seqs 16`, `--api-server-count 4`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.96` and draft5/eager.

For other workloads, replace the explicit values listed in the table for `cold-pd`, replace the P cache switch with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. No external helper or profile file is required.

The measured context budgets are intentionally asymmetric: `--max-model-len 150000` on P and `508576` on D. The larger D budget does not extend the prompt length that P can prefill. All ordinary-length workloads listed here fit within the P budget do not advertise the D value as the end-to-end prompt limit. If a deployment requires equal P/D limits, change both to the chosen service limit and revalidate KV capacity and throughput before reusing these measurements.

Server configuration and client load must be recorded together. For the 16K/1K total-window latency trial, N8192/CC2048/rate0 was tested twice against a current-deployment N8192/CC2304/rate0 control. The last repeat reduced legacy TTFT mean/P90 from 21.30/50.32 seconds to 11.32/42.51 seconds while output throughput changed by -0.54%. TPOT was 93.6 ms, not a 20 ms SLO pass. This is a workload-specific result lower concurrency does not guarantee lower latency elsewhere. Do not substitute total results for native stable results. The 1M cases require a separately validated long-context deployment, not a larger `--max-model-len` in these scripts.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

If you don't want to use the docker image as above, you can also build all from source:

Install `vllm-ascend` from source, refer to [installation](../../getting_started/installation.html).

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to set up the environment on each node.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8).

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

# during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 800000 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 128 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "enforce_eager": true}'  \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

        "temperature": 0

```

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8)

#### A2 Series PD Separation Deployment with DSpark (2P2D, 32 cards)[](#525-a2-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark-2p2d-32-cards)

Use `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on four Atlas 800I A2 servers (8 NPUs per server). Choose the workload settings from the table before starting either role. The settings below retain the configurations selected in completed A2 measurements they are starting points for the listed workloads, not a universal optimum across workloads or software versions.

| Role | Nodes / NPUs | Parallelism | HTTP endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 / 16 | ExternalDP2 × TP1 × PP1 × PCP8 | node A:7100, node B:7101 |
| Decode | 2 / 16 | DP16 × TP1, eight processes per node | 7100–7107 on each node |

Measurement and version scope

The measured setup used the A2 `dev-26.2.0.day20261021` image, MRv2, P eager and D target/draft graph mode. It also included runtime changes for UVA dirty tracking, exact request-hash reuse and RoPE capacity those changes are not delivered by this documentation update. Pin the image, model and loaded code when reproducing measurements.

Topology and dispatch limits

Keep `PP1 × PCP8` with `MooncakeHybridConnector`. The validated implementation rejects simultaneous PP>1 and PCP>1. Its A2 dispatch path also requires `D max-num-seqs × (1 + draft tokens) <= 256`: the measured pairs are 5/42, 2/85 and 1/128. A different draft length changes the legal request capacity 42 is not a universal maximum.

**Choose the server settings and client load.** D uses `--max-num-batched-tokens 720` and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97` in every configuration. P uses `--max-num-seqs 16`, `--api-server-count 4`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.96` and draft5/eager.

| Configuration | Workload / native window | P token budget / prefix cache | D draft / max-num-seqs | Proxy workers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode-4k-total | 4K input / 2K output, pure D, total | 4096 / on | 2 / 85 | 4 |
| decode-4k-stable | 4K / 2K, pure D, native stable | 4096 / on | 4 / 51 | 4 |
| decode-16k | 16K / 1K, pure D | 4096 / on | 4 / 51 | 4 |
| decode-long | 64K / 1K or 128K / 1K, pure D | 4096 / on | 5 / 42 | 1 |
| cold-pd | PC0 pure P or full PD | 8192 / off | 1 / 128 | 4 |
| pc90 | Distinct-suffix, multiple-prefix pooling; see A2 KV Pooling | 8192 / on | 1 / 128 | 4 |

The recorded client loads below are separate from the server profiles. Input counts include the measured client's 84-token template offset for these ordinary-length cases. Keep the payload definition and tokenizer unchanged when comparing them.

| Profile / window | Measured input / output tokens | Requests / concurrency / rate (req/s) |
|---|---|---|
| decode-4k-total / total | 4180 / 2048 | 4096 / 1536 / 0 |
| decode-4k-stable / native stable | 4180 / 2048 | 8192 / 2304 / 0; stable subset chosen by AISBench |
| decode-16k / total, TTFT trial | 16468 / 1024 | 8192 / 2048 / 0 |
| decode-16k / recorded native stable | 16468 / 1024 | 8192 / 2304 / 0; do not substitute the CC2048 total result |
| decode-long / 64K total or native stable | 65620 / 1024 | 3840 / 576 / 0 |
| decode-long / 128K total | 131156 / 1024 | 3920 / 960 / 0 |
| decode-long / 128K native stable | 131156 / 1024 | 2960 / 960 / 0 |
| cold-pd / full PD total | 16468 / 1024 | 240 / 60 / 0 |

The complete scripts below use the measured 16K pure-D setting: P token budget4096/APC on, D draft4/mns51/GMU0.97. For other workloads, replace the explicit values listed in the table for `cold-pd`, replace the P cache switch with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. No external helper or profile file is required.

The measured context budgets are intentionally asymmetric: `--max-model-len 150000` on P and `508576` on D. The larger D budget does not extend the prompt length that P can prefill. All ordinary-length workloads listed here fit within the P budget do not advertise the D value as the end-to-end prompt limit. If a deployment requires equal P/D limits, change both to the chosen service limit and revalidate KV capacity and throughput before reusing these measurements.

Server configuration and client load must be recorded together. For the 16K/1K total-window latency trial, N8192/CC2048/rate0 was tested twice against a current-deployment N8192/CC2304/rate0 control. The last repeat reduced legacy TTFT mean/P90 from 21.30/50.32 seconds to 11.32/42.51 seconds while output throughput changed by -0.54%. TPOT was 93.6 ms, not a 20 ms SLO pass. This is a workload-specific result lower concurrency does not guarantee lower latency elsewhere. Do not substitute total results for native stable results. The 1M cases require a separately validated long-context deployment, not a larger `--max-model-len` in these scripts.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8) node | ModelScope |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 |  | Hugging Face |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8 |  | Quantize locally with msmodelslim |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

If you don't want to use the docker image as above, you can also build all from source:

Install `vllm-ascend` from source, refer to [installation](../../getting_started/installation.html).

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to set up the environment on each node.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8).

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

# during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 800000 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 128 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "enforce_eager": true}'  \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8) node | ModelScope |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 |  | Hugging Face |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8 |  | Quantize locally with msmodelslim |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select an image based on your machine type and start the docker image on your node, refer to [using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Start the docker image on each node.

```bash

export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main

docker run --rm \
    --name vllm-ascend \
    --shm-size=512g \
    --net=host \
    --privileged=true \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

After a successful docker run, you can verify the running container service by executing the `docker ps` command.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and 1 Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8).

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

# during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 800000 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 128 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "enforce_eager": true}'  \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "dsv4",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 256,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected Result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON response containing the `choices` field.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

Atlas 800I A2 (64GB × 8)

#### A2 Series PD Separation Deployment with DSpark (2P2D, 32 cards)[](#525-a2-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark-2p2d-32-cards)

Use `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on four Atlas 800I A2 servers (8 NPUs per server). Choose the workload settings from the table before starting either role. The settings below retain the configurations selected in completed A2 measurements they are starting points for the listed workloads, not a universal optimum across workloads or software versions.

| Role | Nodes / NPUs | Parallelism | HTTP endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 / 16 | ExternalDP2 × TP1 × PP1 × PCP8 | node A:7100, node B:7101 |
| Decode | 2 / 16 | DP16 × TP1, eight processes per node | 7100–7107 on each node |

Measurement and version scope

The measured setup used the A2 `dev-26.2.0.day20261021` image, MRv2, P eager and D target/draft graph mode. It also included runtime changes for UVA dirty tracking, exact request-hash reuse and RoPE capacity those changes are not delivered by this documentation update. Pin the image, model and loaded code when reproducing measurements.

Topology and dispatch limits

Keep `PP1 × PCP8` with `MooncakeHybridConnector`. The validated implementation rejects simultaneous PP>1 and PCP>1. Its A2 dispatch path also requires `D max-num-seqs × (1 + draft tokens) <= 256`: the measured pairs are 5/42, 2/85 and 1/128. A different draft length changes the legal request capacity 42 is not a universal maximum.

**Choose the server settings and client load.** D uses `--max-num-batched-tokens 720` and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97` in every configuration. P uses `--max-num-seqs 16`, `--api-server-count 4`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.96` and draft5/eager.

| Configuration | Workload / native window | P token budget / prefix cache | D draft / max-num-seqs | Proxy workers |

| decode-4k-total | 4K input / 2K output, pure D, total | 4096 / on | 2 / 85 | 4 |
| decode-4k-stable | 4K / 2K, pure D, native stable | 4096 / on | 4 / 51 | 4 |
