### KV Cache Pool Deployment

A3 examples use the MemCache backend,MemCache. Each hardware tab describes backend and storage configuration, Prefill and Decode startup steps,KV cache reuse verification.

#### A3 1P1D Deployment with Memcache KV Cache Pool[](#53-a3-1p1d-deployment-with-memcache-kv-cache-pool)

This example deploys the DSpark checkpoint `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on two A3 servers (16 NPU dies per server), using a Memcache KV Cache Pool:

| Role | DP | TP | PCP | NPU dies | HTTP ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 | 1 | 8 | 16 | 7100-7101 |
| Decode | 16 | 1 | 1 | 16 | 7100-7115 |

The deployment follows the same Memcache service setup as [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. `MooncakeHybridConnector` continues to transfer KV cache from Prefill to Decode, while `AscendStoreConnector` stores reusable KV cache in Memcache. Both connectors are configured as children of `MultiConnector`.

Before starting vLLM, follow the [Memcache backend guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend) to check the HDK/CANN and A3 memory prerequisites, install `memfabric-hybrid` and `memcache-hybrid`, configure `mmc-meta.conf`, `mmc-local.conf`,`mmc-local-standalone.conf`,prepare the services below. The Prefill and Decode nodes must use the same MetaService endpoint. Keep the `/etc/hccn.

This example uses separated Memcache deployment so that the pool reserves host memory before vLLM loads the model. Prepare one MetaService configuration and two LocalService configurations as described below.

1. **Prepare the Memcache Services** Create `mmc-meta.conf` on the node that runs MetaService: `ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<META_SERVICE_IP>:18000 ` Create `mmc-local.conf` on both Prefill and Decode nodes for the LocalService embedded in vLLM: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 0GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` Create `mmc-local-standalone.conf` on both nodes for the standalone Memcache process. It uses the same endpoints, world size,protocol, but contributes the host DRAM used by the pool: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` `world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices that can join the pool, not the DP size. Changing it after LocalServices connect requires restarting MetaService. `device_sdma` is recommended for A3 HCCS and requires LingQu Computing Network 1.5 or later. The `20GB` standalone DRAM value is an example set it according to the host memory available after reserving capacity for the operating system and vLLM. `max.dram.size` must be at least the largest `dram.size` contributed by any LocalService. Start MetaService with `mmc-meta.conf`: `export MMC_META_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-meta.conf" python3 -c 'from memcache_hybrid import MetaService MetaService.main()' ` Save the following script as `memcache_standalone.py` on both Prefill and Decode nodes: `import time from memcache_hybrid import DistributedObjectStore store = DistributedObjectStore() result = store.init(0) if result != 0: raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to initialize Memcache: {result}") print("Successfully initialized Memcache") while True: time.sleep(1) ` After MetaService is ready, start the standalone Memcache process on both Prefill and Decode nodes and wait for successful initialization: `export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-local-standalone.conf" python3 memcache_standalone.py ` For additional parameters and capacity constraints, refer to [Memcache and vLLM separated deployment](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#Memcache-and-vLLM-Separated-Deployment). Reuse `launch_online_dp.py` from [the A3 PD deployment example](#a3-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark). Set `MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH` to the `Location` reported by `pip show memcache_hybrid`,set `MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR` to the absolute directory containing the configuration files above on both nodes. Use the same checkpoint on both nodes. Keep `/etc/hccn. The MetaService, config store, DP RPC, KV transfer,HTTP ports must be reachable between the nodes. The configuration above uses a DRAM-only pool. To enable SSD in this A3 separated deployment, keep `storage.enabled=false` in the LocalService configuration embedded in vLLM and use the following alternative `mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf` for the standalone process on each node: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = true ubsio.disk.path = <DEDICATED_SSD_BLOCK_DEVICE> ubsio.mem.size_in_gb = 50 ubsio.standalone.device_count = 1 ubsio.standalone.force_new_disk = true ` Use a dedicated, unmounted block device without a filesystem signature. `force_new_disk=true` reinitializes the SSD cache layout at startup and invalidates previous cache contents do not point it at a device containing data to keep. The 20 GiB DRAM contribution and 50 GiB UBS IO allocation are separate per-process host-memory budgets. Size both for the actual prefix working set and available host memory. With one standalone process per host, use `device_count=1` it is not the number of model ranks. After MetaService is ready, start one standalone process on each node with the selected SSD configuration, then all Decode ranks, both Prefill ranks and the proxy: `export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf" python3 memcache_standalone.py ` Wait for `Successfully initialized Memcache` before starting vLLM. vLLM processes continue to use `mmc-local.conf`, not the standalone configuration. Follow [Enable Memcache SSD Cache](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#step-7-enable-memcache-ssd-cache) for SDK requirements, storage ownership and capacity constraints. Verify real cache restore and backend hit activity enabling an SSD flag or seeing HTTP 200 alone does not prove three-level cache reuse.
2. **Start the Prefill Node with Pooling** On the Prefill node, save the following script as `run_dp_template.sh` beside `launch_online_dp.py` from [the A3 PD deployment example](#a3-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark). Replace the network, model,Memcache path placeholders for this node. `#!/usr/bin/env bash set -e unset https_proxy http_proxy nic_name="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>" local_ip="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT=3600000 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30000 export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=204 export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 export OMP_PROC_BIND=false export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1800 export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV" export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$1 export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 # Parameters required by the Memcache KV Cache Pool. MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH="<MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH>" MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>" export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="$MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR/mmc-local.conf" export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH/memcache_hybrid/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}:/usr/local/lib/" # Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download vllm serve "<MODEL_PATH>/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8" \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port $2 \ --data-parallel-size $3 \ --data-parallel-rank $4 \ --data-parallel-address $5 \ --data-parallel-rpc-port $6 \ --tensor-parallel-size $7 \ --prefill-context-parallel-size $8 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --seed 1024 \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \ --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 5,"method": "dspark","enforce_eager": true}' \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 32 \ --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \ --quantization ascend \ --enforce-eager \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 1}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_port": "30000", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "MooncakeHybridConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_port": "30000", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "prefill": { "dp_size": 2, "tp_size": 1, "pcp_size": 8 }, "decode": { "dp_size": 16, "tp_size": 1 } } }, { "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "lookup_rpc_port": "0", "backend": "memcache", "use_layerwise": false } } ] } }' `
3. **Start the Decode Node with Pooling** On the Decode node, save the following script as `run_dp_template.sh` beside `launch_online_dp.py` from [the A3 PD deployment example](#a3-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark). Replace the network, model,Memcache path placeholders for this node. `#!/usr/bin/env bash set -e unset https_proxy http_proxy nic_name="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>" local_ip="<DECODE_NODE_IP>" export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV" export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1 export VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT=3600000 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30000 export HCCL_EXEC_TIMEOUT=204 export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=120 export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name export OMP_PROC_BIND=false export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2400 export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$1 export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 # Parameters required by the Memcache KV Cache Pool. MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH="<MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH>" MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>" export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="$MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR/mmc-local.conf" export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH/memcache_hybrid/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}:/usr/local/lib/" # Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download vllm serve "<MODEL_PATH>/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8" \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port $2 \ --data-parallel-size $3 \ --data-parallel-rank $4 \ --data-parallel-address $5 \ --data-parallel-rpc-port $6 \ --tensor-parallel-size $7 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --seed 1024 \ --served-model-name dsv4 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 480 \ --max-num-seqs 60 \ --async-scheduling \ --block-size 32 \ --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --trust-remote-code \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --quantization ascend \ --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 5,"method": "dspark"}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{ "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_port": "30100", "kv_load_failure_policy": "fail", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "MooncakeHybridConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_port": "30100", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "prefill": { "dp_size": 2, "tp_size": 1, "pcp_size": 8 }, "decode": { "dp_size": 16, "tp_size": 1 } } }, { "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "lookup_rpc_port": "0", "backend": "memcache", "use_layerwise": false } } ] } }' \ --additional-config '{ "ascend_compilation_config":{ "enable_npugraph_ex":true, "enable_static_kernel":false }, "enable_cpu_binding":true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true, "recompute_scheduler_enable":true }' `
4. **Startup and Verification** Start MetaService first, then the standalone Memcache process on each node. Wait for both standalone processes to report successful initialization. Keep all three processes running while vLLM is serving requests. Start Decode on the Decode node in a separate terminal: `python launch_online_dp.py \ --dp-size 16 --tp-size 1 --dp-size-local 16 --dp-rank-start 0 \ --dp-address "<DECODE_NODE_IP>" --dp-rpc-port 12321 --vllm-start-port 7100 ` Wait until all Decode engines report `Application startup complete`, then start Prefill on the Prefill node: `python launch_online_dp.py \ --dp-size 2 --tp-size 1 --pcp-size 8 --dp-size-local 2 --dp-rank-start 0 \ --dp-address "<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" --dp-rpc-port 12321 --vllm-start-port 7100 ` Each Prefill DP rank uses eight consecutive NPU dies: 0-7 and 8-15. Each Decode DP rank uses one die. `--dp-address` is the master IP of its own role Prefill and Decode use separate DP groups. After every Prefill engine is ready, start the proxy from [Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) with both Prefill endpoints and all sixteen Decode endpoints: `PREFILL_IP="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" DECODE_IP="<DECODE_NODE_IP>" prefiller_hosts=() decoder_hosts=() for ((i=0 i<2 i++)) do prefiller_hosts+=("$PREFILL_IP") done for ((i=0 i<16 i++)) do decoder_hosts+=("$DECODE_IP") done python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \ --host "$PREFILL_IP" --port 1999 \ --prefiller-hosts "${prefiller_hosts[@]}" \ --prefiller-ports {7100..7101} \ --decoder-hosts "${decoder_hosts[@]}" \ --decoder-ports {7100..7115} ` Send requests to the proxy at `http://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:1999`, using the `dsv4` served model name from Section 6. Verify both the response and the P-to-D transfer in engine logs. To check pool reuse, send the same long prompt (at least 4096 tokens for this example) twice, allowing the first request's KV save to complete before sending the second. Confirm Memcache put activity on the first request and lookup/hit/get activity on a subsequent request in the Prefill logs. A request served entirely by a Prefill engine's local prefix cache may not load from Memcache verify reuse on an engine whose local prefix cache is cold. A successful response alone does not confirm a pool hit. Key pooling parameters: `MultiConnector` combines live P-to-D transfer through `MooncakeHybridConnector` with reusable prefix storage through `AscendStoreConnector`. In this example, both children and the parent use `kv_producer` on Prefill and `kv_consumer` on Decode. Decode does not put or load pool entries unless `consumer_is_to_put` or `consumer_is_to_load` is explicitly enabled. `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` must match across all engines. Prefill enables prefix caching Decode disables it. Keep `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` on both roles and the top-level `kv_load_failure_policy` as `fail` the `recompute` load-failure policy does not support DeepSeek-V4 hybrid attention. `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is required for PCP. Do not enable `enable_dsa_cp` with Model Runner V2. The two roles use the same DSpark checkpoint and five speculative tokens. Keep the connector's DP/TP/PCP sizes aligned with the launcher commands. `lookup_rpc_port` selects the local scheduler-worker IPC endpoint. The implementation adds the DP rank, so this example uses `"0"` for each DP rank. Use a different value for another deployment sharing the same IPC namespace. For capacity tuning, optional SSD configuration,troubleshooting, refer to [KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store)](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html).

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and Decode within the same node. The quantized DSpark model `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` can be deployed on 1 Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) or

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --data-parallel-size 4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 32 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{
        "ascend_compilation_config": {
            "enable_npugraph_ex": true,
            "enable_static_kernel": false
        },
        "enable_cpu_binding": true,
        "enable_dsa_cp": true,
        "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true
    }'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

The following sections describe multi-node PD separation deployment on Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) and

#### A3 Series PD Separation Deployment with DSpark[](#a3-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark)

This section shows the deployment guide of DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) multi-node environment with 1P1D for better performance.

Before you start, please:

1. Prepare the script `launch_online_dp.py` on each node. `import argparse import multiprocessing import os import subprocess import sys def parse_args(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument( "--dp-size", type=int, required=True, help="Data parallel size." ) parser.add_argument( "--tp-size", type=int, default=1, help="Tensor parallel size." ) parser.add_argument( ### KV Cache Pool Deployment

A3 examples use the MemCache backend,MemCache. Each hardware tab describes backend and storage configuration, Prefill and Decode startup steps,KV cache reuse verification.

#### A3 1P1D Deployment with Memcache KV Cache Pool[](#53-a3-1p1d-deployment-with-memcache-kv-cache-pool)

This example deploys the DSpark checkpoint `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on two A3 servers (16 NPU dies per server), using a Memcache KV Cache Pool:

| Role | DP | TP | PCP | NPU dies | HTTP ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 | 1 | 8 | 16 | 7100-7101 |
| Decode | 16 | 1 | 1 | 16 | 7100-7115 |

The deployment follows the same Memcache service setup as [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. `MooncakeHybridConnector` continues to transfer KV cache from Prefill to Decode, while `AscendStoreConnector` stores reusable KV cache in Memcache. Both connectors are configured as children of `MultiConnector`.

Before starting vLLM, follow the [Memcache backend guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend) to check the HDK/CANN and A3 memory prerequisites, install `memfabric-hybrid` and `memcache-hybrid`, configure `mmc-meta.conf`, `mmc-local.conf`,`mmc-local-standalone.conf`,prepare the services below. The Prefill and Decode nodes must use the same MetaService endpoint. Keep the `/etc/hccn.

This example uses separated Memcache deployment so that the pool reserves host memory before vLLM loads the model. Prepare one MetaService configuration and two LocalService configurations as described below.

1. **Prepare the Memcache Services** Create `mmc-meta.conf` on the node that runs MetaService: `ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<META_SERVICE_IP>:18000 ` Create `mmc-local.conf` on both Prefill and Decode nodes for the LocalService embedded in vLLM: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 0GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` Create `mmc-local-standalone.conf` on both nodes for the standalone Memcache process. It uses the same endpoints, world size,protocol, but contributes the host DRAM used by the pool: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` `world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices that can join the pool, not the DP size. Changing it after LocalServices connect requires restarting MetaService. `device_sdma` is recommended for A3 HCCS and requires LingQu Computing Network 1.5 or later. The `20GB` standalone DRAM value is an example set it according to the host memory available after reserving capacity for the operating system and vLLM. `max.dram.size` must be at least the largest `dram.size` contributed by any LocalService. Set `MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH` to the `Location` reported by `pip show memcache_hybrid`,set `MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR` to the absolute directory containing the configuration files above on both nodes. Use the same checkpoint on both nodes. Keep `/etc/hccn. The MetaService, config store, DP RPC, KV transfer,HTTP ports must be reachable between the nodes. The configuration above uses a DRAM-only pool. To enable SSD in this A3 separated deployment, keep `storage.enabled=false` in the LocalService configuration embedded in vLLM and use the following alternative `mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf` for the standalone process on each node: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = true ubsio.disk.path = <DEDICATED_SSD_BLOCK_DEVICE> ubsio.mem.size_in_gb = 50 ubsio.standalone.device_count = 1 ubsio.standalone.force_new_disk = true ` Use a dedicated, unmounted block device without a filesystem signature. `force_new_disk=true` reinitializes the SSD cache layout at startup and invalidates previous cache contents do not point it at a device containing data to keep. The 20 GiB DRAM contribution and 50 GiB UBS IO allocation are separate per-process host-memory budgets. Size both for the actual prefix working set and available host memory. With one standalone process per host, use `device_count=1` it is not the number of model ranks. After MetaService is ready, start one standalone process on each node with the selected SSD configuration, then all Decode ranks, both Prefill ranks and the proxy: `export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf" python3 memcache_standalone.py ` Wait for `Successfully initialized Memcache` before starting vLLM. vLLM processes continue to use `mmc-local.conf`, not the standalone configuration. Verify real cache restore and backend hit activity enabling an SSD flag or seeing HTTP 200 alone does not prove three-level cache reuse.

To check pool reuse, send the same long prompt (at least 4096 tokens for this example) twice, allowing the first request's KV save to complete before sending the second. Confirm Memcache put activity on the first request and lookup/hit/get activity on a subsequent request in the Prefill logs. A request served entirely by a Prefill engine's local prefix cache may not load from Memcache verify reuse on an engine whose local prefix cache is cold. A successful response alone does not confirm a pool hit. Key pooling parameters: `MultiConnector` combines live P-to-D transfer through `MooncakeHybridConnector` with reusable prefix storage through `AscendStoreConnector`. In this example, both children and the parent use `kv_producer` on Prefill and `kv_consumer` on Decode. Decode does not put or load pool entries unless `consumer_is_to_put` or `consumer_is_to_load` is explicitly enabled. `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` must match across all engines. Prefill enables prefix caching Decode disables it. Keep `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` on both roles and the top-level `kv_load_failure_policy` as `fail` the `recompute` load-failure policy does not support DeepSeek-V4 hybrid attention. `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is required for PCP. Do not enable `enable_dsa_cp` with Model Runner V2. The two roles use the same DSpark checkpoint and five speculative tokens. Keep the connector's DP/TP/PCP sizes aligned with the launcher commands. `lookup_rpc_port` selects the local scheduler-worker IPC endpoint. The implementation adds the DP rank, so this example uses `"0"` for each DP rank. Use a different value for another deployment sharing the same IPC namespace. For capacity tuning, optional SSD configuration,troubleshooting, refer to [KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store)](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html).

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and Decode within the same node. The quantized DSpark model `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` can be deployed on 1 Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) or

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --data-parallel-size 4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 32 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{
        "ascend_compilation_config": {
            "enable_npugraph_ex": true,
            "enable_static_kernel": false
        },
        "enable_cpu_binding": true,
        "enable_dsa_cp": true,
        "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true
    }'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

```shell
curl http://<node0_ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions \

```

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

The following sections describe multi-node PD separation deployment on Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) and

### KV Cache Pool Deployment

A3 examples use the MemCache backend,MemCache. Each hardware tab describes backend and storage configuration, Prefill and Decode startup steps,KV cache reuse verification.

#### A3 1P1D Deployment with Memcache KV Cache Pool[](#53-a3-1p1d-deployment-with-memcache-kv-cache-pool)

This example deploys the DSpark checkpoint `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on two A3 servers (16 NPU dies per server), using a Memcache KV Cache Pool:

| Role | DP | TP | PCP | NPU dies | HTTP ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 | 1 | 8 | 16 | 7100-7101 |
| Decode | 16 | 1 | 1 | 16 | 7100-7115 |

The deployment follows the same Memcache service setup as [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. `MooncakeHybridConnector` continues to transfer KV cache from Prefill to Decode, while `AscendStoreConnector` stores reusable KV cache in Memcache. Both connectors are configured as children of `MultiConnector`.

Before starting vLLM, follow the [Memcache backend guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend) to check the HDK/CANN and A3 memory prerequisites, install `memfabric-hybrid` and `memcache-hybrid`, configure `mmc-meta.conf`, `mmc-local.conf`,`mmc-local-standalone.conf`,prepare the services below. The Prefill and Decode nodes must use the same MetaService endpoint. Keep the `/etc/hccn.

This example uses separated Memcache deployment so that the pool reserves host memory before vLLM loads the model. Prepare one MetaService configuration and two LocalService configurations as described below.

1. **Prepare the Memcache Services** Create `mmc-meta.conf` on the node that runs MetaService: `ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<META_SERVICE_IP>:18000 ` Create `mmc-local.conf` on both Prefill and Decode nodes for the LocalService embedded in vLLM: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 0GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` Create `mmc-local-standalone.conf` on both nodes for the standalone Memcache process. It uses the same endpoints, world size,protocol, but contributes the host DRAM used by the pool: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` `world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices that can join the pool, not the DP size. Changing it after LocalServices connect requires restarting MetaService. `device_sdma` is recommended for A3 HCCS and requires LingQu Computing Network 1.5 or later. The `20GB` standalone DRAM value is an example set it according to the host memory available after reserving capacity for the operating system and vLLM. `max.dram.size` must be at least the largest `dram.size` contributed by any LocalService. Start MetaService with `mmc-meta.conf`: `export MMC_META_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-meta.conf" python3 -c 'from memcache_hybrid import MetaService MetaService.main()' ` Save the following script as `memcache_standalone.py` on both Prefill and Decode nodes: `import time from memcache_hybrid import DistributedObjectStore store = DistributedObjectStore() result = store.init(0) if result != 0: raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to initialize Memcache: {result}") print("Successfully initialized Memcache") while True: time.sleep(1) ` After MetaService is ready, start the standalone Memcache process on both Prefill and Decode nodes and wait for successful initialization: `export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-local-standalone.conf" python3 memcache_standalone.py ` For additional parameters and capacity constraints, refer to [Memcache and vLLM separated deployment](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#Memcache-and-vLLM-Separated-Deployment). Reuse `launch_online_dp.py` from [the A3 PD deployment example](#a3-series-pd-separation-deployment-with-dspark). Set `MEMCACHE_INSTALL_PATH` to the `Location` reported by `pip show memcache_hybrid`,set `MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR` to the absolute directory containing the configuration files above on both nodes. Use the same checkpoint on both nodes. Keep `/etc/hccn. The MetaService, config store, DP RPC, KV transfer,HTTP ports must be reachable between the nodes. The configuration above uses a DRAM-only pool. To enable SSD in this A3 separated deployment, keep `storage.enabled=false` in the LocalService configuration embedded in vLLM and use the following alternative `mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf` for the standalone process on each node: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = true ubsio.disk.path = <DEDICATED_SSD_BLOCK_DEVICE> ubsio.mem.size_in_gb = 50 ubsio.standalone.device_count = 1 ubsio.standalone.force_new_disk = true ` Use a dedicated, unmounted block device without a filesystem signature. `force_new_disk=true` reinitializes the SSD cache layout at startup and invalidates previous cache contents do not point it at a device containing data to keep. The 20 GiB DRAM contribution and 50 GiB UBS IO allocation are separate per-process host-memory budgets. Size both for the actual prefix working set and available host memory. With one standalone process per host, use `device_count=1` it is not the number of model ranks. After MetaService is ready, start one standalone process on each node with the selected SSD configuration, then all Decode ranks, both Prefill ranks and the proxy: `export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf" python3 memcache_standalone.py ` Wait for `Successfully initialized Memcache` before starting vLLM. vLLM processes continue to use `mmc-local.conf`, not the standalone configuration. Follow [Enable Memcache SSD Cache](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#step-7-enable-memcache-ssd-cache) for SDK requirements, storage ownership and capacity constraints. Verify real cache restore and backend hit activity enabling an SSD flag or seeing HTTP 200 alone does not prove three-level cache reuse.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and Decode within the same node. The quantized DSpark model `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` can be deployed on 1 Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) or

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --data-parallel-size 4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 32 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{
        "ascend_compilation_config": {
            "enable_npugraph_ex": true,
            "enable_static_kernel": false
        },
        "enable_cpu_binding": true,
        "enable_dsa_cp": true,
        "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true
    }'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

The following sections describe multi-node PD separation deployment on Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) and

#### A3 1P1D Deployment with Memcache KV Cache Pool[](#53-a3-1p1d-deployment-with-memcache-kv-cache-pool)

This example deploys the DSpark checkpoint `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` on two A3 servers (16 NPU dies per server), using a Memcache KV Cache Pool:

| Role | DP | TP | PCP | NPU dies | HTTP ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 | 1 | 8 | 16 | 7100-7101 |
| Decode | 16 | 1 | 1 | 16 | 7100-7115 |

Both connectors are configured as children of `MultiConnector`.

Before starting vLLM, follow the [Memcache backend guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend) to check the HDK/CANN and A3 memory prerequisites, install `memfabric-hybrid` and `memcache-hybrid`, configure `mmc-meta.conf`, `mmc-local.conf`,`mmc-local-standalone.conf`,prepare the services below. The Prefill and Decode nodes must use the same MetaService endpoint. Keep the `/etc/hccn.

This example uses separated Memcache deployment so that the pool reserves host memory before vLLM loads the model. Prepare one MetaService configuration and two LocalService configurations as described below.

1. **Prepare the Memcache Services** Create `mmc-meta.conf` on the node that runs MetaService: `ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<META_SERVICE_IP>:18000 ` Create `mmc-local.conf` on both Prefill and Decode nodes for the LocalService embedded in vLLM: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 0GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` Create `mmc-local-standalone.conf` on both nodes for the standalone Memcache process. It uses the same endpoints, world size,protocol, but contributes the host DRAM used by the pool: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` `world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices that can join the pool, not the DP size. Changing it after LocalServices connect requires restarting MetaService. `device_sdma` is recommended for A3 HCCS and requires LingQu Computing Network 1.5 or later. The `20GB` standalone DRAM value is an example set it according to the host memory available after reserving capacity for the operating system and vLLM. `max.dram.size` must be at least the largest `dram.size` contributed by any LocalService. The 20 GiB DRAM contribution and 50 GiB UBS IO allocation are separate per-process host-memory budgets. Size both for the actual prefix working set and available host memory. With one standalone process per host, use `device_count=1` it is not the number of model ranks. After MetaService is ready, start one standalone process on each node with the selected SSD configuration, then all Decode ranks, both Prefill ranks and the proxy: `export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<MEMCACHE_CONFIG_DIR>/mmc-local-standalone-ssd.conf" python3 memcache_standalone.py ` Wait for `Successfully initialized Memcache` before starting vLLM. vLLM processes continue to use `mmc-local.conf`, not the standalone configuration. Each Decode DP rank uses one die. `--dp-address` is the master IP of its own role Prefill and Decode use separate DP groups. After every Prefill engine is ready, start the proxy from [Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) with both Prefill endpoints and all sixteen Decode endpoints: `PREFILL_IP="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" DECODE_IP="<DECODE_NODE_IP>" prefiller_hosts=() decoder_hosts=() for ((i=0 i<2 i++)) do prefiller_hosts+=("$PREFILL_IP") done for ((i=0 i<16 i++)) do decoder_hosts+=("$DECODE_IP") done python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \ --host "$PREFILL_IP" --port 1999 \ --prefiller-hosts "${prefiller_hosts[@]}" \ --prefiller-ports {7100..7101} \ --decoder-hosts "${decoder_hosts[@]}" \ --decoder-ports {7100..7115} ` Send requests to the proxy at `http://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:1999`, using the `dsv4` served model name from Section 6. Verify both the response and the P-to-D transfer in engine logs. To check pool reuse, send the same long prompt (at least 4096 tokens for this example) twice, allowing the first request's KV save to complete before sending the second. Confirm Memcache put activity on the first request and lookup/hit/get activity on a subsequent request in the Prefill logs. A request served entirely by a Prefill engine's local prefix cache may not load from Memcache verify reuse on an engine whose local prefix cache is cold. A successful response alone does not confirm a pool hit. Key pooling parameters: `MultiConnector` combines live P-to-D transfer through `MooncakeHybridConnector` with reusable prefix storage through `AscendStoreConnector`. In this example, both children and the parent use `kv_producer` on Prefill and `kv_consumer` on Decode. Prefill enables prefix caching Decode disables it. Do not enable `enable_dsa_cp` with Model Runner V2. The two roles use the same DSpark checkpoint and five speculative tokens. Keep the connector's DP/TP/PCP sizes aligned with the launcher commands. `lookup_rpc_port` selects the local scheduler-worker IPC endpoint. The implementation adds the DP rank, so this example uses `"0"` for each DP rank. Use a different value for another deployment sharing the same IPC namespace. For capacity tuning, optional SSD configuration,troubleshooting, refer to [KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store)](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html).

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) node or | ModelScope |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 |  | Hugging Face |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8 |  | Quantize locally with msmodelslim |

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w4a4c8` (W4A4 MXFP4 mixed-precision quantization): For how the ultra-low-bit quantization preserves accuracy, see the [W4A4C8 FAQ](#q-how-do-the-w4a4c8-ultra-low-bit-quantized-weights-preserve-accuracy).

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

If you don't want to use the docker image as above, you can also build all from source:

Install `vllm-ascend` from source, refer to [installation](../../getting_started/installation.html).

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to set up the environment on each node.

## Deployment

###

Note

In this tutorial, we suppose you downloaded the model weight to `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/`. Feel free to change it to your own path.

It is recommended that the following service code be encapsulated in a .sh script file and executed in Bash mode.

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and Decode within the same node. The quantized DSpark model `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8` can be deployed on 1 Atlas 800I A3 (128GB × 8) or

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
export OMP_PROC_BIND=false
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=10
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 \
    --served-model-name dsv4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --data-parallel-size 4 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}' \
    --quantization ascend \
    --port 8000 \
    --block-size 32 \
    --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype int8 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --additional-config '{
        "ascend_compilation_config": {
            "enable_npugraph_ex": true,
            "enable_static_kernel": false
        },
        "enable_cpu_binding": true,
        "enable_dsa_cp": true,
        "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true
    }'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length - that is, the sum of input and output tokens for a single request. Adjust it according to your actual scenario.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks, while `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure them together according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model.

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` enables 4-bit TurboQuant quantization for DeepSeek-V4's Compress-4 attention KV cache to reduce memory usage. It is suited to ultra-long-context workloads such as AI coding, especially when KV cache memory limits concurrency. It is independent of weight and indexer cache quantization and requires compatible TurboQuant and fused attention operators. P/D disaggregated deployments are not currently supported.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding to accelerate inference. Use `dspark` for DSpark models. When using DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens` must be at least 5 (check the checkpoint's `config.json`).

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase to reduce scheduling latency.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput.

### PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard single-node deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. This can lead to two issues:

**Prefill preemption interrupts Decode**: Prefill is a compute-intensive task that processes the entire input context at once, while Decode generates tokens one by one. When a new user request arrives, its Prefill phase can preempt and interrupt ongoing Decode tasks, causing jitter and higher time-per-output-token (TPOT) latency.

**Inflexible resource allocation**: Prefill and Decode have fundamentally different computational characteristics — Prefill is compute-bound and memory-bandwidth-intensive, while Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Running them on the same hardware forces a compromise that satisfies neither optimally.

PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses these issues by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated NPU groups, each configured independently, on one or more nodes. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

| Role | DP | TP | PCP | NPU dies | HTTP ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 2 | 1 | 8 | 16 | 7100-7101 |
| Decode | 16 | 1 | 1 | 16 | 7100-7115 |

The deployment follows the same Memcache service setup as [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. `MooncakeHybridConnector` continues to transfer KV cache from Prefill to Decode, while `AscendStoreConnector` stores reusable KV cache in Memcache. Both connectors are configured as children of `MultiConnector`.

Before starting vLLM, follow the [Memcache backend guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend) to check the HDK/CANN and A3 memory prerequisites, install `memfabric-hybrid` and `memcache-hybrid`, configure `mmc-meta.conf`, `mmc-local.conf`,`mmc-local-standalone.conf`,prepare the services below. The Prefill and Decode nodes must use the same MetaService endpoint. Keep the `/etc/hccn.

This example uses separated Memcache deployment so that the pool reserves host memory before vLLM loads the model. Prepare one MetaService configuration and two LocalService configurations as described below.

1. **Prepare the Memcache Services** Create `mmc-meta.conf` on the node that runs MetaService: `ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<META_SERVICE_IP>:18000 ` Create `mmc-local.conf` on both Prefill and Decode nodes for the LocalService embedded in vLLM: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 0GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` Create `mmc-local-standalone.conf` on both nodes for the standalone Memcache process. It uses the same endpoints, world size,protocol, but contributes the host DRAM used by the pool: `ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:15000 ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<META_SERVICE_IP>:16000 ock.mmc.log_level = info ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256 ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false ` `world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices that can join the pool, not the DP size. Start Decode on the Decode node in a separate terminal: `python launch_online_dp.py \ --dp-size 16 --tp-size 1 --dp-size-local 16 --dp-rank-start 0 \ --dp-address "<DECODE_NODE_IP>" --dp-rpc-port 12321 --vllm-start-port 7100 ` Wait until all Decode engines report `Application startup complete`, then start Prefill on the Prefill node: `python launch_online_dp.py \ --dp-size 2 --tp-size 1 --pcp-size 8 --dp-size-local 2 --dp-rank-start 0 \ --dp-address "<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" --dp-rpc-port 12321 --vllm-start-port 7100 ` Each Prefill DP rank uses eight consecutive NPU dies: 0-7 and 8-15. Each Decode DP rank uses one die. `--dp-address` is the master IP of its own role Prefill and Decode use separate DP groups. After every Prefill engine is ready, start the proxy from [Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) with both Prefill endpoints and all sixteen Decode endpoints: `PREFILL_IP="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" DECODE_IP="<DECODE_NODE_IP>" prefiller_hosts=() decoder_hosts=() for ((i=0 i<2 i++)) do prefiller_hosts+=("$PREFILL_IP") done for ((i=0 i<16 i++)) do decoder_hosts+=("$DECODE_IP") done python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \ --host "$PREFILL_IP" --port 1999 \ --prefiller-hosts "${prefiller_hosts[@]}" \ --prefiller-ports {7100..7101} \ --decoder-hosts "${decoder_hosts[@]}" \ --decoder-ports {7100..7115} ` Send requests to the proxy at `http://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:1999`, using the `dsv4` served model name from Section 6. Verify both the response and the P-to-D transfer in engine logs. To check pool reuse, send the same long prompt (at least 4096 tokens for this example) twice, allowing the first request's KV save to complete before sending the second. Confirm Memcache put activity on the first request and lookup/hit/get activity on a subsequent request in the Prefill logs. A request served entirely by a Prefill engine's local prefix cache may not load from Memcache verify reuse on an engine whose local prefix cache is cold. A successful response alone does not confirm a pool hit. Key pooling parameters: `MultiConnector` combines live P-to-D transfer through `MooncakeHybridConnector` with reusable prefix storage through `AscendStoreConnector`. In this example, both children and the parent use `kv_producer` on Prefill and `kv_consumer` on Decode. Decode does not put or load pool entries unless `consumer_is_to_put` or `consumer_is_to_load` is explicitly enabled. `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` must match across all engines. Prefill enables prefix caching Decode disables it. Keep `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` on both roles and the top-level `kv_load_failure_policy` as `fail` the `recompute` load-failure policy does not support DeepSeek-V4 hybrid attention. `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` is required for PCP. Do not enable `enable_dsa_cp` with Model Runner V2. The two roles use the same DSpark checkpoint and five speculative tokens. Keep the connector's DP/TP/PCP sizes aligned with the launcher commands. `lookup_rpc_port` selects the local scheduler-worker IPC endpoint. The implementation adds the DP rank, so this example uses `"0"` for each DP rank. Use a different value for another deployment sharing the same IPC namespace. For capacity tuning, optional SSD configuration,troubleshooting, refer to [KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store)](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html).

Key Parameter Descriptions:

`--data-parallel-size` sets the global number of data parallel ranks,`--data-parallel-size-local` sets the number of DP ranks on the current node.

`--data-parallel-start-rank` specifies the starting data parallel rank of the current node. Set a unique value on each headless node (e.g., Node1 = 1). On Node0, omit `--data-parallel-start-rank` even when the start rank is 0, to avoid enabling hybrid load balancing with headless remote engines.

`--data-parallel-address` specifies the IP address of the data parallel master node (Node0). It must be consistent across all nodes.

`--data-parallel-rpc-port` is the DP RPC port. Use the same value on all nodes and ensure the port is available.

`--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size within each DP rank. Configure it together with the DP sizes according to the deployment topology and available NPUs.

`--prefill-context-parallel-size` configures prefill context parallelism (PCP) on Model Runner V2 (MRv2), which spreads a long prompt across multiple NPUs during prefill. Besides speeding up prefill, enabling PCP also shards the o_proj weights across the PCP group, providing partial tensor parallelism even when `--tensor-parallel-size` is `1`. The 950DT DP mixed-deployment uses `DP2/TP1` with PCP `8`,the o_proj weight sharding also relieves its memory pressure. Do not combine it with `enable_dsa_cp`, which is mutually exclusive with PCP and unsupported by the V2 model runner.

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--headless` (used on non-master nodes) disables the API server on the node, since only the master node serves requests.

`--max-model-len` specifies the maximum context length. The example values are intended to allow startup with the documented hardware and configuration. To tune this value, check the startup log `Maximum concurrency for L tokens per request: Cx`: `L × C` provides a rough KV-cache capacity reference for increasing the context length with the same configuration. Use the smallest estimate across all ranks and, for PD-disaggregated deployment, across both Prefill and Decode pools.

`--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of requests that each DP group is allowed to process. If the number of requests sent to the service exceeds this limit, the excess requests will remain in a waiting state and will not be scheduled. Note that the time spent in the waiting state is also counted in metrics such as TTFT and TPOT. Therefore, when testing performance, it is generally recommended that `--max-num-seqs` * `--data-parallel-size` >= the actual total concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4`, `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v4`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice`,`--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4` enable the DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer behavior, automatic tool calling,reasoning-output parsing.

`--no-enable-prefix-caching` indicates that prefix caching is disabled. To enable it, remove this option.

`--block-size` sets the KV cache block size. To enable the experimental 4k prefix cache hit support, change it from `128` to `32`.

950DT products do not require this option.

`--model-loader-extra-config='{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 128}'` selects the multi-thread weight iterator. `enable_multithread_load` must be a JSON boolean and `num_threads` must be a positive integer.

`--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch` is an alternative that warms checkpoint files into the OS page cache before the normal iterator loads them. Do not combine it with multi-thread loading: the default loader rejects `prefetch`, `eager`,`torchao` when `enable_multithread_load` is `true`. The examples in this document use only multi-thread loading.

`--speculative-config` configures speculative decoding. Use `mtp` for the preview MTP checkpoint and `dspark` for the `DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813` checkpoint. For DSpark, use the value declared by the checkpoint the example uses 5 speculative tokens,all ranks must use the same value.

`--kv-cache-dtype` and `--attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype` set the KV cache data type. The 950DT example uses FP8 KV cache with both options set to `fp8`.

`--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` keeps the hybrid KV cache manager enabled. DeepSeek-V4 deployments require this flag otherwise, the service may OOM during startup.

`--async-scheduling` enables asynchronous scheduling to overlap scheduler overhead with model execution.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full ACL graph execution in the decode phase.

`--additional-config` enables Ascend-specific optimizations. `enable_npugraph_ex` enables enhanced ACL graph execution, `enable_static_kernel: false` keeps static-kernel compilation disabled, `enable_cpu_binding` enables Ascend-native CPU binding, `enable_shared_expert_dp` enables data parallelism for shared experts,`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better MoE throughput. `enable_fused_mc2: 0` disables the Fused MC2 dispatch/combine path.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

### Multi-Node PD Separation Deployment

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment: [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html).

In the standard deployment mode, Prefill (prompt processing) and Decode (token generation) tasks run on the same set of NPUs. PD (Prefill-Decode) separation addresses this by running Prefill and Decode on dedicated node groups, each configured independently. This architecture is recommended for production deployments with concurrent multi-user workloads, where stable latency and high throughput are both required.

The following tabs describe PD separation deployment on Ascend 950DT nodes (96GB × 8)
