guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

Download the checkpoint from ModelScope for the hardware shown below. A3 and do not interchange them. The scripts use `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/vllm-ascend/<checkpoint-name>` as a local mount path, not as a download source. Preserve the exact case of the repository name when naming the local directory.

| Checkpoint | Hardware | Deployment | Download | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8-mxfp8 |  | 1 node for single-node deployment; 2 nodes for PD | ModelScope | Supports a W8A8C8 configuration: C8 is dynamic KV-cache quantization. Set --kv-cache-dtype fp8 in the serving command to enable FP8 KV cache; no separate C8 checkpoint is required. |
| GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 | A3 series (64GB × 16) | 1 node for single-node deployment; 2 nodes for PD | ModelScope | Supports a W8A8C8 configuration: C8 is dynamic KV-cache quantization. Set --kv-cache-dtype int8 in the serving command to enable INT8 KV cache; no separate C8 checkpoint is required. |
| GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8 |  | 2 nodes for colocated deployment; 4 nodes for PD | ModelScope | / |

You can use [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) to quantize the model directly.

The checkpoints linked above are already quantized and can be served directly. For self-quantization, follow the installation and command examples in the [msModelSlim quantization guide](https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/en/mindstudio/2610/TITools/msModelSlim/docs/en/user_guide/feature_guide/quick_quantization_v1/usage.md) and select the configuration for the exact model and target hardware from the [model recipes](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim/tree/master/lab_practice). Do not reuse a different model's YAML file.

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

If you want to deploy multi-node environment, you need to verify multi-node communication according to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

Select an image for your hardware and start a container on each node. Refer to [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image) for details.

Start the Docker container on each node.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a3
export NAME=vllm-ascend

# If you use Docker bridge networking, expose the required ports for multi-node communication in advance.
docker run --rm \
--name $NAME \
--net=host \
--shm-size=100g \
--device /dev/davinci0 \
--device /dev/davinci1 \
--device /dev/davinci2 \
--device /dev/davinci3 \
--device /dev/davinci4 \
--device /dev/davinci5 \
--device /dev/davinci6 \
--device /dev/davinci7 \
--device /dev/davinci8 \
--device /dev/davinci9 \
--device /dev/davinci10 \
--device /dev/davinci11 \
--device /dev/davinci12 \
--device /dev/davinci13 \
--device /dev/davinci14 \
--device /dev/davinci15 \
--device /dev/davinci_manager \
--device /dev/devmm_svm \
--device /dev/hisi_hdc \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
-v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
-v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf:ro \
-v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
-it $IMAGE bash
```

## Deployment

###

Note

Do not set `enable_thinking: false` / `thinking: false` for GLM-5.3-Flash, otherwise the output quality may degrade.

**Common Parameter Descriptions**

These definitions apply to the deployment scenarios in this chapter. Use the values in the selected hardware and role scripts hardware-specific values are not interchangeable.

| Parameter | Meaning and constraints |
|---|---|
| HCCL_BUFFSIZE | CANN/HCCL communication buffer size in MB; a positive integer, with a documented default of 200. Larger buffers consume more device memory, multiplied by the number of communication domains. Keep the example's hardware/role-specific value and account for this memory when sizing the KV cache. See the CANN HCCL reference for allocation details and version-specific constraints. |
| HCCL_IF_IP and socket interface variables | Set the current node's communication IP and matching network interface. Peers must be reachable through the selected network. |
| --data-parallel-size, --tensor-parallel-size, --pipeline-parallel-size | DP is the number of data-parallel ranks; TP and PP partition each model engine across devices and pipeline stages. Follow the topology and placement in the selected tab. |
| --max-model-len | Maximum total sequence length in tokens, including input and generated output. Requests must fit this limit and the available KV cache capacity. |
| --max-num-seqs, --max-num-batched-tokens | Scheduler limits for sequences and tokens processed in an iteration, respectively. These are per engine, not aggregate proxy limits; tune them together with context length and memory capacity. |
| --gpu-memory-utilization | Fraction of device memory budgeted to the model executor. Despite the flag name, it also applies to the NPU backend. Leave room for communication buffers and other device allocations. |
| --quantization ascend | Selects the Ascend quantization loader for ModelSlim checkpoints. Use weights matching the selected hardware and quantization format. |
| --kv-cache-dtype, --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype | Select the attention and indexer KV cache formats. Follow the selected checkpoint and hardware example; the supported formats differ across platforms. |
| --tool-call-parser glm47, --enable-auto-tool-choice | Parse tool calls and allow automatic tool selection. Configure them on both API-serving roles in a PD deployment. |
| --reasoning-parser | Separates reasoning from the final answer. Use glm47 for all examples on this page. |
| --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch | Reads checkpoint files into the operating system page cache before workers load them. It can help with network or high-latency storage and needs sufficient host memory; it does not preload weights into NPU memory. See vLLM weight-loading options. |

### Single-Node Online Deployment

#### A3 series[](#glm53-flash-5-1-a3)

- Quantized model `GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8` can be deployed on 1 A3 series (64GB × 16) .

Run the following script to execute online inference.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024

vllm serve Eco-Tech/GLM-5.3-Flash-w8a8   \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name glm \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization ascend \
  --kv-cache-dtype int8 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 5, "method": "deepseek_mtp", "enforce_eager": false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}' \
  --api-server-count 1
```

**Key Parameter Descriptions**

Only the key parameters specific to this model/scenario are described below. `max-model-len` and `max-num-seqs` need to be set according to the actual usage scenario.

**Model-specific parameters:**

16 on A3 series. This layout is recommended to balance memory capacity and compute efficiency for the w8a8 weights.

`--enable-expert-parallel`: Must be enabled for the MoE architecture of GLM-5.3-Flash.

`--quantization ascend`: Enables Ascend quantization for the w8a8 quantized weights.

`--kv-cache-dtype`: Enables 8-bit KV cache quantization (C8) for Sparse Flash Attention (SFA). Use C8 when long contexts or `int8` on A3 series. KV cache quantization is independent of weight quantization: enabling C8 does not require W8A8 weights or a separate C8 checkpoint.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`: Enables graph capture for the decode phase only, improving decode performance by reducing kernel launch overhead.

`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}'`: Allows at most one image per prompt and disables video input in all deployment examples.

five on A3 series. `enforce_eager: true` keeps the MTP draft model in eager mode on , while `enforce_eager: false` enables graph mode for the draft model on A3 series. GLM-5.3-Flash supports MTP draft graph execution the forced-eager restriction for other GLM models does not apply to this model.

### PD Disaggregated Deployment

Before starting any role script, verify [multi-node communication](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect), select the matching host IP and interface on every node,allow the DP RPC, API, HCCL socket, Mooncake handshake/control,transfer-engine ports through the firewall. Use the port settings in the selected hardware tab allowing only the proxy port is insufficient. Physical node count and the number of DP engines are different: follow each tab's topology and endpoint mapping.

 A3 series and Decode node before following the platform-specific instructions below.

```python
import argparse
import multiprocessing
import subprocess

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--template", default="./run_p.sh")
    parser.add_argument("--dp-size", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tp-size", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-size-local", type=int, default=-1)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-rank-start", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-address", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--dp-rpc-port", default="12325")
    parser.add_argument("--vllm-start-port", type=int, default=8000)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.dp_size_local == -1:
        args.dp_size_local = args.dp_size
    return args

def run(args, devices, port, dp_rank):
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "bash",
            args.template,
            devices,
            str(port),
            str(args.dp_size),
            str(dp_rank),
            args.dp_address,
            args.dp_rpc_port,
            str(args.tp_size),
        ],
        check=True,
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    processes = []
    for i in range(args.dp_size_local):
        devices = ",".join(
            str(device)
            for device in range(i * args.tp_size, (i + 1) * args.tp_size)
        )
        process = multiprocessing.Process(
            target=run,
            args=(
                args,
                devices,
                args.vllm_start_port + i,
                args.dp_rank_start + i,
            ),
        )
        processes.append(process)
        process.start()
    for process in processes:
        process.join()
```

The launcher passes visible devices, engine port, global DP size, DP rank, DP address, DP RPC port,TP size to each role script as `$1` through `$7`.

#### A3 series[](#glm53-flash-5-3-a3)

This example uses two A3 series servers. The Prefill node runs two DP ranks with TP8 (DP2/TP8),the Decode node runs four DP ranks with TP4 (DP4/TP4). Both layouts consume all 16 logical devices on their respective servers. `MooncakeConnectorV2` transfers KV cache from the Prefill engines to the Decode engines.

Before starting the services, replace `LOCAL_IP`, `NIC_NAME`,`MODEL_PATH` in the following scripts with values for the deployment environment. These scripts target an A3 series supernode using HCCS with its device RoCE ports down. They explicitly select `hccs:device` for device communication the socket interface variables still select the host network. Adjust the resource configuration for other network topologies.

Start Decode first, then Prefill. In another terminal, check `<DECODE_NODE_IP>:9900/health` through port `9903` and `<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:9081/health` through port `9082` with `curl --fail`. Start the proxy only after all six endpoints respond successfully inspect each launcher terminal if a rank fails to initialize.

##### Start the Prefill node[](#start-the-prefill-node)

On the Prefill node, save the following script as `run_p.sh`. The launcher passes the visible devices, API port, DP configuration,TP size as positional arguments.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# This A3 series supernode uses HCCS; its device RoCE ports are down.
export ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG='{"comm_resource_config.protocol_desc":["hccs:device"]}'
export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.2"}'

LOCAL_IP="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>"
NIC_NAME="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
MODEL_PATH="<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>"

export HCCL_IF_IP="$LOCAL_IP"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NIC_NAME"
export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NIC_NAME"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NIC_NAME"
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1"

exec vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port "$2" \
  --data-parallel-size "$3" \
  --data-parallel-rank "$4" \
  --data-parallel-address "$5" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \
  --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name glm \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization ascend \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype int8 \
  --prefix-cache-retention-interval None \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 3, "method": "deepseek_mtp", "enforce_eager": true}' \
  --additional-config '{
    "enable_flashcomm1": true,
    "enable_dsa_cp": true,
    "enable_prefill_mc2": true,
    "enable_fused_mc2": 1,
    "enable_shared_expert_dp": true,
    "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": false
  }' \
  --kv-transfer-config \
  '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "engine_id": "0", "kv_port": "36680"}'
```

Start two DP2/TP8 Prefill engines. `--dp-address` uses the Prefill node IP. The launcher assigns API ports `9081-9082`.

```shell
python launch_online_dp.py \
  --template ./run_p.sh \
  --dp-size 2 \
  --tp-size 8 \
  --dp-address "<PREFILL_NODE_IP>" \
  --vllm-start-port 9081
```

##### Start the Decode Node[](#start-the-decode-node)

On the Decode node, save the following script as `run_d.sh`. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graph mode for the target model, enables graph mode for the MTP draft model,enables FlashComm1.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# This A3 series supernode uses HCCS; its device RoCE ports are down.
export ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG='{"comm_resource_config.protocol_desc":["hccs:device"]}'
export ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.2"}'

LOCAL_IP="<DECODE_NODE_IP>"
NIC_NAME="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
MODEL_PATH="<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>"

export HCCL_IF_IP="$LOCAL_IP"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NIC_NAME"
export TP_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NIC_NAME"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="$NIC_NAME"
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1"

exec vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port "$2" \
  --data-parallel-size "$3" \
  --data-parallel-rank "$4" \
  --data-parallel-address "$5" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \
  --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name glm \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 192 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization ascend \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --kv-cache-dtype int8 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens": 3, "method": "deepseek_mtp", "enforce_eager": false}' \
  --additional-config '{
    "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true,
    "recompute_scheduler_enable": true,
    "enable_shared_expert_dp": true,
    "enable_flashcomm1": true
  }' \
  --kv-transfer-config \
  '{"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "engine_id": "1", "kv_port": "36580"}'
```

Start four TP4 Decode engines(total DP4). `--dp-address` uses the Decode node IP. The launcher assigns API ports `9900-9903`.

```shell
python launch_online_dp.py \
  --template ./run_d.sh \
  --dp-size 4 \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --dp-address "<DECODE_NODE_IP>" \
  --vllm-start-port 9900
```

##### Deploy the PD Proxy[](#deploy-the-pd-proxy)

After all Prefill and Decode engines are ready, open another terminal in the Prefill container and start the [load-balancing proxy](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/main/examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py). The proxy listens on port `8081`, distributes requests across Prefill endpoints `9081-9082`,then forwards Decode work to endpoints `9900-9903`.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash

P_IP="${P_IP:-<PREFILL_NODE_IP>}"
P_N=${P_N:-2}
P_PORT0=${P_PORT0:-9081}
D_IP="${D_IP:-<DECODE_NODE_IP>}"
D_N=${D_N:-4}
D_PORT0=${D_PORT0:-9900}

unset http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy
python /vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8081 \
  --prefiller-hosts $(printf "$P_IP %.0s" $(seq 1 "$P_N")) \
  --prefiller-ports $(seq "$P_PORT0" $((P_PORT0 + P_N - 1))) \
  --decoder-hosts $(printf "$D_IP %.0s" $(seq 1 "$D_N")) \
  --decoder-ports $(seq "$D_PORT0" $((D_PORT0 + D_N - 1)))
```

**Key Parameter Descriptions**

- `--data-parallel-size` and `--tensor-parallel-size` define DP2/TP8 on Prefill and DP4/TP4 on Decode. Both layouts use all 16 logical devices on their respective A3 series nodes.
- `--data-parallel-address` and `--data-parallel-rpc-port` coordinate DP ranks within one role. Prefill and Decode use their respective node IPs. The default RPC port `12325` can be reused because the roles run on different hosts.
- `--vllm-start-port 9081` assigns API ports `9081-9082` on Prefill, while `--vllm-start-port 9900` assigns `9900-9903` on Decode. All endpoints must be reachable from the proxy.
- Both roles use `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--kv-cache-dtype int8`,MTP speculative decoding with three speculative tokens. The MTP draft model uses `enforce_eager: true` on Prefill and `enforce_eager: false` on Decode.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` explicitly selects model runner V1 on both roles for this configuration.
- Prefill uses `--max-num-seqs 64` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. Decode uses `--max-num-seqs 32` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 192`. Tune these role-specific scheduler limits independently for the target workload.
- Prefill sets `--prefix-cache-retention-interval None`.
- Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graph mode. Both roles explicitly enable FlashComm1.
- Prefill sets `enable_dsa_cp: true`, `enable_prefill_mc2: true`, `enable_fused_mc2: 1`,`enable_shared_expert_dp: true`, with `multistream_overlap_shared_expert: false`. Decode sets `multistream_overlap_shared_expert: true`, `enable_shared_expert_dp: true`,`recompute_scheduler_enable: true`.
- Both Prefill and Decode use `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}'`, allowing at most one image per prompt and disabling video input.
- `MooncakeConnectorV2` transfers KV cache between the two roles. `kv_role` must be `kv_producer` on Prefill and `kv_consumer` on Decode. The role-specific KV ports must be available on their respective hosts.
- `ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG` selects `hccs:device`,`ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES` sets resource configuration version `1.2` for this HCCS supernode. `HCCL_IF_IP` and all socket interface variables must select the host network used by the configured node IPs. The DP RPC, engine, Mooncake,proxy ports must be allowed by the host firewall.

### Prefill-Decode Disaggregation with KV Cache Pool

This section uses the Memcache backend for A3 series and

`MooncakeConnectorV2` continues to transfer KV cache from Prefill to Decode.

`AscendStoreConnector` lets Prefill look up, load,save cached prefixes in the KV Cache Pool, reducing repeated Prefill computation.

For backend installation, hardware dependencies, memory sizing, eviction,tenant options, refer to the [KV Cache Pool Deployment Guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html).

#### A3 series[](#glm53-flash-5-4-a3)

##### Prepare the Memcache Backend[](#prepare-the-memcache-backend)

Follow [Scenario 2: Memcache Backend](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#scenario-2-memcache-backend) for prerequisite checks and memory sizing. The A3 series HCCS configuration uses `device_sdma`, which requires LingQu Computing Network 1.5 or later. Also check the HDK and CANN requirements in the guide's [HDK and CANN Version Compatibility Reference](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#hdk-and-cann-version-compatibility-reference).

LingQu Computing Network is a host-side platform prerequisite for `device_sdma`, not the version of the Memcache Python package. Before starting the containers, have the platform administrator check the installed LingQu release against the server's vendor installation records and confirm version 1.5 or later together with the HDK/CANN compatibility matrix linked above. Installing or upgrading `memcache-hybrid` alone does not establish this prerequisite.

**When starting the A3 series containers on both Prefill and Decode nodes, you must include the following read-only mount in the Docker command from Section 4:**

```shell
-v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf:ro \
```

The Docker images in Section 4 already include `memfabric-hybrid` and `memcache-hybrid`. Locate the installed Memcache package in each container:

```shell
pip show memcache_hybrid
```

The `Location` field from `pip show` is `<PYTHON_SITE_PACKAGES>` in the commands below. Replace `<CONFIG_DIRECTORY>` with the absolute directory containing the configuration files on each node.

This example stores pooled KV cache in DDR memory on both the Prefill and Decode nodes. The Memcache LocalService initializes within each vLLM worker,each worker contributes `20GB` of DDR memory to the pool. Decode receives KV cache through `MooncakeConnectorV2`.

On the Prefill node, create `mmc-meta.conf`:

```ini
ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:5000
ock.mmc.meta_service.config_store_url = tcp://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:6000
ock.mmc.meta_service.metrics_url = http://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:8000
ock.mmc.log_level = info
```

On both the Prefill and Decode nodes, create the following `mmc-local.conf`:

```ini
ock.mmc.meta_service_url = tcp://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:5000
ock.mmc.local_service.config_store_url = tcp://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:6000
ock.mmc.log_level = info
ock.mmc.local_service.world_size = 256
ock.mmc.local_service.protocol = device_sdma
ock.mmc.local_service.dram.size = 20GB
ock.mmc.local_service.max.dram.size = 1024GB
ock.mmc.local_service.storage.enabled = false
```

`dram.size` specifies the DDR capacity allocated per worker. Prefill (DP2/TP8) and Decode (DP4/TP4) each start 16 workers. At `20GB` per worker, each node contributes `320GB`, for a total DDR pool capacity of `640GB`. Reserve sufficient DDR memory for the operating system and vLLM. For `device_sdma`, keep each non-zero size aligned to `1GB`.

`world_size` is the maximum number of LocalServices supported by Memcache. Keep it consistent across all workers and large enough for the 32 workers in this deployment.

##### Add the Pool Environment Variables[](#add-the-pool-environment-variables)

In both `run_p.sh` and `run_d.

```shell
MEMCACHE_PACKAGE_DIR="<PYTHON_SITE_PACKAGES>/memcache_hybrid"
PYTHON_LIB_DIR="$(python -c 'import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var("LIBDIR"))')"

export PYTHONHASHSEED=0
export MMC_LOCAL_CONFIG_PATH="<CONFIG_DIRECTORY>/mmc-local.conf"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${MEMCACHE_PACKAGE_DIR}/lib:${PYTHON_LIB_DIR}:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"

# A3 series HCCS fabric-memory pooling.
export ACL_OP_INIT_MODE=1
export ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM=1
```

Use the same `PYTHONHASHSEED` and Memcache service endpoints on both nodes.

##### Update the Prefill and Decode Connectors[](#update-the-prefill-and-decode-connectors)

For A3 series KV Cache Pool deployment, add `--enable-prefix-caching` to both `run_p.sh` and `run_d. GLM-5.3-Flash has linear-attention state,`AscendStoreConnector` requires `mamba_cache_mode=align` the model configuration selects this mode when prefix caching is enabled. Keep the hybrid KV cache manager enabled and `use_layerwise` disabled for this configuration.

Replace the final `--kv-transfer-config` argument in `run_p.sh` with the following fragment.

```shell
  --kv-transfer-config \
  '{
    "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "engine_id": "0",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "connectors": [
        {
          "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2",
          "kv_role": "kv_producer",
          "kv_port": "36680"
        },
        {
          "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",
          "kv_role": "kv_producer",
          "kv_connector_extra_config": {
            "backend": "memcache",
            "memcache_dp_init_barrier": true,
            "use_layerwise": false,
            "lookup_rpc_port": '"$((37000 + $4))"'
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

Replace the final `--kv-transfer-config` argument in `run_d.sh` with the following fragment.

```shell
  --kv-transfer-config \
  '{
    "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "engine_id": "1",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "connectors": [
        {
          "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2",
          "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
          "kv_port": "36580"
        },
        {
          "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",
          "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
          "kv_connector_extra_config": {
            "backend": "memcache",
            "memcache_dp_init_barrier": true,
            "use_layerwise": false,
            "consumer_is_to_load": false,
            "consumer_is_to_put": false,
            "lookup_rpc_port": '"$((37100 + $4))"'
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`$4` is the DP rank passed by `launch_online_dp.py`. Each engine must have a unique `lookup_rpc_port`. The Prefill lookup values are `37000-37001`,the Decode lookup values are `37100-37103`.

Keep `memcache_dp_init_barrier` set to `true` on every rank in each DP group. It synchronizes workers after Memcache initialization and before NPU graph capture. Set it in the `AscendStoreConnector` child, as shown above.

##### Start the Services[](#start-the-services)

Start the services in this order: Memcache MetaService → Decode → Prefill → Proxy. Each vLLM worker initializes its Memcache LocalService during startup.

1. In a separate terminal in the Prefill container, start MetaService. Ensure ports `5000` and `6000` are reachable from both nodes and port `8000` is available for metrics.

```shell
MEMCACHE_PACKAGE_DIR="<PYTHON_SITE_PACKAGES>/memcache_hybrid"
PYTHON_LIB_DIR="$(python -c 'import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var("LIBDIR"))')"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${MEMCACHE_PACKAGE_DIR}/lib:${PYTHON_LIB_DIR}:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
export MMC_META_CONFIG_PATH="<CONFIG_DIRECTORY>/mmc-meta.conf"
python -c "from memcache_hybrid import MetaService; MetaService.main()"
```

1. Wait until all four Decode engines on ports `9900-9903` are ready and their Memcache LocalServices have reserved the configured DDR pool memory.
2. Wait until both Prefill engines on ports `9081-9082` are ready and their Memcache LocalServices have reserved the configured DDR pool memory.
3. Send inference requests to `<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:8081` using the examples in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

##### Verify KV Cache Reuse[](#verify-kv-cache-reuse)

Warm up the pool through the proxy with a prompt longer than one cache block, then repeat requests with the same prefix. Check Prefill output for successful pool saves, lookups, loads,cache hits,check Decode output for successful P→D transfers.

Capture the Prefill launcher's standard output and standard error when starting the service. Compare `vllm:ascend_store_load_get_keys_total` at each Prefill API's `/metrics` endpoint before and after repeating the prefix on the other Prefill rank: an increase records pool GET keys, unlike a local prefix-cache hit alone. Also verify that requests complete successfully a GET counter alone does not prove a successful transfer or an accuracy result.

The proxy distributes requests across two Prefill engines. A repeated request can also hit an engine's local prefix cache confirm pool load/hit information on the other Prefill rank to verify shared pool reuse. Only complete, cacheable blocks are reused, so a partial trailing block can still require computation.

## Verification

Once the selected deployment is ready, use the separate proxy host and port `8000`. For the A3 series/, use the Prefill node IP and  use the configured proxy host and port `28000`. For a single-node or  use the API endpoint exposed by its vLLM service.

```shell
curl http://<service_ip>:<service_port>/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "glm",
        "prompt": "The future of AI is",
        "max_tokens": 50
    }'
```

Expected Result: The response is a JSON payload containing the model's generated text in a text_completion format.

```json
{
  "id": "cmpl-123abc",
  "object": "text_completion",
  "created": 1725444000,
  "model": "glm",
  "choices": [
    {
      "text": " incredibly promising, with rapid advancements in machine learning and autonomous systems.",
      "index": 0,
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 5,
    "completion_tokens": 15,
    "total_tokens": 20
  }
}
```

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

Download the Gemma4 model weight to a local or shared directory, such as `/root/.cache/`. In the following examples, replace `/root/.cache/path/to/gemma4` with your actual model path.

| Weight version | Description | Recommended hardware | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| google/gemma-4-31B-it | BF16 dense model. | 950PR&950DT Products. Adjust the number of visible NPUs according to the available memory. | ModelScope |
| Eco-Tech/gemma-4-31B-it-w4a4-mxfp4 | MXFP4 quantized dense model. | 1 950DT Products (96GB × 8) node. | ModelScope |
| google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | BF16 MoE model with approximately 26 billion total and 4 billion active parameters. | 950PR&950DT Products. Use tensor parallelism or expert parallelism according to the deployment plan. | ModelScope |
| Eco-Tech/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-w4a4-mxfp4 | MXFP4 quantized MoE model. | 1 950DT Products (96GB × 8) node. | ModelScope |

Both MXFP4 checkpoints contain a `quant_model_description.json` file and require `--quantization ascend` when served. For information about preparing quantized weights, refer to the [Quantization Guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/quantization.html).

## Installation

Select the official all-in-one vLLM Ascend Docker image for your hardware. The MXFP4 checkpoints are supported on 950PR&950DT Products

The Gemma4 MXFP4 checkpoints were validated with this image. You can use it or a later compatible v0.30.0 A5 image.

```shell
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a5
docker pull ${IMAGE}
```

Follow the hardware-specific `docker run` command in [Using a prebuilt image](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image) and mount the directory containing the Gemma4 weights into the container. The prebuilt image includes the matching CANN user-space environment, PyTorch, TorchNPU, vLLM,vLLM Ascend versions.

After entering the container, verify the environment:

```shell
npu-smi info
python -m pip show vllm vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: `npu-smi info` lists the expected Ascend devices,both Python packages are installed.

## Deployment

### Multi-Card Deployment

950PR&950DT Products. For different model sizes or device counts, adjust `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `--tensor-parallel-size` according to the available NPUs.

## Verification

After the service is started, Gemma4 can be invoked through OpenAI-compatible APIs.

### Completions API

```shell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma4",
    "prompt": "Explain why graph execution improves decode performance.",
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

### Chat Completions API

```shell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma4",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Explain why graph execution improves decode performance."}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the request returns HTTP 200,the JSON response contains a `choices` field with generated text from the model.

### Multimodal Chat Completions API

Send an image request to verify Gemma4 multimodal inference:

```shell
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemma4",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "image_url",
            "image_url": {
              "url": "https://modelscope.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/resource/tiger.jpeg"
            }
          },
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Describe this image."
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 128,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the request returns HTTP 200,the response describes the image in the `choices` field.

### Offline Inference

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="/root/.cache/path/to/gemma4",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    tensor_parallel_size=4,
    compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"},
)

sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128)
outputs = llm.generate(
    ["Explain why graph execution improves decode performance."],
    sampling_params,
)

for output in outputs:
    print(output.outputs[0].text)
```

950PR&950DT Products. For different model sizes or device counts, adjust `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `--tensor-parallel-size` according to the available NPUs.

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-M3 (BF16) |  | ModelScope | / |
| MiniMax-M3-w8a8 (W8A8) |  | ModelScope | / |
| MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 (MXFP8) | 1 950DT node (96GB × 8) | ModelScope | Supports a W8A8C8 configuration: C8 is dynamic KV-cache quantization. Set --kv-cache-dtype fp8 in the serving command to enable FP8 KV cache. |
| MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA | / | ModelScope | Draft model for EAGLE3 speculative decoding; uses Grouped Query Attention (GQA). |

It is recommended to place the model weight in a shared cache directory.

Record the downloaded model directories for use in the deployment commands. Set `WEIGHT_PATH` (or `MODEL_PATH` in the PD templates) to the target-weight directory, for example `/models/MiniMax-M3-w8a8`,`EAGLE3_WEIGHT_PATH` to the downloaded EAGLE3 draft directory when speculative decoding is enabled. Replace the weight-path placeholders below with these actual paths and ensure they are accessible inside the container. `LOG_PATH` is a writable log-file path the single-node examples use files in the current directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication (Optional)

For multi-node deployment, verify the communication environment by following [Verify Multi-node Communication Environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

## Installation

You can use the official all-in-one Docker image. For the available image tags and published versions, refer to [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

**Step 1:** Download the latest Docker image

```bash
docker pull quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{tag}
```

**Step 2:** Start Docker container

Select the `docker run` command for your hardware platform:

```bash
# Set the vLLM Ascend image name.
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:{tag}
export NAME=minimax-m3-dev

# 950DT products have 8 NPUs and use Device UB.
docker run --rm \
--name $NAME \
--net=host \
--privileged=true \
--shm-size=60g \
--device /dev/davinci_manager \
--device /dev/hisi_hdc \
--device /dev/ummu \
--device /dev/uburma \
--device /dev/davinci0 \
--device /dev/davinci1 \
--device /dev/davinci2 \
--device /dev/davinci3 \
--device /dev/davinci4 \
--device /dev/davinci5 \
--device /dev/davinci6 \
--device /dev/davinci7 \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/firmware:/usr/local/Ascend/firmware \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
-v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
-v /etc/hixlep:/etc/hixlep \
-v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf \
-v /var/log/npu/:/usr/slog \
-v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
-it $IMAGE bash
```

Adjust data volume mounts (for example, model weights and datasets) according to your environment. On 950DT products

In another terminal on the same host, check the container status (replace `minimax-m3-dev` if you changed `NAME`):

```bash
docker ps --filter name=minimax-m3-dev
```

Expected result: The container is listed with status `Up`. In the original container terminal, verify the vLLM Ascend version:

```bash
pip show vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: The version information is displayed, matching the pulled image version.

## Deployment

###

Start the online serving service with the deployment commands in the following sections. Select the tab for your hardware platform and weight format.

For descriptions of the standard `vllm serve` arguments used in the deployment examples, refer to the [vLLM Serving Arguments documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/cli/serve/#arguments). For Ascend-specific options passed through `--additional-config`, refer to [Additional Configuration](../../user_guide/configuration/additional_config.html). For Ascend-specific environment variables, refer to [Environment Variables](../../user_guide/configuration/env_vars.html).

The `--speculative-config` examples use single-quoted JSON. The `'"${EAGLE3_WEIGHT_PATH}"'` segment expands the draft-weight path within that JSON.

### Single-Node Deployment

1 Atlas 800 950DT products (96GB × 8).

Note

The `--quantization` parameter is **only required for quantized weights** and must match the weight variant:

- **BF16 weights** (`MiniMax-M3`): do **not** add `--quantization` the model loads as float.
- **W8A8 weights** (`MiniMax-M3-w8a8`, ModelSlim format): use `--quantization ascend`. vLLM Ascend can auto-detect this from the checkpoint files, but specifying it explicitly is recommended for clarity.
- **MXFP8 weights** (`MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`): use `--quantization mxfp8`.

Adding the wrong `--quantization` value (or adding it to BF16 weights) will cause the checkpoint to be misinterpreted and fail to load.

```bash
WEIGHT_PATH="<MINIMAX_M3_MXFP8_PATH>"
EAGLE3_WEIGHT_PATH="<MINIMAX_M3_EAGLE3_GQA_PATH>"
LOG_PATH="./minimax-m3-mxfp8.log"

export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=512
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

vllm serve "${WEIGHT_PATH}" \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 11223 \
  --served-model-name minimax-m3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \

```

**Note**: In the scripts above, `max-num-seqs` limits the number of sequences scheduled in one iteration. Tune this limit using the expected input/output lengths and request concurrency,measure throughput and latency after each change. Increase it only when additional sequences fit in the available KV cache a higher limit does not guarantee higher throughput and can increase latency or KV-cache preemption.

Text requests do not require `--limit-mm-per-prompt`, but omitting this flag does not disable multimodal support or its memory planning. For multimodal deployment, configure the limits according to the actual request shape. For example, use `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":2,"video":0}'` for two-image requests,use `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":1}'` for one-video requests.

### Sub-1M-Token Context Deployment

The following PD examples cover contexts below 1M tokens and use `--max-model-len 133000`. Choose ordinary PD or add a KV cache pool with the same serving topology.

#### Prefill-Decode Disaggregation

 on 950DT it runs on two nodes,the 950DT example below also describes scaling the same 1P1D deployment to three nodes. Here, 1P1D means one Prefill service group and one Decode service group. The Decode group can span two machines while remaining one global DP group.

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. Prefill nodes process large prompt chunks, Decode nodes serve token generation,a proxy forwards requests between them. Use Mooncake for KV cache transfer. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

The launch pattern is: prepare `launch_online_dp.py` and a role-specific `run_dp_template.sh` on each node, Prefill uses `DP=1`, `TP=4`,pipeline parallel (`PP=4`) with a `16,15,15,14` split of the 60 transformer layers, while the 950DT products MXFP8 launch uses `PP=1` with `DP=2` on both roles. Each DP rank occupies `tp_size * pp_size` NPUs.

**Common Issues Tip:** For PD disaggregation issues such as KV transfer timeouts or Mooncake connection errors, refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html). For MiniMax-specific issues, refer to [Chapter 10 FAQ](#10-faq).

Before you start, prepare the script `launch_online_dp.py` on each node:

```python
import argparse
import multiprocessing
import os
import subprocess
import sys

def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dp-size",
        type=int,
        required=True,
        help="Data parallel size."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--tp-size",
        type=int,
        default=1,
        help="Tensor parallel size."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--pp-size",
        type=int,
        default=1,
        help="Pipeline parallel size."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dp-size-local",
        type=int,
        default=-1,
        help="Local data parallel size."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dp-rank-start",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="Starting rank for data parallel."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dp-address",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        help="IP address for data parallel master node."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dp-rpc-port",
        type=str,
        default="12321",
        help="Port for data parallel master node."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--vllm-start-port",
        type=int,
        default=8000,
        help="Starting port for the engine."
    )
    return parser.parse_args()

args = parse_args()
dp_size = args.dp_size
tp_size = args.tp_size
pp_size = args.pp_size
dp_size_local = args.dp_size_local
if dp_size_local == -1:
    dp_size_local = dp_size
dp_rank_start = args.dp_rank_start
dp_address = args.dp_address
dp_rpc_port = args.dp_rpc_port
vllm_start_port = args.vllm_start_port
gpus_per_dp_rank = tp_size * pp_size

def run_command(visible_devices, dp_rank, vllm_engine_port):
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.update(
        VISIBLE_DEVICES=visible_devices,
        SERVICE_PORT=str(vllm_engine_port),
        DP_SIZE=str(dp_size),
        DP_RANK=str(dp_rank),
        DP_ADDRESS=dp_address,
        DP_RPC_PORT=dp_rpc_port,
        TP_SIZE=str(tp_size),
        PP_SIZE=str(pp_size),
    )
    subprocess.run(["bash", "./run_dp_template.sh"], env=env, check=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    template_path = "./run_dp_template.sh"
    if not os.path.exists(template_path):
        print(f"Template file {template_path} does not exist.")
        sys.exit(1)

    processes = []
    for i in range(dp_size_local):
        dp_rank = dp_rank_start + i
        vllm_engine_port = vllm_start_port + i
        visible_devices = ",".join(
            str(x) for x in range(i * gpus_per_dp_rank, (i + 1) * gpus_per_dp_rank)
        )
        process = multiprocessing.Process(
            target=run_command,
            args=(visible_devices, dp_rank, vllm_engine_port),
        )
        processes.append(process)
        process.start()

    for process in processes:
        process.join()
```

The templates use named environment variables instead of positional shell arguments. Replace the `<...>` IP, NIC and weight-path placeholders in each template,export those variables in the shell before launching. The numeric defaults below describe one engine `launch_online_dp.py` overrides the per-rank values when it starts all local engines. You do not need to calculate a different port or device list for every rank. When using the launcher, edit `export DP_SIZE=...`, `export TP_SIZE=...`, `export PP_SIZE=...` and the other values in the node-specific launch block these take precedence over the `${VARIABLE:-default}` values in the template.

| Variable | Meaning | How it is set |
|---|---|---|
| LOCAL_IP | Current node's communication IP | Fill in <CURRENT_NODE_IP> separately on each node. |
| NIC_NAME | NIC associated with LOCAL_IP | Fill in <CURRENT_NODE_NIC>. |
| MODEL_PATH / EAGLE3_WEIGHT_PATH | Target / draft weight directories | Use the same mounted paths on every node. |
| DP_SIZE / TP_SIZE / PP_SIZE | Global DP size / TP and PP size within one rank | Numeric values are exported in each launch command below. |
| LOCAL_DP_SIZE | Number of engines on the current node | Passed to the launcher as --dp-size-local. |
| DP_RANK_START | First global DP rank on this node | Passed as --dp-rank-start; differs between the two Decode nodes. |
| DP_ADDRESS | DP coordinator IP for this role | Prefill's IP for P; the first Decode node's IP for every D node. |
| DP_RPC_PORT | DP coordinator port | All nodes in the same role use the same value. |
| SERVICE_PORT | First local API port in the launch shell | The launcher adds the local rank index for each engine. |
| DP_RANK | Engine's global DP rank | The launcher sets DP_RANK_START + local_rank. |
| VISIBLE_DEVICES | NPU IDs for one engine | The launcher assigns TP_SIZE × PP_SIZE consecutive IDs per local rank. |

An explicit `--data-parallel-rank` enables external DP load balancing, which vLLM requires to have `DP_SIZE > 1`. The templates below build `DP_RANK_ARGS` from the actual `DP_SIZE`: omit the rank argument for DP1,pass the launcher-assigned rank for DP greater than 1. Keep `DP_RANK` available for per-rank connector identifiers and ports, including in DP1.

Save the Prefill template as `run_dp_template.sh` on the P node and the Decode template under that name on each D node. Run the launcher from the directory containing the matching template. If using a shared filesystem, keep P and D templates in separate directories. Changing TP/DP/PP also requires updating the matching `prefill` and `decode` layouts in both roles' `--kv-transfer-config`.

The following values match the configurations in Sections 5.3.1 and 5.3.2. P/D node counts refer to machines `DP_SIZE` is the global number of ranks for that role.

| Section / platform | Role / node | DP_SIZE | TP_SIZE | PP_SIZE | LOCAL_DP_SIZE | DP_RANK_START | First SERVICE_PORT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.3.1 950DT, two nodes | P | 2 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 31050 |
| 5.3.1 950DT, two nodes | D | 2 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 31060 |
| 5.3.1 950DT, three nodes | P | 2 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 31050 |
| 5.3.1 950DT, three nodes | First D | 4 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 31060 |
| 5.3.1 950DT, three nodes | Second D | 4 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 31062 |
| 5.3.2 950DT, two nodes | P | 2 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 31050 |
| 5.3.2 950DT, two nodes | D | 2 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 31060 |

**Scaling to three nodes (still 1P1D)**

Only one template change is required: in **both** the Prefill and Decode `run_dp_template.sh`, update the Mooncake extra config to describe the new Decode group — `"decode":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":4,"pp_size":1}` (Prefill stays `dp_size: 2`). Also set `LOCAL_IP` in each node's template to that node's compute-network IP.

Start the Prefill node exactly as in the two-node example. Then start the first Decode node (`DECODE0_IP`, global DP ranks 0–1), which also acts as the DP group master:

In a contributor-verified text-only run using this three-node layout with MXFP8, EAGLE3, fp8 KV cache and the optional `--language-model-only` flag, all 232 requests succeeded at 128k input / 1k output and concurrency 58. Average TPOT was 27.3 ms and aggregate output throughput was about 1840 tokens/s. In that setup, enabling Decode FlashComm1 increased output throughput from 1807.9 to 1840.7 tokens/s (about 1.8%). These measurements describe that workload and configuration the launch templates leave `--language-model-only` optional.

Key Parameter Descriptions:

**`launch_online_dp.py` parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| --dp-size | int | Yes | - | Data parallel size (total number of DP ranks across all nodes). |
| --tp-size | int | No | 1 | Tensor parallel size within each DP rank. |
| --pp-size | int | No | 1 | Pipeline parallel size within each DP rank. Each rank occupies tp_size * pp_size NPUs. |
| --dp-size-local | int | No | (same as --dp-size) | Number of DP ranks on the current node. |
| --dp-rank-start | int | No | 0 | Starting rank offset for data parallel ranks on this node. |
| --dp-address | str | Yes | - | IP address of the data parallel master node. |
| --dp-rpc-port | str | No | 12321 | RPC port for data parallel master communication. |

**Prefill node-specific configurations:**

`--language-model-only` (optional): For text-only tests, add this flag as needed based on the available KV cache capacity to avoid reserving memory for multimodal processing. This flag can be used together with FLASHCOMM1 for text-only serving.

 for shorter inputs, set it to the input token length.

`--enforce-eager`: Prefill nodes retain eager execution without graph capture.

`--speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3", ...}'`: Enables the `MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA` draft model.

**Decode node-specific configurations:**

`--language-model-only` (optional): For text-only tests, add this flag as needed based on the available KV cache capacity to avoid reserving memory for multimodal processing.

`"max_cudagraph_capture_size"` (optional, omitted by default): Limits the maximum decode batch size covered by ACL graph capture and the graph memory reserved for it the program default is `512`. With EAGLE3 speculative decoding, each request is expanded to `1 + num_speculative_tokens` tokens in one decode step (`4` tokens when `num_speculative_tokens=3`). Since DP distributes requests per rank, the per-rank batch size matters: for example, with `DP2` and `--max-num-seqs 256`, each DP rank handles 128 requests, producing `4 × 128 = 512` tokens per step — exactly at the default limit. If concurrency rises to 257, one DP rank handles 129 requests, giving `4 × 129 = 516 > 512` batches above 512 skip graph capture and fall back to eager execution, lowering decode throughput. In that case set `"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024` in `--compilation-config` (e.g., `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}'`). Because a larger capture size reserves additional NPU memory, the configurations in this tutorial keep the default add this option only when your target concurrency requires it.

`--max-num-seqs 256`: Decode concurrency used by the verified 950DT products 1P1D launch.

**Mooncake KV transfer configuration (`--kv-transfer-config`):**

`"kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV1"`: Uses Mooncake as the KV cache transfer connector between prefill and decode nodes.

`"kv_role": "kv_producer"` / `"kv_consumer"`: `kv_producer` on prefill nodes, `kv_consumer` on decode nodes.

`"kv_port"`: Port for Mooncake KV transfer. Use different ports for prefill and 950DT products `30000`/`26900`.

`"use_ascend_direct": true`: Enables Ascend direct transfer for KV cache.

`"ascend_local_comm_res_path": "/etc/hixlep"` (950DT products only): Used for RoCE-attached 950DT with `/etc/hixlep/` mounted. On SuperPod UB fabric, omit this option and export `ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES='{"version":"1.

`"prefill"` / `"decode"` sections: `dp_size`, `tp_size`,`decode: dp8 tp4 pp1` across two nodes (four local DP ranks per Decode node). 950DT products uses `prefill: dp2 tp4 pp1` and `decode: dp2 tp4 pp1` for two nodes,`decode: dp4 tp4 pp1` for three nodes.

**Request forwarding (proxy):**

Wait until Prefill node and DP ranks prints `Application startup complete` before starting the proxy.

The proxy maps every prefill engine endpoint and every decode engine endpoint to a single entry point on port `8009`.

If requests reach the proxy but no output is returned, check that the proxy host list includes every healthy Prefill node and DP ranks,that all nodes still have free NPU memory after the previous run.

#### PREREQUISITES

Mount the host HCCN config into every container that participates in pooling:

```bash
-v /etc/hccn.conf:/etc/hccn.conf:ro
```

Use a local SSD directory on each Prefill and Decode host to store KV cache data offloaded from the memory pool. `/nvme/mooncake_offload` is an example directory inside the container, not a required SSD mount point or a directory that already exists on every host.

On each host, first identify the local SSD and its mount point:

```bash
lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE,ROTA,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,MODEL
df -hT
```

Use `MODEL` to identify the SSD and `MOUNTPOINTS` to find its mounted filesystem. `ROTA=0` indicates a non-rotational device confirm the storage type with the machine's disk information, especially for RAID or virtual disks. Choose an existing local SSD filesystem with enough free space. A shared network filesystem is not the local SSD tier.

For example, if the SSD is mounted at `/data/nvme`, create the offload directory there before starting the container. Replace `/data/nvme` below with the actual SSD mount point:

```bash
mkdir -p /data/nvme/mooncake_offload
findmnt -T /data/nvme/mooncake_offload
df -hT /data/nvme/mooncake_offload
```

Confirm that `findmnt` reports the selected SSD filesystem and that `df` shows enough available space. Creating a directory named `/nvme` alone does not mount an SSD or ensure that data is stored on one.

Add this bind mount when creating each model container:

```bash
-v /data/nvme/mooncake_offload:/nvme/mooncake_offload
```

The left side is the directory on that host's SSD the right side is the directory visible inside the container. With this mapping, keep `"ssd_offload_path": "/nvme/mooncake_offload"` in `mooncake.json`. If the container path changes, update `ssd_offload_path` to match. Use an absolute path that exists and is writable by the vLLM process do not use a symlink. Repeat this setup on P and every D host: identical path strings refer to separate local SSD storage on each host. The backend creates per-rank subdirectories beneath it. The installed Mooncake package must support the `enable_ssd_offload` and `ssd_offload_path` arguments in `MooncakeDistributedStore.setup()` use the dependencies in the [KV Cache Pool Deployment Guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html).

Place `mooncake.json` next to `run_dp_template.sh` on every node. Use the same reachable Mooncake Master address and `tenant_id` across P and D. `global_segment_size` is allocated per worker rank, not per node a non-zero value must be aligned to `1GB`. ```bash

```bash
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${MOONCAKE_LIB_DIRS}:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"

# SSD I/O buffer per worker: 1GB, aligned for A3 fabric memory.
export MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_LOCAL_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES=1073741824
# SSD disk budget per NPU worker rank: 10 GiB.
export MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_TOTAL_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES=$((10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024))
export MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE=$((10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024))
export MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_EVICTION_POLICY=lru
```

The SSD I/O buffer is allocated separately from `global_segment_size`. The `1GB` value above is an aligned starting point size it for the KV read/write batches and include it in the per-rank memory budget.

For this three-tier (NPU, host memory,SSD) example, the recommended starting SSD budget is **10 GiB per NPU worker rank** on every Prefill and Decode node. The two capacity limits describe the same SSD budget they do not add up to 20 GiB:

`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_TOTAL_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` sets the per-worker SSD capacity reported to Mooncake Master. Its default is `2199023255552` bytes (2 TiB) per worker this is advertised capacity, not an immediate disk allocation.

`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE` sets the local bucket size limit. Its default is `0`, meaning 90% of the physical disk capacity. Set it explicitly alongside the reported capacity.

`MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_EVICTION_POLICY=lru` enables least-recently-used eviction, removing old SSD cache entries to make room for new writes within the configured bucket limit.

 they do not change the host-memory pool or SSD I/O buffer size. For details, see [Mooncake SSD Offload Parameter Tuning](../../user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.html#mooncake-ssd-offload-parameter-tuning).

--dp-size-local "$LOCAL_DP_SIZE" --dp-rank-start "$DP_RANK_START" \
--dp-address "$DP_ADDRESS" --dp-rpc-port "$DP_RPC_PORT" \
--vllm-start-port "$SERVICE_PORT"
` Both Decode nodes expose API ports `31260`–`31263`. Wait for all eight DP ranks to print `Application startup complete`.

export LOCAL_IP="$PREFILL_IP"
export DP_SIZE=1
export TP_SIZE=4
export PP_SIZE=4
export LOCAL_DP_SIZE=1
export DP_RANK_START=0
export DP_ADDRESS="$PREFILL_IP"
export DP_RPC_PORT=6884
export SERVICE_PORT=31050

python launch_online_dp.py \
--dp-size "$DP_SIZE" --tp-size "$TP_SIZE" --pp-size "$PP_SIZE" \

--dp-address "$DP_ADDRESS" --dp-rpc-port "$DP_RPC_PORT" \

 Wait for every Prefill rank to print `Application startup complete`.

export DECODE0_IP="<FIRST_DECODE_NODE_IP>"
export DECODE1_IP="<SECOND_DECODE_NODE_IP>"

unset http_proxy https_proxy ftp_proxy all_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY FTP_PROXY ALL_PROXY

python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
--port 8009 \
--host $PREFILL_IP \
--prefiller-hosts \
$PREFILL_IP \

31050 \

$DECODE0_IP $DECODE0_IP $DECODE0_IP $DECODE0_IP \
$DECODE1_IP $DECODE1_IP $DECODE1_IP $DECODE1_IP \
--decoder-ports \
31260 31261 31262 31263 31260 31261 31262 31263
 The service is accessible at `<proxy_ip>:8009` use this endpoint in [Section 7](#7-functional-verification).

#### VERIFICATION

 for 950DT, confirm P and D both load `"64GB"`. Check worker logs for successful segment registration.

 950DT has four (two P plus two D).

Send requests only to the proxy on port `8009`.

Warm up with a repeated-prefix request, then send again and check Prefill logs for KV Pool lookup/get/put and hit information.

Confirm Decode logs still show a normal Mooncake P→D KV transfer.

Confirm SSD storage initializes under `ssd_offload_path` for each contributing worker. Use a working set larger than the memory pool to verify SSD offload and subsequent reads a memory-pool hit alone does not exercise the SSD tier.

### Multimodal and ViT DP (Optional)

MiniMax-M3 supports image and video inputs on Ascend. The deployment examples above keep `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}'` as the default multimodal capacity assumption because the other serving parameters are tuned for the single-image path.

MiniMax-M3 image and video inputs share the same Vision Tower. If a service only needs one modality, explicitly set the unused modality to `0` for example, use `{"image":1,"video":0}` for image-only serving and `{"image":0,"video":1}` for video-only serving. As long as either image or video remains enabled, the shared Vision Tower is retained. Setting an unused modality to `0` is clearer than omitting it, because omitted modalities may still participate in multimodal capacity and profiling planning.

For the ViT / multimodal encoder part, data parallel execution is supported and can be enabled with:

```bash
--mm-encoder-tp-mode data
```

This option is not enabled in the default deployment examples because it can increase per-card memory usage. When enabling ViT DP, re-evaluate memory-related parameters such as `--max-model-len`, `--max-num-seqs`,`--gpu-memory-utilization` for the target workload.

For video or mixed image-video requests, adjust the multimodal limit according to the actual request shape instead of changing the default template blindly:

```bash
# one video
--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":1}'

# one image and one video
--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":1}'
```

When using local media paths in requests, such as `file:///path/to/video.mp4`, add an explicit allowlist path:

```bash
--allowed-local-media-path /
```

If the number of sampled video frames is not specified, vLLM uses its default video sampling policy, which samples 32 frames by default. For quick functional smoke tests, a smaller frame count such as 8 or 16 can be set in the request or evaluation config. For benchmark runs, follow the dataset protocol.

 Enable FLASHCOMM1 through `additional_config.enable_flashcomm1`. The `--language-model-only` flag is optional and must be omitted for multimodal inputs.

```bash
# Enable FLASHCOMM1.
--additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'

# Enable language-model-only mode.
--language-model-only
```

## Verification

### Text

```bash
curl http://{ip}:{port}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @- <<EOF
{
  "model": "minimax-m3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Answer the following multiple choice question. The last line of your response should be of the following format: 'Answer: LETTER' (without quotes) where LETTER is one of ABCD. Think step by step before answering.\n\nA student regrets that he fell asleep during a lecture in electrochemistry, facing the following incomplete statement in a test:\nThermodynamically, oxygen is a …oxidant in basic solutions. Kinetically, oxygen reacts …in acidic solutions.\nWhich combination of weaker/stronger and faster/slower is correct?\n\nA) weaker —faster\nB) stronger —faster\nC) weaker - slower\nD) stronger —slower"
    }
  ],
  "max_tokens": 8000,
  "temperature": 1.0
}
EOF
```

Expected result: the answer is C.

### Single Image

Start the service with image input enabled, for example `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}'`. Replace `${IMAGE_PATH}` with a local image path on the client side.

```bash
IMAGE_PATH=/path/to/image.jpg
IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 -w 0 "${IMAGE_PATH}")"

curl http://{ip}:{port}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @- <<EOF
{
  "model": "minimax-m3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,${IMAGE_BASE64}"}},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Briefly describe this image."}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0
}
EOF
```

Expected result: HTTP 200 response with a JSON body containing non-empty `choices` and generated text describing the image.

### Single Video

Start the service with video input enabled, for example `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":1}'`. If the request uses `file://` local video paths, also add `--allowed-local-media-path /` or a narrower allowed directory. If `media_io_kwargs.video.num_frames` is not specified, vLLM samples 32 frames by default.

```bash
curl http://{ip}:{port}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "minimax-m3",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {
            "type": "video_url",
            "video_url": {
              "url": "file:///path/to/video.mp4"
            }
          },
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Briefly describe the main content of this video."
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "max_tokens": 512,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: HTTP 200 response with a JSON body containing non-empty `choices` and generated text describing the video content.

### Mixed Image and Video Request

Start the service with both image and video input enabled. For the following request, use `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":1}'`. If the request uses `file://` local video paths, also add `--allowed-local-media-path /` or a narrower allowed directory.

```bash
IMAGE_BASE64="$(base64 -w 0 /path/to/image.jpg)"

curl http://{ip}:{port}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @- <<EOF
{
  "model": "minimax-m3",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,${IMAGE_BASE64}"}},
        {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "file:///path/to/video.mp4"}},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the image and video separately, and explain whether they are related."}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0
}
EOF
```

Expected result: HTTP 200 response with a JSON body containing non-empty `choices` and generated text that describes the image and video separately and explains whether they are related.
