## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | KV Cache Selection | Download Links |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (BF16 version) | 2 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) nodes or | auto for the baseline | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp (quantized version) | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) node or | Follow the checkpoint KV quantization recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp (quantized version) | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) node or | Follow the checkpoint KV quantization recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | Check KV metadata; the model name alone is insufficient | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a4-mxfp4 (quantized version) |  | Check KV metadata; the model name alone is insufficient | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | mxfp8 for the supported C8 recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3. |  |  |  |

Note

`--quantization ascend` selects the Ascend model quantization implementation `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` selects MXFP8 KV cache storage. They configure different parts of inference. Enable `mxfp8` only with a supported checkpoint and its required KV scale metadata. A W4A8/W8A8 name,an MXFP weight format, does not by itself establish C8 KV cache compatibility. Do not copy a W4A8C8 or W8A8C8 KV setting to a different checkpoint without checking its quantization description and serving logs. Keep the weight revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata,KV cache settings consistent on P and D.

It is recommended to download the model weights to a shared directory across multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`, so that all serving nodes can load the same path.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication

For multi-node deployment, verify inter-node connectivity by following [Verify Multi-node Communication](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

Use mutually reachable service IPs on all nodes. In the scripts below, `local_ip` must belong to `nic_name`.

## Installation

Select an image for your hardware and start a container on each node. Refer to [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image) for details.

For PD deployment, use the same vLLM-Ascend release image and dependency versions on P and D.

Run the following commands as root on the **host** before starting the container. Do not run them inside the serving container: the container mounts `/sys` and `/proc/sys` read-only, so the CPU governor write fails and `sysctl` is silently ignored (it still returns 0), which makes the tuning appear to succeed without taking effect.

```bash
# Host CPU governor and kernel tuning (run on the host, not in the container).
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
```

Start a Docker container on each node.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a3
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
  --name $NAME \
  --net=host \
  --shm-size=64g \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 \
  --device /dev/davinci0 \
  --device /dev/davinci1 \
  --device /dev/davinci2 \
  --device /dev/davinci3 \
  --device /dev/davinci4 \
  --device /dev/davinci5 \
  --device /dev/davinci6 \
  --device /dev/davinci7 \
  --device /dev/davinci8 \
  --device /dev/davinci9 \
  --device /dev/davinci10 \
  --device /dev/davinci11 \
  --device /dev/davinci12 \
  --device /dev/davinci13 \
  --device /dev/davinci14 \
  --device /dev/davinci15 \
  --device /dev/davinci_manager \
  --device /dev/devmm_svm \
  --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
  -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
  -it $IMAGE bash
```

Note

`--shm-size=64g` is recommended for the documented 397B long-context deployment recipes. Use both sufficient shared memory and an unlimited memlock setting: a 1g shared memory or the default 64 MB locked-memory limit is too small,worker startup and memory profiling can fail with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` / `aclrtMallocHostWithCfg error 207001` (host memory allocation failure) and HCCL link setup can time out. If the container runtime does not permit `--ulimit memlock=-1`, configure the host/runtime policy or grant the minimum required capability. Increasing `--shm-size` alone does not remove the memlock limit.

The CPU governor and `sysctl` tuning commands must run on the host before starting the container see the host preparation block at the top of this section. Do not run them inside the serving container, where `/sys` and `/proc/sys` are read-only.

After entering the actual serving container on each node, check the executables, versions,imported paths:

```shell
command -v python3 vllm
python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.metadata as metadata
import sys

import torch_npu
import vllm
import vllm_ascend

print("Python:", sys.executable)
for module in (vllm, vllm_ascend, torch_npu):
    print(module.__name__, module.__file__)
for package in (
    "vllm", "vllm-ascend", "torch", "torch-npu", "triton-ascend",
    "mooncake-transfer-engine-npu", "mooncake-transfer-engine",
):
    try:
        print(package, metadata.version(package))
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        print(package, "not installed under this distribution name")
PY
```

If you want to deploy a multi-node service, set up the same environment on each node.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs both Prefill and Decode on the same node. It is suitable for functional validation and long-context serving.

Run the following script for online inference with a 133k context on one Atlas 800I A3 node (64 GB x 16). W8A8 deployment requires `--quantization ascend`.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download.
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
MODEL_PATH="Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp"
vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 133000 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "enforce_eager": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 1, "enable_flashcomm1": true}'
```

Common Issues Tip: If the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient,requests are not scheduled as expected, refer to [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) first,then check the model-specific FAQ in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Key parameters:**

`--data-parallel-size 1` uses one DP group. `--tensor-parallel-size` is 16 for the A3 example and

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--max-model-len` is the maximum input plus output length for a single request. Increase it only when enough KV cache is available.

`--max-num-seqs` is the maximum number of active requests scheduled by each DP group. For performance tests, set `--max-num-seqs * --data-parallel-size` greater than or equal to the test concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--gpu-memory-utilization` controls how much HBM vLLM can use to calculate KV cache capacity. A higher value increases KV cache size but can trigger OOM if runtime memory is higher than the profile run.

`--enable-prefix-caching` enables prefix caching. For Qwen3.5, short prefixes may not be cached when the hybrid KV cache manager adjusts the block size to a large value.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the quantized weights used above. Remove this option when deploying the BF16 model.

`--speculative-config` enables Qwen3.5 MTP speculative decoding. Reduce `num_speculative_tokens` or remove this option if the workload is sensitive to first-token latency or if MTP is unstable in your environment.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full decode ACLGraph replay to reduce dispatch overhead.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 for the single-node examples above.

`--additional-config` configures Ascend-specific optimizations: `enable_cpu_binding=true` enables Ascend-native CPU binding `enable_fused_mc2=1` selects dispatch-FFN-combine and A3 examples for compatibility with the documented MTP and batching configurations `2` selects CANN MegaMoe and should only be enabled with a matching CANN/operator stack and supported token-shape limits `0` disables the fused path. `enable_flashcomm1=true` enables MoE sequence parallelism across TP ranks and requires `--enable-expert-parallel` with a TP size greater than 1.

### Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (A3)

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. This performance-oriented example deploys 1P1D on one 16-NPU Atlas 800I A3 host with the `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp` checkpoint. In this section, 1P1D describes two service groups it does not mean that P and D must occupy separate hosts.

The 16 NPUs are divided into two non-overlapping device sets:

| Service group | Physical devices | TP | DP | EP world size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 0-7 | 8 | 1 | 8 |
| Decode | 8-15 | 4 | 2 | 8 |

Prefill and Decode use the same service NIC and IP because they run on the same host, but they use different HTTP and Mooncake ports. The Decode launcher creates two local DP engines, each with TP4. Do not start a second copy of the Decode command.

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

**Key parameters for PD disaggregation:**

Prefill uses TP8/DP1 on devices 0-7. Decode uses TP4/DP2 on devices 8-15. With expert parallelism enabled, both service groups have an EP world size of 8.

The P and D device lists must not overlap. P and D can share the same service IP on a single host, but their HTTP and Mooncake ports must be different.

The Decode command starts both local DP ranks. Do not launch one Decode command per DP rank.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 on both service groups.

Use the same MTP method and `num_speculative_tokens` on P and D. To disable MTP for a comparison, remove `--speculative-config` from both commands.

`kv_connector_extra_config.prefill` must remain DP1/TP8,`decode` must remain DP2/TP4 for this topology.

`enable_flashcomm1=true`, `enable_fused_mc2=2`,`enable_shared_expert_dp=true` reproduce the performance-case MoE configuration. They require the matching CANN operators and software stack.

Prefill runs eagerly. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, enables NPU graph extensions,enables the recompute scheduler.

`--max-num-batched-tokens 300` and `--max-num-seqs 100` are Decode scheduler limits applied to each DP engine by vLLM.

Prefix caching and asynchronous scheduling are enabled on both service groups in this validated case. Revalidate output correctness if either setting or the connector version changes.

| Node role | NPUs | TP | DP | EP world size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 8 | 8 | 1 | 8 |
| Decode | 8 | 4 | 2 | 8 |

Both nodes must use the same checkpoint revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata,`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. This example uses `MooncakeConnectorV2`: the proxy calls Prefill first,Decode pulls the KV cache. The connector topology must remain DP1/TP8 for Prefill and DP2/TP4 for Decode.

Use a high-speed service network that is reachable in both directions. On each host, `local_ip` must be the IP assigned to `nic_name`. Do not reuse another host's endpoint resources.

    "scheduler_config": {
      "recompute_scheduler_enable": true
    }
  }' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2",
    "kv_buffer_device": "npu",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_port": "56010",
    "engine_id": "2",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "ascend_local_comm_res_path": "/etc/hixlep",
      "prefill": {
        "dp_size": 1,
        "tp_size": 8
      },
      "decode": {
        "dp_size": 2,
        "tp_size": 4
      }
    }
  }'
```

Run the Decode script on the Decode node:

```shell
bash run_d.sh
```

If the Decode service starts successfully, information similar to the following example is displayed:

```text
INFO:     Started server process [44611]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Common Issues Tip: If Decode fails to initialize, confirm that `--data-parallel-size 2`, `--data-parallel-size-local 2`, `--tensor-parallel-size 4`,the Mooncake topology describe the same DP2/TP4 layout. Verify ports 30050, 6884,56010,confirm that both local DP engines start.

#### Proxy

After both services report ready, start the standard Pull proxy on the Prefill host. Use the same reachable service IPs assigned to `local_ip` in the P and D commands. The Decode backend is the HTTP port `30050`, not the DP RPC port `6884`.

Run the command from the directory containing `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py` (for example, `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/` in the matching vLLM-Ascend revision):

```shell
unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

PREFILL_HOST="<P_HIGH_SPEED_SERVICE_IP>"
DECODE_HOST="<D_HIGH_SPEED_SERVICE_IP>"

python3 load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
  --prefiller-hosts "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --prefiller-ports 30060 \
  --decoder-hosts "${DECODE_HOST}" \
  --decoder-ports 30050 \
  --host "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --port 8000
```

Send client requests to `http://<P_HIGH_SPEED_SERVICE_IP>:8000`. Before testing generation, check the P endpoint, D endpoint,proxy health as described in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

#### C8 Accuracy and Compatibility Requirements

C8 KV cache is part of this performance recipe, not just a model-name convention. Keep the following conditions together:

Use the same compatible W4A8C8 checkpoint revision, tokenizer, chat template, quantization metadata,`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` on P and D.

Use a v0.30.0 MRv1 build containing [the MXFP8 KV-scale fix #19017](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19017), merged into `releases/v0.30.0` as `14c6c3f43`,a build with an equivalent verified fix.

Keep `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, the P DP1/TP8 and D DP2/TP4 topology,the connector topology consistent.

Keep MTP settings identical on P and D. To run an MTP-off comparison, remove `--speculative-config` from both commands.

Prefix caching and asynchronous scheduling are enabled on both nodes for this performance case.

Prefill uses eager execution. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and enables NPU graph extensions.

`enable_fused_mc2=0` and `enable_prefill_mc2=false` reproduce this performance case. Do not infer the active setting from a profiling directory name.

`enable_shared_expert_dp=true` and `enable_flashcomm1=true` require expert parallelism and the matching CANN/software stack.

The D HTTP endpoint fronts both local DP engines. Do not use the DP RPC port as a Decode endpoint.

Use the standard Pull proxy with Prefill port 30060 and Decode port 30050. Start with short non-streaming requests, then verify request churn and the full accuracy baseline before performance testing. HTTP success or Mooncake transfer completion alone does not prove that C8 scale contents are correct. Check predictions for empty output, repeated punctuation, incoherent text,abnormal repetition evaluate MTP acceptance together with actual output correctness.

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. Prefill nodes process large prompt chunks, Decode nodes serve token generation,a proxy forwards requests between them. These examples demonstrate how to tune prefill and decode resource ratios.

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

Deploy `run_p.sh` and `run_d.sh` on the corresponding nodes,deploy a proxy script on the prefill master node to forward requests.

#### Prefill Node

Create `run_p.sh` on the prefill node.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30000

# nic_name is the network interface name corresponding to local_ip.
nic_name="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
local_ip="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>"
export IP_ADDRESS="${local_ip}"
export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_IF_IP="${local_ip}"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1"

vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp \
  --host "${local_ip}" \
  --port "$2" \
  --data-parallel-size "$3" \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --allowed-local-media-path / \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":false,"enable_static_kernel":false}, "weight_nz_mode":1, "enable_shared_expert_dp":true,"scheduler_config":{"recompute_scheduler_enable":false}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_port":"55220","engine_id":"0","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8},"decode":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8}}}'
```

#### Decode Node

Create `run_d.sh` on the decode node.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30000

# nic_name is the network interface name corresponding to local_ip.
nic_name="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
local_ip="<DECODE_NODE_IP>"
export IP_ADDRESS="${local_ip}"
export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_IF_IP="${local_ip}"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1
export VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1"

vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp \
  --host "${local_ip}" \
  --port "$2" \
  --data-parallel-size "$3" \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-rank "$4" \
  --data-parallel-address "$5" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \
  --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 300 \
  --max-num-seqs 200 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --allowed-local-media-path / \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":false}, "weight_nz_mode":1, "enable_shared_expert_dp":false, "scheduler_config":{"recompute_scheduler_enable":true}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":"56010","engine_id":"2","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8},"decode":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8}}}'
```

Common Issues Tip: If the decode node fails to initialize, check that `--tensor-parallel-size` is 8, `--data-parallel-size-local` matches the global decode DP size (1),`kv_connector_extra_config.decode.dp_size` matches the global decode DP size.

**Key parameters for PD disaggregation:**

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 on both nodes.

`--distributed-executor-backend mp` uses multiprocessing on each node for the local workers.

Prefill uses `--data-parallel-size 1` and `--tensor-parallel-size 8`. This creates 1 DP group with TP8.

Decode uses `--data-parallel-size 1` and `--tensor-parallel-size 8`. This creates 1 DP group with TP8.

`--data-parallel-address` and `--data-parallel-rpc-port` define the DP control plane.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is larger on the prefill node and smaller on the decode node because prefill is prompt-token intensive while decode is latency sensitive.

`scheduler_config.recompute_scheduler_enable` sends requests back to the prefill side to recompute KV cache when decode KV cache is insufficient. Enable it only on the decode node in PD mode.

`--kv-transfer-config` sets the Mooncake connector. `kv_role` is `kv_producer` on prefill and `kv_consumer` on decode.

`kv_connector_extra_config.prefill.dp_size/tp_size` and `decode.dp_size/tp_size` must match the actual global DP and TP layout.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` is recommended on the decode node to reduce decode dispatch overhead.

Run the two scripts on their respective hosts after filling in each host's NIC and IP. The examples use seven argument positions: visible devices, HTTP port, global DP size, DP rank, DP master address, DP RPC port,TP size. P reads only positions 1–3 and 7 positions 4–6 are unused and retained for invocation compatibility. D uses all seven positions its argument 5 is the D host's service IP. Use DP1/TP8 to match the fixed KV topology changing topology also requires updating the connector JSON and device allocation.

Prefill uses the self-contained DP1 mode and therefore does not set the DP address or RPC port. Decode explicitly sets `--data-parallel-rank`, so the launcher also supplies its DP control-plane address and RPC port. In this DP1/rank0 example, the Decode address points to the Decode host itself. The Prefill and Decode services are separate vLLM instances and do not share a DP group. Do not mistake the DP RPC port for the HTTP port the proxy always uses the HTTP ports (argument 2), never the DP RPC port.

```shell
# On P:
bash run_p.sh 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 30060 1 0 "<P_SERVICE_IP>" 6884 8
# On D:
bash run_d.sh 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 30050 1 0 "<D_SERVICE_IP>" 6884 8
```

#### Proxy

After both services report ready, start the standard Pull proxy on the Prefill host. Use the same service IPs configured as `local_ip` in the two scripts and the HTTP ports passed as argument 2.

Run the command from the directory containing `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`:

```shell
unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

PREFILL_HOST="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>"
DECODE_HOST="<DECODE_NODE_IP>"

python3 load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
  --prefiller-hosts "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --prefiller-ports 30060 \
  --decoder-hosts "${DECODE_HOST}" \
  --decoder-ports 30050 \
  --host "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --port 8000
```

Send client requests to `http://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:8000`. Use the Decode HTTP port `30050`, not the DP RPC port `6884`.

### Request Forwarding

Use the proxy paired with the actual connector, rather than choosing it by hardware name. The standard proxy script is in `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/` run the command from that directory. Replace the example hosts with reachable service IPs and use each service's HTTP port. P, D,the client must use the same `--served-model-name`.

| Connector | Request Order | Proxy | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| MooncakeConnectorV1 | Proxy calls P, then D; D pulls KV | load_balance_proxy_server_example.6 |  |
| MooncakeConnectorV2 | Proxy calls P, then D; D pulls KV | load_balance_proxy_server_example. |  |

Equal TP sizes do not make these connectors interchangeable. For unequal TP, verify the direction, divisibility, replicated KV heads, hybrid state layout,quantization support of the selected implementation. The TP8-to-TP4 example does not imply arbitrary TP ratios or reverse-direction support. Use scripts from the same vLLM-Ascend revision as the serving stack.

Use the complete proxy command for the selected deployment:

[A3 single-host 1P1D](#543-proxy): P and D use the same service IP and different HTTP ports.

 the D backend is HTTP port `30050`.

Do not use a DP RPC port or Mooncake KV-transfer port as a proxy backend. If requests reach the proxy but return no output, verify the P and D `/health` endpoints from the proxy host, confirm that the configured backend addresses exactly match each service's `--host` and HTTP port,then run the end-to-end checks in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

## Verification

Wait for both P and D to report ready, verify each HTTP service, then start the matching proxy. For single-node and MP deployment, use the API endpoint on node 0. For PD disaggregation, send generation requests through the proxy so that the test covers KV transfer.

```shell
curl -f "http://<prefill_ip>:<prefill_http_port>/health"
curl -f "http://<decode_ip>:<decode_http_port>/health"
curl -f "http://<proxy_ip>:<proxy_port>/healthcheck"
curl -f "http://<prefill_ip>:<prefill_http_port>/v1/models"
```

Check that the advertised model name matches the request. A health check only establishes HTTP readiness it does not verify the PD data path. Send several short requests, followed by concurrent requests that complete and reuse cache slots,inspect P, D,proxy logs.

```shell
curl "http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "prompt": "The future of AI is",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the HTTP status is 200 and the JSON response contains nonempty, coherent generated text in `choices`. Also verify a chat request with the checkpoint's chat template a short completion request alone is not an accuracy test. Check for transfer errors, empty results, repeated punctuation,abnormal repetition before running a full benchmark. Start with non-streaming requests, then repeat with streaming to test the proxy's chunked-response path.

### Function Calling

To enable tool calling, append the following options to the `vllm serve` command. For PD deployment, add them to both the Prefill and Decode commands and restart both services.

```text
--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

`--enable-auto-tool-choice` allows the model to select a tool, `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` parses tool calls,`--reasoning-parser qwen3` separates reasoning from the final answer.

Send a chat request with a tool definition to the service endpoint. For PD deployment, use the proxy endpoint.

```shell
curl "http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Use get_weather to check the current weather in Beijing."}
    ],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "max_tokens": 2048,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

When the model selects the tool, check that `choices[0].message.tool_calls` contains the function name `get_weather` and a JSON argument string with `city` set to `Beijing`. The client must execute the function, then send the assistant tool-call message and a `role: "tool"` result message with the matching `tool_call_id` in the next request to obtain the final answer. The serving process parses tool calls it does not execute the function.

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | KV Cache Selection | Download Links |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (BF16 version) | 2 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) nodes or | auto for the baseline | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp (quantized version) | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) node or | Follow the checkpoint KV quantization recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp (quantized version) | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) node or | Follow the checkpoint KV quantization recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | Check KV metadata; the model name alone is insufficient | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a4-mxfp4 (quantized version) |  | Check KV metadata; the model name alone is insufficient | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | mxfp8 for the supported C8 recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3. |  |  |  |

Note

`--quantization ascend` selects the Ascend model quantization implementation `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` selects MXFP8 KV cache storage. They configure different parts of inference. Enable `mxfp8` only with a supported checkpoint and its required KV scale metadata. A W4A8/W8A8 name,an MXFP weight format, does not by itself establish C8 KV cache compatibility. Do not copy a W4A8C8 or W8A8C8 KV setting to a different checkpoint without checking its quantization description and serving logs. Keep the weight revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata,KV cache settings consistent on P and D.

It is recommended to download the model weights to a shared directory across multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`, so that all serving nodes can load the same path.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication

For multi-node deployment, verify inter-node connectivity by following [Verify Multi-node Communication](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

Use mutually reachable service IPs on all nodes. In the scripts below, `local_ip` must belong to `nic_name`.

## Installation

Select an image for your hardware and start a container on each node. Refer to [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image) for details.

For PD deployment, use the same vLLM-Ascend release image and dependency versions on P and D.

Run the following commands as root on the **host** before starting the container. Do not run them inside the serving container: the container mounts `/sys` and `/proc/sys` read-only, so the CPU governor write fails and `sysctl` is silently ignored (it still returns 0), which makes the tuning appear to succeed without taking effect.

```bash
# Host CPU governor and kernel tuning (run on the host, not in the container).
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
```

Start a Docker container on each node.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-a3
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
  --name $NAME \
  --net=host \
  --shm-size=64g \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 \
  --device /dev/davinci0 \
  --device /dev/davinci1 \
  --device /dev/davinci2 \
  --device /dev/davinci3 \
  --device /dev/davinci4 \
  --device /dev/davinci5 \
  --device /dev/davinci6 \
  --device /dev/davinci7 \
  --device /dev/davinci8 \
  --device /dev/davinci9 \
  --device /dev/davinci10 \
  --device /dev/davinci11 \
  --device /dev/davinci12 \
  --device /dev/davinci13 \
  --device /dev/davinci14 \
  --device /dev/davinci15 \
  --device /dev/davinci_manager \
  --device /dev/devmm_svm \
  --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
  -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
  -it $IMAGE bash
```

Note

`--shm-size=64g` is recommended for the documented 397B long-context deployment recipes. Use both sufficient shared memory and an unlimited memlock setting: a 1g shared memory or the default 64 MB locked-memory limit is too small,worker startup and memory profiling can fail with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` / `aclrtMallocHostWithCfg error 207001` (host memory allocation failure) and HCCL link setup can time out. If the container runtime does not permit `--ulimit memlock=-1`, configure the host/runtime policy or grant the minimum required capability. Increasing `--shm-size` alone does not remove the memlock limit.

The CPU governor and `sysctl` tuning commands must run on the host before starting the container see the host preparation block at the top of this section. Do not run them inside the serving container, where `/sys` and `/proc/sys` are read-only.

After entering the actual serving container on each node, check the executables, versions,imported paths:

```shell
command -v python3 vllm
python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.metadata as metadata
import sys

import torch_npu
import vllm
import vllm_ascend

print("Python:", sys.executable)
for module in (vllm, vllm_ascend, torch_npu):
    print(module.__name__, module.__file__)
for package in (
    "vllm", "vllm-ascend", "torch", "torch-npu", "triton-ascend",
    "mooncake-transfer-engine-npu", "mooncake-transfer-engine",
):
    try:
        print(package, metadata.version(package))
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        print(package, "not installed under this distribution name")
PY
```

If you want to deploy a multi-node service, set up the same environment on each node.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs both Prefill and Decode on the same node. It is suitable for functional validation and long-context serving.

Run the following script for online inference with a 133k context on one Atlas 800I A3 node (64 GB x 16). W8A8 deployment requires `--quantization ascend`.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download.
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
MODEL_PATH="Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp"
vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 133000 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "enforce_eager": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 1, "enable_flashcomm1": true}'
```

Common Issues Tip: If the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient,requests are not scheduled as expected, refer to [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) first,then check the model-specific FAQ in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Key parameters:**

`--data-parallel-size 1` uses one DP group. `--tensor-parallel-size` is 16 for the A3 example and

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--max-model-len` is the maximum input plus output length for a single request. Increase it only when enough KV cache is available.

`--max-num-seqs` is the maximum number of active requests scheduled by each DP group. For performance tests, set `--max-num-seqs * --data-parallel-size` greater than or equal to the test concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--gpu-memory-utilization` controls how much HBM vLLM can use to calculate KV cache capacity. A higher value increases KV cache size but can trigger OOM if runtime memory is higher than the profile run.

`--enable-prefix-caching` enables prefix caching. For Qwen3.5, short prefixes may not be cached when the hybrid KV cache manager adjusts the block size to a large value.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the quantized weights used above. Remove this option when deploying the BF16 model.

`--speculative-config` enables Qwen3.5 MTP speculative decoding. Reduce `num_speculative_tokens` or remove this option if the workload is sensitive to first-token latency or if MTP is unstable in your environment.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full decode ACLGraph replay to reduce dispatch overhead.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 for the single-node examples above.

`--additional-config` configures Ascend-specific optimizations: `enable_cpu_binding=true` enables Ascend-native CPU binding `enable_fused_mc2=1` selects dispatch-FFN-combine and A3 examples for compatibility with the documented MTP and batching configurations `2` selects CANN MegaMoe and should only be enabled with a matching CANN/operator stack and supported token-shape limits `0` disables the fused path. `enable_flashcomm1=true` enables MoE sequence parallelism across TP ranks and requires `--enable-expert-parallel` with a TP size greater than 1.

### Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (A3)

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. This performance-oriented example deploys 1P1D on one 16-NPU Atlas 800I A3 host with the `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp` checkpoint. In this section, 1P1D describes two service groups it does not mean that P and D must occupy separate hosts.

The 16 NPUs are divided into two non-overlapping device sets:

| Service group | Physical devices | TP | DP | EP world size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 0-7 | 8 | 1 | 8 |
| Decode | 8-15 | 4 | 2 | 8 |

Prefill and Decode use the same service NIC and IP because they run on the same host, but they use different HTTP and Mooncake ports. The Decode launcher creates two local DP engines, each with TP4. Do not start a second copy of the Decode command.

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

**Key parameters for PD disaggregation:**

Prefill uses TP8/DP1 on devices 0-7. Decode uses TP4/DP2 on devices 8-15. With expert parallelism enabled, both service groups have an EP world size of 8.

The P and D device lists must not overlap. P and D can share the same service IP on a single host, but their HTTP and Mooncake ports must be different.

The Decode command starts both local DP ranks. Do not launch one Decode command per DP rank.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 on both service groups.

Use the same MTP method and `num_speculative_tokens` on P and D. To disable MTP for a comparison, remove `--speculative-config` from both commands.

`kv_connector_extra_config.prefill` must remain DP1/TP8,`decode` must remain DP2/TP4 for this topology.

`enable_flashcomm1=true`, `enable_fused_mc2=2`,`enable_shared_expert_dp=true` reproduce the performance-case MoE configuration. They require the matching CANN operators and software stack.

Prefill runs eagerly. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, enables NPU graph extensions,enables the recompute scheduler.

`--max-num-batched-tokens 300` and `--max-num-seqs 100` are Decode scheduler limits applied to each DP engine by vLLM.

Prefix caching and asynchronous scheduling are enabled on both service groups in this validated case. Revalidate output correctness if either setting or the connector version changes.

| Node role | NPUs | TP | DP | EP world size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 8 | 8 | 1 | 8 |
| Decode | 8 | 4 | 2 | 8 |

Both nodes must use the same checkpoint revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata,`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. This example uses `MooncakeConnectorV2`: the proxy calls Prefill first,Decode pulls the KV cache. The connector topology must remain DP1/TP8 for Prefill and DP2/TP4 for Decode.

Use a high-speed service network that is reachable in both directions. On each host, `local_ip` must be the IP assigned to `nic_name`. Do not reuse another host's endpoint resources.

Common Issues Tip: If Decode fails to initialize, confirm that `--data-parallel-size 2`, `--data-parallel-size-local 2`, `--tensor-parallel-size 4`,the Mooncake topology describe the same DP2/TP4 layout. Verify ports 30050, 6884,56010,confirm that both local DP engines start.

#### Proxy

After both services report ready, start the standard Pull proxy on the Prefill host. Use the same reachable service IPs assigned to `local_ip` in the P and D commands. The Decode backend is the HTTP port `30050`, not the DP RPC port `6884`.

Run the command from the directory containing `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py` (for example, `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/` in the matching vLLM-Ascend revision):

```shell
unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

PREFILL_HOST="<P_HIGH_SPEED_SERVICE_IP>"
DECODE_HOST="<D_HIGH_SPEED_SERVICE_IP>"

python3 load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
  --prefiller-hosts "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --prefiller-ports 30060 \
  --decoder-hosts "${DECODE_HOST}" \
  --decoder-ports 30050 \
  --host "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --port 8000
```

Send client requests to `http://<P_HIGH_SPEED_SERVICE_IP>:8000`. Before testing generation, check the P endpoint, D endpoint,proxy health as described in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

#### C8 Accuracy and Compatibility Requirements

C8 KV cache is part of this performance recipe, not just a model-name convention. Keep the following conditions together:

Use the same compatible W4A8C8 checkpoint revision, tokenizer, chat template, quantization metadata,`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` on P and D.

Use a v0.30.0 MRv1 build containing [the MXFP8 KV-scale fix #19017](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19017), merged into `releases/v0.30.0` as `14c6c3f43`,a build with an equivalent verified fix.

Keep `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, the P DP1/TP8 and D DP2/TP4 topology,the connector topology consistent.

Keep MTP settings identical on P and D. To run an MTP-off comparison, remove `--speculative-config` from both commands.

Prefix caching and asynchronous scheduling are enabled on both nodes for this performance case.

Prefill uses eager execution. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and enables NPU graph extensions.

`enable_fused_mc2=0` and `enable_prefill_mc2=false` reproduce this performance case. Do not infer the active setting from a profiling directory name.

`enable_shared_expert_dp=true` and `enable_flashcomm1=true` require expert parallelism and the matching CANN/software stack.

The D HTTP endpoint fronts both local DP engines. Do not use the DP RPC port as a Decode endpoint.

Use the standard Pull proxy with Prefill port 30060 and Decode port 30050. Start with short non-streaming requests, then verify request churn and the full accuracy baseline before performance testing. HTTP success or Mooncake transfer completion alone does not prove that C8 scale contents are correct. Check predictions for empty output, repeated punctuation, incoherent text,abnormal repetition evaluate MTP acceptance together with actual output correctness.

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. Prefill nodes process large prompt chunks, Decode nodes serve token generation,a proxy forwards requests between them. These examples demonstrate how to tune prefill and decode resource ratios.

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

Deploy `run_p.sh` and `run_d.sh` on the corresponding nodes,deploy a proxy script on the prefill master node to forward requests.

#### Prefill Node

Create `run_p.sh` on the prefill node.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30000

# nic_name is the network interface name corresponding to local_ip.
nic_name="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
local_ip="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>"
export IP_ADDRESS="${local_ip}"
export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_IF_IP="${local_ip}"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1"

vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp \
  --host "${local_ip}" \
  --port "$2" \
  --data-parallel-size "$3" \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --allowed-local-media-path / \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":false,"enable_static_kernel":false}, "weight_nz_mode":1, "enable_shared_expert_dp":true,"scheduler_config":{"recompute_scheduler_enable":false}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_port":"55220","engine_id":"0","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8},"decode":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8}}}'
```

#### Decode Node

Create `run_d.sh` on the decode node.

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30000

# nic_name is the network interface name corresponding to local_ip.
nic_name="<NETWORK_INTERFACE>"
local_ip="<DECODE_NODE_IP>"
export IP_ADDRESS="${local_ip}"
export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_IF_IP="${local_ip}"
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${nic_name}"

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1
export VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$1"

vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp \
  --host "${local_ip}" \
  --port "$2" \
  --data-parallel-size "$3" \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-rank "$4" \
  --data-parallel-address "$5" \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port "$6" \
  --tensor-parallel-size "$7" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 300 \
  --max-num-seqs 200 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --allowed-local-media-path / \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config":{"enable_npugraph_ex":true,"enable_static_kernel":false}, "weight_nz_mode":1, "enable_shared_expert_dp":false, "scheduler_config":{"recompute_scheduler_enable":true}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":"56010","engine_id":"2","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8},"decode":{"dp_size":1,"tp_size":8}}}'
```

Common Issues Tip: If the decode node fails to initialize, check that `--tensor-parallel-size` is 8, `--data-parallel-size-local` matches the global decode DP size (1),`kv_connector_extra_config.decode.dp_size` matches the global decode DP size.

**Key parameters for PD disaggregation:**

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 on both nodes.

`--distributed-executor-backend mp` uses multiprocessing on each node for the local workers.

Prefill uses `--data-parallel-size 1` and `--tensor-parallel-size 8`. This creates 1 DP group with TP8.

Decode uses `--data-parallel-size 1` and `--tensor-parallel-size 8`. This creates 1 DP group with TP8.

`--data-parallel-address` and `--data-parallel-rpc-port` define the DP control plane.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is larger on the prefill node and smaller on the decode node because prefill is prompt-token intensive while decode is latency sensitive.

`scheduler_config.recompute_scheduler_enable` sends requests back to the prefill side to recompute KV cache when decode KV cache is insufficient. Enable it only on the decode node in PD mode.

`--kv-transfer-config` sets the Mooncake connector. `kv_role` is `kv_producer` on prefill and `kv_consumer` on decode.

`kv_connector_extra_config.prefill.dp_size/tp_size` and `decode.dp_size/tp_size` must match the actual global DP and TP layout.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` is recommended on the decode node to reduce decode dispatch overhead.

Run the two scripts on their respective hosts after filling in each host's NIC and IP. The examples use seven argument positions: visible devices, HTTP port, global DP size, DP rank, DP master address, DP RPC port,TP size. P reads only positions 1–3 and 7 positions 4–6 are unused and retained for invocation compatibility. D uses all seven positions its argument 5 is the D host's service IP. Use DP1/TP8 to match the fixed KV topology changing topology also requires updating the connector JSON and device allocation.

Prefill uses the self-contained DP1 mode and therefore does not set the DP address or RPC port. Decode explicitly sets `--data-parallel-rank`, so the launcher also supplies its DP control-plane address and RPC port. In this DP1/rank0 example, the Decode address points to the Decode host itself. The Prefill and Decode services are separate vLLM instances and do not share a DP group. Do not mistake the DP RPC port for the HTTP port the proxy always uses the HTTP ports (argument 2), never the DP RPC port.

```shell
# On P:
bash run_p.sh 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 30060 1 0 "<P_SERVICE_IP>" 6884 8
# On D:
bash run_d.sh 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 30050 1 0 "<D_SERVICE_IP>" 6884 8
```

#### Proxy

After both services report ready, start the standard Pull proxy on the Prefill host. Use the same service IPs configured as `local_ip` in the two scripts and the HTTP ports passed as argument 2.

Run the command from the directory containing `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`:

```shell
unset ftp_proxy
unset https_proxy
unset http_proxy

PREFILL_HOST="<PREFILL_NODE_IP>"
DECODE_HOST="<DECODE_NODE_IP>"

python3 load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \
  --prefiller-hosts "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --prefiller-ports 30060 \
  --decoder-hosts "${DECODE_HOST}" \
  --decoder-ports 30050 \
  --host "${PREFILL_HOST}" \
  --port 8000
```

Send client requests to `http://<PREFILL_NODE_IP>:8000`. Use the Decode HTTP port `30050`, not the DP RPC port `6884`.

### Request Forwarding

Use the proxy paired with the actual connector, rather than choosing it by hardware name. The standard proxy script is in `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/` run the command from that directory. Replace the example hosts with reachable service IPs and use each service's HTTP port. P, D,the client must use the same `--served-model-name`.

| Connector | Request Order | Proxy | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| MooncakeConnectorV1 | Proxy calls P, then D; D pulls KV | load_balance_proxy_server_example.6 |  |
| MooncakeConnectorV2 | Proxy calls P, then D; D pulls KV | load_balance_proxy_server_example. |  |

Equal TP sizes do not make these connectors interchangeable. For unequal TP, verify the direction, divisibility, replicated KV heads, hybrid state layout,quantization support of the selected implementation. The TP8-to-TP4 example does not imply arbitrary TP ratios or reverse-direction support. Use scripts from the same vLLM-Ascend revision as the serving stack.

Use the complete proxy command for the selected deployment:

[A3 single-host 1P1D](#543-proxy): P and D use the same service IP and different HTTP ports.

 the D backend is HTTP port `30050`.

Do not use a DP RPC port or Mooncake KV-transfer port as a proxy backend. If requests reach the proxy but return no output, verify the P and D `/health` endpoints from the proxy host, confirm that the configured backend addresses exactly match each service's `--host` and HTTP port,then run the end-to-end checks in [Section 6](#6-functional-verification).

## Verification

Wait for both P and D to report ready, verify each HTTP service, then start the matching proxy. For single-node and MP deployment, use the API endpoint on node 0. For PD disaggregation, send generation requests through the proxy so that the test covers KV transfer.

```shell
curl -f "http://<prefill_ip>:<prefill_http_port>/health"
curl -f "http://<decode_ip>:<decode_http_port>/health"
curl -f "http://<proxy_ip>:<proxy_port>/healthcheck"
curl -f "http://<prefill_ip>:<prefill_http_port>/v1/models"
```

Check that the advertised model name matches the request. A health check only establishes HTTP readiness it does not verify the PD data path. Send several short requests, followed by concurrent requests that complete and reuse cache slots,inspect P, D,proxy logs.

```shell
curl "http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "prompt": "The future of AI is",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

Expected result: the HTTP status is 200 and the JSON response contains nonempty, coherent generated text in `choices`. Also verify a chat request with the checkpoint's chat template a short completion request alone is not an accuracy test. Check for transfer errors, empty results, repeated punctuation,abnormal repetition before running a full benchmark. Start with non-streaming requests, then repeat with streaming to test the proxy's chunked-response path.

### Function Calling

To enable tool calling, append the following options to the `vllm serve` command. For PD deployment, add them to both the Prefill and Decode commands and restart both services.

```text
--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

`--enable-auto-tool-choice` allows the model to select a tool, `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` parses tool calls,`--reasoning-parser qwen3` separates reasoning from the final answer.

Send a chat request with a tool definition to the service endpoint. For PD deployment, use the proxy endpoint.

```shell
curl "http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.5",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Use get_weather to check the current weather in Beijing."}
    ],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather for a city.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["city"]
        }
      }
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "max_tokens": 2048,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

When the model selects the tool, check that `choices[0].message.tool_calls` contains the function name `get_weather` and a JSON argument string with `city` set to `Beijing`. The client must execute the function, then send the assistant tool-call message and a `role: "tool"` result message with the matching `tool_call_id` in the next request to obtain the final answer. The serving process parses tool calls it does not execute the function.

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | KV Cache Selection | Download Links |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (BF16 version) | 2 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) nodes or | auto for the baseline | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp (quantized version) | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) node or | Follow the checkpoint KV quantization recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp (quantized version) | 1 Atlas 800I A3 (64 GB x 16) node or | Follow the checkpoint KV quantization recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | Check KV metadata; the model name alone is insufficient | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a4-mxfp4 (quantized version) |  | Check KV metadata; the model name alone is insufficient | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | mxfp8 for the supported C8 recipe | ModelScope |
| Qwen3. |  |  |  |

Note

`--quantization ascend` selects the Ascend model quantization implementation `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` selects MXFP8 KV cache storage. They configure different parts of inference. Enable `mxfp8` only with a supported checkpoint and its required KV scale metadata. A W4A8/W8A8 name,an MXFP weight format, does not by itself establish C8 KV cache compatibility. Do not copy a W4A8C8 or W8A8C8 KV setting to a different checkpoint without checking its quantization description and serving logs. Keep the weight revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata,KV cache settings consistent on P and D.

It is recommended to download the model weights to a shared directory across multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`, so that all serving nodes can load the same path.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

### Verify Multi-node Communication

For multi-node deployment, verify inter-node connectivity by following [Verify Multi-node Communication](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect).

Use mutually reachable service IPs on all nodes. In the scripts below, `local_ip` must belong to `nic_name`.

## Installation

You can also build and install `vllm-ascend` from source. Refer to [set up using python](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-existing-cann-install).

If you want to deploy a multi-node service, install the same version of vLLM and vLLM-Ascend on each node.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs both Prefill and Decode on the same node. It is suitable for functional validation and long-context serving.

Run the following script for online inference with a 133k context on one Atlas 800I A3 node (64 GB x 16). W8A8 deployment requires `--quantization ascend`.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download.
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
MODEL_PATH="Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp"
vllm serve "${MODEL_PATH}" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 133000 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "enforce_eager": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 1, "enable_flashcomm1": true}'
```

Common Issues Tip: If the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient,requests are not scheduled as expected, refer to [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) first,then check the model-specific FAQ in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Key parameters:**

`--data-parallel-size 1` uses one DP group. `--tensor-parallel-size` is 16 for the A3 example and

`--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers. Do not mix MoE tensor parallelism and expert parallelism in the same MoE layer.

`--max-model-len` is the maximum input plus output length for a single request. Increase it only when enough KV cache is available.

`--max-num-seqs` is the maximum number of active requests scheduled by each DP group. For performance tests, set `--max-num-seqs * --data-parallel-size` greater than or equal to the test concurrency.

`--max-num-batched-tokens` is the maximum number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. A larger value can improve prefill efficiency but consumes more activation memory.

`--gpu-memory-utilization` controls how much HBM vLLM can use to calculate KV cache capacity. A higher value increases KV cache size but can trigger OOM if runtime memory is higher than the profile run.

`--enable-prefix-caching` enables prefix caching. For Qwen3.5, short prefixes may not be cached when the hybrid KV cache manager adjusts the block size to a large value.

`--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the quantized weights used above. Remove this option when deploying the BF16 model.

`--speculative-config` enables Qwen3.5 MTP speculative decoding. Reduce `num_speculative_tokens` or remove this option if the workload is sensitive to first-token latency or if MTP is unstable in your environment.

`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'` enables full decode ACLGraph replay to reduce dispatch overhead.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 for the single-node examples above.

`--additional-config` configures Ascend-specific optimizations: `enable_cpu_binding=true` enables Ascend-native CPU binding `enable_fused_mc2=1` selects dispatch-FFN-combine and A3 examples for compatibility with the documented MTP and batching configurations `2` selects CANN MegaMoe and should only be enabled with a matching CANN/operator stack and supported token-shape limits `0` disables the fused path. `enable_flashcomm1=true` enables MoE sequence parallelism across TP ranks and requires `--enable-expert-parallel` with a TP size greater than 1.

### Multi-Node Deployment with MP (Recommended)

Run the following script on node 0.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

# nic_name is the network interface name corresponding to local_ip.
nic_name="xxxx"
local_ip="xxxx"
export IP_ADDRESS="${local_ip}"
export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="${nic_name}"

export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --api-server-count 2 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-address $local_ip \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 13389 \
  --seed 1024 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --quantization ascend \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}'
```

Common Issues Tip: If node 1 cannot join the service or HCCL initialization times out, refer to [verify multi-node communication environment](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-multi-node-interconnect) and [FAQs](../../faqs.html). Make sure the network interface names, IP addresses,RPC ports are consistent across nodes.

Run the following script on node 1.

```shell
#!/bin/sh

# nic_name is the network interface name corresponding to local_ip.
nic_name="xxxx"
local_ip="xxxx"
export IP_ADDRESS="${local_ip}"
export NETWORK_CARD_NAME="${nic_name}"

export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export HCCL_IF_IP=$local_ip
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=$nic_name

# The value of node0_ip must be consistent with local_ip on node 0.
node0_ip="xxxx"

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w8a8-mtp \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --headless \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-start-rank 1 \
  --data-parallel-address $node0_ip \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 13389 \
  --seed 1024 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --quantization ascend \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}'

**Key parameters for MP deployment:**

`--data-parallel-size` is the global DP size across all nodes. In the example, 2 DP ranks are used.

`--data-parallel-start-rank` is the first DP rank on the current node. Node 0 starts from 0 by default,node 1 starts from 1.

`--data-parallel-address` must point to the master DP node. Use node 0 `local_ip` on node 0 and `node0_ip` on other nodes.

`--data-parallel-rpc-port` is the DP RPC port. Use the same value on all nodes and ensure the port is available.

`--api-server-count` controls how many API server processes are started on the master node.

`--headless` starts a worker node without exposing an API server. Use it on non-master nodes.

`HCCL_IF_IP`, `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`,`HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` bind HCCL and Gloo communication to the selected network.

`multistream_overlap_shared_expert` overlaps shared expert computation for better throughput on MoE workloads.

### Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (A3)

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. This performance-oriented example deploys 1P1D on one 16-NPU Atlas 800I A3 host with the `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-w4a8-mtp` checkpoint. In this section, 1P1D describes two service groups it does not mean that P and D must occupy separate hosts.

The 16 NPUs are divided into two non-overlapping device sets:

| Service group | Physical devices | TP | DP | EP world size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 0-7 | 8 | 1 | 8 |
| Decode | 8-15 | 4 | 2 | 8 |

Prefill and Decode use the same service NIC and IP because they run on the same host, but they use different HTTP and Mooncake ports. The Decode launcher creates two local DP engines, each with TP4. Do not start a second copy of the Decode command.

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

**Key parameters for PD disaggregation:**

Prefill uses TP8/DP1 on devices 0-7. Decode uses TP4/DP2 on devices 8-15. With expert parallelism enabled, both service groups have an EP world size of 8.

The P and D device lists must not overlap. P and D can share the same service IP on a single host, but their HTTP and Mooncake ports must be different.

The Decode command starts both local DP ranks. Do not launch one Decode command per DP rank.

`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` selects Model Runner V1 on both service groups.

Use the same MTP method and `num_speculative_tokens` on P and D. To disable MTP for a comparison, remove `--speculative-config` from both commands.

`kv_connector_extra_config.prefill` must remain DP1/TP8,`decode` must remain DP2/TP4 for this topology.

`enable_flashcomm1=true`, `enable_fused_mc2=2`,`enable_shared_expert_dp=true` reproduce the performance-case MoE configuration. They require the matching CANN operators and software stack.

Prefill runs eagerly. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, enables NPU graph extensions,enables the recompute scheduler.

`--max-num-batched-tokens 300` and `--max-num-seqs 100` are Decode scheduler limits applied to each DP engine by vLLM.

Prefix caching and asynchronous scheduling are enabled on both service groups in this validated case. Revalidate output correctness if either setting or the connector version changes.

| Node role | NPUs | TP | DP | EP world size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 8 | 8 | 1 | 8 |
| Decode | 8 | 4 | 2 | 8 |

Both nodes must use the same checkpoint revision, tokenizer, quantization metadata,`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8`. This example uses `MooncakeConnectorV2`: the proxy calls Prefill first,Decode pulls the KV cache. The connector topology must remain DP1/TP8 for Prefill and DP2/TP4 for Decode.

Use a high-speed service network that is reachable in both directions. On each host, `local_ip` must be the IP assigned to `nic_name`. Do not reuse another host's endpoint resources.

#### C8 Accuracy and Compatibility Requirements

C8 KV cache is part of this performance recipe, not just a model-name convention. Keep the following conditions together:

Use the same compatible W4A8C8 checkpoint revision, tokenizer, chat template, quantization metadata,`--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` on P and D.

Use a v0.30.0 MRv1 build containing [the MXFP8 KV-scale fix #19017](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19017), merged into `releases/v0.30.0` as `14c6c3f43`,a build with an equivalent verified fix.

Keep `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, the P DP1/TP8 and D DP2/TP4 topology,the connector topology consistent.

Keep MTP settings identical on P and D. To run an MTP-off comparison, remove `--speculative-config` from both commands.

Prefix caching and asynchronous scheduling are enabled on both nodes for this performance case.

Prefill uses eager execution. Decode uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and enables NPU graph extensions.

`enable_fused_mc2=0` and `enable_prefill_mc2=false` reproduce this performance case. Do not infer the active setting from a profiling directory name.

`enable_shared_expert_dp=true` and `enable_flashcomm1=true` require expert parallelism and the matching CANN/software stack.

The D HTTP endpoint fronts both local DP engines. Do not use the DP RPC port as a Decode endpoint.

Use the standard Pull proxy with Prefill port 30060 and Decode port 30050. Start with short non-streaming requests, then verify request churn and the full accuracy baseline before performance testing. HTTP success or Mooncake transfer completion alone does not prove that C8 scale contents are correct. Check predictions for empty output, repeated punctuation, incoherent text,abnormal repetition evaluate MTP acceptance together with actual output correctness.

PD disaggregation separates Prefill and Decode into different service groups. Prefill nodes process large prompt chunks, Decode nodes serve token generation,a proxy forwards requests between them. These examples demonstrate how to tune prefill and decode resource ratios.

We recommend using Mooncake for deployment. Refer to [Mooncake](../features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.html) for the general PD disaggregation workflow.

Deploy `run_p.sh` and `run_d.sh` on the corresponding nodes,deploy a proxy script on the prefill master node to forward requests.
