guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (BF16 version) | Atlas 300I DUO | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8 (quantized version) | Atlas 300I DUO | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w4a8-mxfp (quantized version) |  | ModelScope |

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

## Installation

Refer to [using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image) for the complete installation guide.

#### Standard container[](#standard-container)

```bash
# Download the model weight to /root/.cache in advance.
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p

docker run --rm \
--name vllm-ascend \
--shm-size=10g \
--device /dev/davinci0 \
--device /dev/davinci1 \
--device /dev/davinci2 \
--device /dev/davinci3 \
--device /dev/davinci4 \
--device /dev/davinci5 \
--device /dev/davinci6 \
--device /dev/davinci7 \
--device /dev/davinci_manager \
--device /dev/devmm_svm \
--device /dev/hisi_hdc \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
-v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
-v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
-p 8080:8080 \
-it $IMAGE bash
```

After entering the container, verify that vLLM and vLLM-Ascend can be imported:

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm_ascend are ready')"
```

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs both Prefill and Atlas 300I DUO. `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-mxfp8` can be deployed on a single NPU of a

```shell
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6 \
  --dtype float16 \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex":false}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,8]}' \
  --quantization ascend \
  --max-model-len 20480 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

**Key parameters:**

- `--tensor-parallel-size 2` maps the model across two Atlas inference devices. Adjust it together with `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` according to the available devices and memory.
- `--dtype float16` is used for Atlas 300I DUO to match the Atlas inference execution path.
- `--max-num-seqs 16` limits concurrent active requests to reduce KV cache and graph capture pressure on Atlas 300I DUO.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization` controls KV cache capacity. Reduce it if startup or runtime requests report OOM.
- `--additional-config` with `"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": false}` is required because `enable_npugraph_ex` is not supported on Atlas 300I DUO.
- `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,8]}'` enables decode ACLGraph replay and explicitly limits capture sizes for Atlas 300I DUO.
- `--no-enable-prefix-caching` is the default recommendation for this Atlas 300I DUO example to reduce memory pressure.
- `--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model. Remove this option when deploying the BF16 model.
- To enable MTP speculative decoding, use `--speculative_config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}'`. We recommend setting num_speculative_tokens to 1. If your usage scenario involves fewer than two concurrent requests, it is recommended to enable MTP. Otherwise, it is recommended not to enable MTP.

Common Issues Tip: If the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient,requests are not scheduled as expected, refer to [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) first,then check the model-specific FAQ in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Service Verification:**

```shell
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

For other deployments, use their configured API port. The Atlas 300I DUO example listens on `127.0.0.1:8080`, so run its check on the serving node or container. A healthy service returns HTTP `200`. If the check fails, inspect the startup log for errors and wait for initialization to finish. After the health check passes, use [Section 6](#6-functional-verification) to verify that the model generates a response.

## Verification

- `--max-num-seqs 128` sets the maximum number of active requests scheduled concurrently. Reduce it if KV cache or graph capture memory is insufficient.
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` limits the number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. Increase it only after checking prefill throughput and activation memory usage.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` sets the fraction of device memory available to the model executor when calculating KV cache capacity. Reduce it if startup or runtime requests report OOM.

vllm serve Eco-Tech/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 135168 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --dtype float16 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}'
```

**Key parameters:**

- `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`, `--tensor-parallel-size 2`,`--data-parallel-size 1` run one model instance across the two selected NPUs with tensor parallelism and one data-parallel group.
- `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` selects Model Runner V2 for this deployment example.
- `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024` sets the HCCL communication buffer size for this example.
- `--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for MoE layers.
- `--safetensors-load-strategy lazy` uses lazy loading for Safetensors model weights.
- `--dtype float16` selects FP16 for this deployment example.
- `--max-model-len 135168` sets the maximum input plus output length for a single request. Ensure enough KV cache is available for the required context length.
- `--max-num-seqs 128` sets the maximum number of active requests scheduled concurrently. Reduce it if KV cache or graph capture memory is insufficient.
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` limits the number of tokens processed in one scheduler step. Increase it only after checking prefill throughput and activation memory usage.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90` sets the fraction of device memory available to the model executor when calculating KV cache capacity. Reduce it if startup or runtime requests report OOM.
- `--speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` enables Qwen3.5-style MTP speculative decoding with three draft tokens per step.
- `--additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true}'` enables Ascend-native CPU binding and shared-expert computation overlap.
- `--enable-prefix-caching` enables prefix caching. For long-context serving, monitor memory usage because prefix caching can increase KV cache pressure.
- `--quantization ascend` enables Ascend quantization for the W8A8 model used in this example.
- `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'` enables the hybrid full and piecewise ACLGraph mode.

Common Issues Tip: If the service fails to start, HBM is insufficient,requests are not scheduled as expected, refer to [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) first,then check the model-specific FAQ in [Section 10](#10-faq).

**Service Verification:**

```shell
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

## Verification

After the server is started, send a request to verify basic model functionality.

```shell
curl http://<server_ip>:<port>/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.6",
    "prompt": "The future of AI is",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0
  }'
```

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

The following model weights are available:

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B (BF16 version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 (Quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-mxfp8 (Quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8 (Quantized version) |  | ModelScope |
| Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p (Quantized version) | 1 Atlas 300I DUO | ModelScope |

`Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8c8-mxfp8` (W8A8 MXFP8 quantization with C8 MXFP8 KV cache): serve it with `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp8` recommended for long-sequence scenarios.

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

**Path description**: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. Ensure the model path in the subsequent deployment command matches this directory.

## Installation

Select an image based on your machine type and start the docker container on your node, refer to [using docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Start the docker image on each node.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p
export NAME=vllm-ascend

docker run --rm \
    --name $NAME \
    --shm-size=1g \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
    -it $IMAGE bash
```

After entering the container, verify that vLLM and vLLM-Ascend can be imported:

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm_ascend are ready')"
```

Expected output:

```output
vllm and vllm_ascend are ready
```

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment completes both Prefill and Decode within the same node, suitable for development, testing,medium-scale inference scenarios. On Atlas 300I DUO, at least 2 devices are required.

Before starting the service:

Replace the model path, parallel sizes and service port with values from the target environment.

Currently only the **TP** scenario is supported. Choose **TP=2** or **TP=4** according to the available devices. Replace `MODEL_PATH` with a ModelScope model id or a local directory path. The quantized version needs to start with the `--quantization ascend` parameter.

[Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8](#__tabbed_3_1)

Startup Command:

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# Load model from ModelScope to speed up download
export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True

# Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
export MODEL_PATH=Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8-310p

vllm serve $MODEL_PATH \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 8000 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.8 \
    --max-num-seqs 128 \
    --max-model-len 16384 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
    --dtype float16 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [2,16]}' \
    --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": false}}'
```

Key Parameter Descriptions:

- `--tensor-parallel-size` sets the tensor parallel size. Choose **TP=2** or **TP=4** according to the available devices.
- `--max-model-len` represents the context length, which is the maximum value of the input plus output for a single request. Configure it based on the actual workload and available memory `Qwen3.8-27B` supports up to 262144.
- `--max-num-seqs` indicates the maximum number of concurrent requests.
- `--gpu-memory-utilization` represents the proportion of HBM that vLLM will use for actual inference. Configure this value according to the actual device memory setting it too high may cause OOM. The default value is `0.9`.
- `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` sets the data type of the Mamba SSM cache. On Atlas 300I DUO, only `float16` is supported.
- `--dtype float16` must be set on Atlas 300I DUO. These devices only support the FP16 data type.
- `--speculative-config` uses `qwen3_5_mtp` for `Qwen3.8-27B` because it shares the same MTP head design as `Qwen3.5-27B`. On Atlas 300I DUO, it is recommended to set `num_speculative_tokens` to `1`.
- `--compilation-config` contains configurations related to the aclgraph graph mode. The most significant configurations are `"cudagraph_mode"` and `"cudagraph_capture_sizes"`, which have the following meanings: `"cudagraph_mode"`: represents the specific graph mode. Currently, `"PIECEWISE"` and `"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"` are supported. The graph mode is mainly used to reduce the cost of operator dispatch. Currently, `"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"` is recommended. `"cudagraph_capture_sizes"`: specifies the batch size tiers at which graphs are captured. When tensor parallelism (TP) is enabled, hardware event-id constraints allow at most two capture sizes (for example, `[1, 8]`). With MTP enabled, calculate each capture size as `n * (num_speculative_tokens + 1)`, where `n` is a capture size for the deployment without MTP. For example, when `num_speculative_tokens` is `1`, the non-MTP sizes `[1,2,4,8]` become `[2,4,8,16]`.
- `--additional-config` with `"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": false}` is required on Atlas 300I DUO because `enable_npugraph_ex` is not supported on this platform.

Wait until the engine finishes loading weights and graph capture. A successful startup includes output similar to the following:

```output
INFO:     Started server process
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

## Verification

After the service is started, the model can be invoked by sending a prompt. Two API interfaces are supported: `completions` and `chat/completions`. Use the `--served-model-name` you configured (`qwen3.8` for `Qwen3.8-27B`).

**Completions API:**

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8",
        "prompt": "The future of AI is",
        "max_tokens": 50,
        "temperature": 0.7
    }'
```

**Chat Completions API:**

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "user", "content": "The future of AI is"}
        ],
        "max_completion_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 1.0,
        "top_p": 0.95,
        "reasoning_effort": "xhigh",
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
            "enable_thinking": true,
            "preserve_thinking": true
        }
    }'
```

Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled by setting `enable_thinking` to `false` in `chat_template_kwargs`. The example above keeps thinking mode on,`preserve_thinking` retains the reasoning context of historical messages.

Set `reasoning_effort` in the top-level Chat Completions request body to adjust the model's reasoning depth. The example above uses `xhigh` omit the field to use the default `xhigh`. The model officially supports these levels:

`xhigh`: default deeper reasoning for complex tasks.

`medium`: balances accuracy and speed.

`low`: prioritizes speed and cost.

Expected Result: The service returns HTTP 200 OK. The JSON response contains the `choices` field with generated text. Example output for the completions API (content truncated for brevity):

```json
{
    "id": "cmpl-xxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "object": "text_completion",
    "created": 1780971952,
    "model": "qwen3.8",
    "choices": [
        {
            "index": 0,
            "text": "The future of AI is a rapidly evolving landscape with breakthroughs in natural language understanding, multimodal reasoning, and autonomous agents. As models grow more capable and efficient...",
            "logprobs": null,
            "finish_reason": "length"
        }
    ],
    "usage": {
        "prompt_tokens": 4,
        "total_tokens": 54,
        "completion_tokens": 50
    }
}
```

## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

The following model weight is available:

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp` (Quantized version): requires 1 Atlas 800 A3 (64GB × 8) node to serve. [https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp)

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as /root/.cache/.

## Installation

The pre-built images listed below have been validated for this tutorial.

A pre-built Qwen3.8 A3 image is available in the [vllm-ascend repository](https://quay.io/repository/ascend/vllm-ascend?tab=tags&tag=latest). Select the image that matches the host operating system:

openEuler: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:qwen3.8-next-a3-openeuler`

Ubuntu: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:qwen3.8-next-a3`

The following example uses the AArch64 image and exposes 16 devices on an Atlas 800 A3 node.

Start the docker image on each node.

```bash
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:qwen3.8-next-a3
export NAME=vllm-ascend-qwen38-flash-next

docker pull "$IMAGE"

docker run --rm \
    --name "$NAME" \
    --shm-size=16g \
    --net=host \
    --device /dev/davinci0 \
    --device /dev/davinci1 \
    --device /dev/davinci2 \
    --device /dev/davinci3 \
    --device /dev/davinci4 \
    --device /dev/davinci5 \
    --device /dev/davinci6 \
    --device /dev/davinci7 \
    --device /dev/davinci8 \
    --device /dev/davinci9 \
    --device /dev/davinci10 \
    --device /dev/davinci11 \
    --device /dev/davinci12 \
    --device /dev/davinci13 \
    --device /dev/davinci14 \
    --device /dev/davinci15 \
    --device /dev/davinci_manager \
    --device /dev/devmm_svm \
    --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
    -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
    -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /path/to/models:/models \
    -it "$IMAGE" bash
```

After entering the container, verify that vLLM and vLLM-Ascend can be imported:

```shell
python -c "import vllm, vllm_ascend; print('vllm and vllm-ascend are ready')"
```

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

For single-node online deployment on Atlas 800 A3, the following DP1 × TP8 command was validated with an Ascend-compatible W8A8 checkpoint. It enables QSA Lightning Indexer, QSA Expand E3, MTP speculative decoding, Function Calling,reasoning parsing.

Before starting the service:

Replace `MODEL_PATH` with the directory recorded when downloading the model weight.

Revalidate memory capacity (e.g., with `npu-smi info`) before changing the context length, concurrency,memory utilization.

The following example is for Atlas 800 A3.

```bash
unset CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH CPATH C_INCLUDE_PATH
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export MODEL_PATH=/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_LIGHTNING_INDEXER=1
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_E3V=1
unset VLLM_ASCEND_FORCE_QSA_REFERENCE

vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8088 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.8-flash-next \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --quantization ascend \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
    --data-parallel-start-rank 0 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --max-model-len 131072 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32],"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false}}'
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

The following model weight is available:

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp` (Quantized version): requires 1 Atlas 800 A3 (64GB × 8) node to serve. [https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp)

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as /root/.cache/.

## Installation

If you don't want to use the docker image as above, you can also build all from source:

Install `vllm-ascend` from source, refer to [installation](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-existing-cann-install).

If you want to deploy a multi-node environment, you need to set up the environment on each node.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

For single-node online deployment on Atlas 800 A3, the following DP1 × TP8 command was validated with an Ascend-compatible W8A8 checkpoint. It enables QSA Lightning Indexer, QSA Expand E3, MTP speculative decoding, Function Calling,reasoning parsing.

Before starting the service:

Replace `MODEL_PATH` with the directory recorded when downloading the model weight.

Revalidate memory capacity (e.g., with `npu-smi info`) before changing the context length, concurrency,memory utilization.

The following example is for Atlas 800 A3.

```bash
unset CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH CPATH C_INCLUDE_PATH
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export MODEL_PATH=/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mtp
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_LIGHTNING_INDEXER=1
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_E3V=1
unset VLLM_ASCEND_FORCE_QSA_REFERENCE

vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8088 \
    --served-model-name qwen3.8-flash-next \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --quantization ascend \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
    --data-parallel-start-rank 0 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --max-model-len 131072 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --mamba-cache-mode align \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32],"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"enforce_eager":true}' \
    --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"ascend_compilation_config":{"fuse_norm_quant":false}}'
```

Key parameter descriptions:

- `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_LIGHTNING_INDEXER=1` enables the fused QSA Lightning Indexer path.
- `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_QSA_E3V=1` enables the fused QSA Expand E3 path.
- `--quantization ascend` loads the Ascend-compatible W8A8 checkpoint.
- `--tensor-parallel-size 8` and `--data-parallel-size 1` configure the A3 single-DP TP8 topology.
- `--max-model-len 131072` caps the maximum context length. Common values: `65536` (64K), `131072` (128K).
- `--enable-expert-parallel` enables expert parallelism for the MoE layers.
- `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align` enables Prefix Caching with aligned GDN and PLE state checkpoints.
- The validated command does not set `--language-model-only`, so the vision encoder remains enabled and the service accepts both text and multimodal requests. For a text-only deployment, you may add `--language-model-only` to skip loading the vision encoder.
- `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` enables automatic Function Calling with the Qwen3 XML parser.
- `--reasoning-parser qwen3` separates reasoning from the final answer in the OpenAI-compatible response.
- `--speculative-config` uses the model's MTP head to draft three tokens. `enforce_eager=true` keeps the MTP proposer in eager mode.
- `--compilation-config` enables `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` ACLGraph for decode.
- `fuse_norm_quant=false` selects the validated norm and quantization path for this W8A8 deployment.

Verify the service is ready: the log should show `Application startup complete`.

## Verification

After the service is started, the model can be invoked by sending a prompt. The `chat/completions` API is supported. Use the `--served-model-name` you configured (`qwen3.8-flash-next` for `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`).

### Basic Chat Completion

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
        "messages": [
            {"role": "user", "content": "Who are you?"}
        ],
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected result: the service returns HTTP 200 OK.

### Multimodal Chat Completion

The validated deployment accepts image-and-text input. Replace `<IMAGE_URL>` with an image URL accessible from the serving environment:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "image_url",
                        "image_url": {
                            "url": "<IMAGE_URL>"
                        }
                    },
                    {
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Describe this image."
                    }
                ]
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

Expected result: the service returns HTTP 200 OK and describes the supplied image in `choices[0].message.content`.

### Function Calling

Function Calling requires the following startup options, which are already included in [Section 5](#5-online-service-deployment):

```text
--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml
```

Send a request containing the available tools and set `tool_choice` to `auto`:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "What is the weather in Beijing?"
            }
        ],
        "tools": [
            {
                "type": "function",
                "function": {
                    "name": "get_weather",
                    "description": "Get current weather for a city",
                    "parameters": {
                        "type": "object",
                        "properties": {
                            "city": {
                                "type": "string",
                                "description": "City name"
                            }
                        },
                        "required": ["city"]
                    }
                }
            }
        ],
        "tool_choice": "auto",
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0
    }'
```

When the model chooses the function, the parsed result appears in `choices[0].message.tool_calls`. The caller must execute the function and send its result back to the model in a follow-up message.

### Reasoning Parser and Thinking Control

Reasoning parsing requires the following startup option, which is already included in [Section 5](#5-online-service-deployment):

```text
--reasoning-parser qwen3
```

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next uses thinking mode by default. To request reasoning explicitly, set `enable_thinking` to `true` (or omit it). The parser returns the reasoning separately from the final answer:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0,
        "top_p": 1,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
            "enable_thinking": true
        }
    }'
```

The final answer is returned in `choices[0].message.content`, while the parsed reasoning is returned separately in the `reasoning_content` field of the response.

To disable thinking and request a direct answer, use the validated non-thinking request:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
        "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Who are you?"
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0,
        "top_p": 1,
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
            "enable_thinking": false
        }
    }'
```

guideMd:
## Prerequisites

### Model Weight

| Weight Version | Hardware Requirements | Download Links |
|---|---|---|
| siglip2-base-patch16-224 (FP16) | 1 Atlas 300I DUO node | Modelscope \ |

**Path description:** Please download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record this path. For example: `/root/.cache/modelscope/hub/models/google/siglip2-base-patch16-224`. In subsequent commands, replace `<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>` with the path you recorded here (a local directory or a Hugging Face / ModelScope model id such as `google/siglip2-base-patch16-224`).

### ImageNet Labels (Optional, for Accuracy Evaluation)

For ImageNet val zero-shot Top-1 evaluation, prepare:

[ImageNet ILSVRC 2012 val images](https://www.image-net.org/download.php) (login and agree to terms)

`val_label.txt` in PyTorch index format (0–999), for example from [simple-imagenet-test](https://github.com/rentainhe/simple-imagenet-test/blob/master/val_label.txt)

`imagenet1000_clsidx_to_labels.txt` from [yrevar gist](https://gist.github.com/yrevar/942d3a0ac09ec9e5eb3a)

## Installation

**Hardware support:** SigLIP2 in this tutorial is supported and validated on **Atlas 300I DUO** only. Use the corresponding Docker image and the installation steps below.

You can use the official all-in-one Docker image. For the available image tags and published versions, refer to [Using Docker](../../getting_started/installation.html#installation-prebuilt-image).

Step 1: Download the latest Docker image

```bash
docker pull quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p
```

Step 2: Start Docker container

```bash
# Set the vLLM Ascend image name.
export IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0-310p
export NAME=siglip2-dev

# Atlas 300I DUO uses a single NPU device (/dev/davinci0).
docker run --rm \
--name $NAME \
--net=host \
--shm-size=1g \
--privileged=true \
--device /dev/davinci0 \
--device /dev/davinci_manager \
--device /dev/devmm_svm \
--device /dev/hisi_hdc \
-v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/tools/hccn_tool \
-v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64/ \
-v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/version.info \
-v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
-v /root/.cache:/root/.cache \
-it $IMAGE bash
```

Step 3: Installation Verification

After starting the container, run the following command to verify the installation:

```bash
docker ps | grep $NAME
```

Expected result: The container is listed with status `Up`. You can also verify the vllm-ascend version inside the container:

```bash
pip show vllm-ascend
```

Expected result: The version information is displayed, matching the pulled image version.

## Deployment

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs text and image embedding on one Atlas 300I DUO node, suitable for development, testing,online `/v1/embeddings` serving.

Startup command:

```shell
#!/bin/sh

export MODEL_PATH=<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>

vllm serve $MODEL_PATH \
    --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
    --runner pooling \
    --chat-template template_basic.jinja \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [64,32]}' \
    --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_npugraph_ex": false}}' \
    --dtype float16 \
    --port 8000 \
    --max-model-len 64
```

Expected Result:

If the service starts successfully, the log contains:

```text
INFO:     Started server process [<pid>]
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Required Parameter Descriptions:

`--compilation-config` For Atlas 300I DUO, due to limited hardware streams, the size of cudagraph_capture_sizes is restricted.

Key Parameter Descriptions:

**Tensor parallelism (TP) is not supported** for SigLIP2 online serving. Do not set `--tensor-parallel-size` deploy on a single Atlas 300I DUO NPU as shown above.

`--served-model-name` must match the `"model"` field in `/v1/embeddings` requests use the same value as `MODEL_PATH`.

`--runner pooling` is required. SigLIP2 is an embedding model, not a generative LLM.

`--max-model-len 64` matches SigLIP2 text tokenization (`padding=max_length`, `max_length=64`).

`--chat-template template_basic.jinja` is required when sending images via `messages` on `/v1/embeddings`.

`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}'` allows one image per request.

For image-only embedding over HTTP, use an **empty** text prompt in `messages` or offline `prompt=""` with `multi_modal_data`.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.html) for troubleshooting.

### Multi-Node PD Separation Deployment

SigLIP2 is a pooling embedding model and **does not support** multi-node PD (Prefill-Decode) separation deployment. Use [§5.1 Single-Node Online Deployment](#51-single-node-online-deployment) instead.

## Verification

Once your server is started, you can verify with the following commands.

### Text Embedding

```bash
0.0.1:8000/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"model\": \"${MODEL_PATH}\",
    \"input\": [\"This is a photo of a dog.\"]
  }"
```

Expected Result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON response containing the `embedding` field. Example output (embedding truncated for brevity):

```json
{
  "id": "embd-xxxxxxxx",
  "object": "list",
  "created": 1770000000,
  "model": "<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>",
  "data": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "object": "embedding",
      "embedding": [
        0.0123,
        -0.0456
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Use the template `"This is a photo of {}."` for zero-shot classification prompts. SigLIP2 was trained with `padding=max_length` and `max_length=64` for text vLLM applies this when using offline `tokenization_kwargs`.

### Image Embedding

Encode the image as base64 and send via `messages`:

```bash
jpg  # Replace with your local image path
IMG_B64=$(base64 -w 0 "${IMAGE_PATH}")

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"model\": \"${MODEL_PATH}\",
    \"encoding_format\": \"float\",
    \"messages\": [{
      \"role\": \"user\",
      \"content\": [{
        \"type\": \"image_url\",
        \"image_url\": {\"url\": \"data:image/jpeg;base64,${IMG_B64}\"}
      }]
    }]
  }"
```

Expected Result:

The service returns HTTP 200 OK with a JSON response containing the `embedding` field. Example output (embedding truncated for brevity):

```json
{
  "id": "embd-xxxxxxxx",
  "object": "list",
  "created": 1770000000,
  "model": "<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>",
  "data": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "object": "embedding",
      "embedding": [
        0.0234,
        -0.0567
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

For more usage examples, please reference the [vLLM pooling embed examples](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/examples/pooling/embed).

### Offline Embedding

**Note**: Stop the online service from [§5.1 Single-Node Online Deployment](#51-single-node-online-deployment) before this offline test (press `Ctrl+C` in the `vllm serve` terminal).

```python
from vllm import LLM

    model=MODEL_PATH,
    runner="pooling",
    limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    max_model_len=64,
)

# Text
text_out = llm.embed(
    ["This is a photo of a dog."],
    tokenization_kwargs={"padding": "max_length", "max_length": 64},
)
print(len(text_out[0].outputs.embedding))

# Image (empty prompt; field name must be multi_modal_data)
from PIL import Image

IMAGE_PATH = "/path/to/image.jpg"  # Replace with your local image path
img = Image.open(IMAGE_PATH).convert("RGB")
img_out = llm.embed(
    {"prompt": "", "multi_modal_data": {"image": img}},
)
print(len(img_out[0].outputs.embedding))
```

### Single-Node Online Deployment

Single-node deployment runs text and image embedding on one Atlas 300I DUO node, suitable for development, testing,online `/v1/embeddings` serving.

Startup command:

```shell
#!/bin/sh

export MODEL_PATH=<YOUR_MODEL_PATH>

vllm serve $MODEL_PATH \
    --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
    --runner pooling \
    --chat-template template_basic.jinja \

Expected Result:

```text

INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
INFO:     Application startup complete.

`--compilation-config` For Atlas 300I DUO, due to limited hardware streams, the size of cudagraph_capture_sizes is restricted.

`--served-model-name` must match the `"model"` field in `/v1/embeddings` requests use the same value as `MODEL_PATH`.

`--runner pooling` is required. SigLIP2 is an embedding model, not a generative LLM.

`--max-model-len 64` matches SigLIP2 text tokenization (`padding=max_length`, `max_length=64`).

`--chat-template template_basic.jinja` is required when sending images via `messages` on `/v1/embeddings`.

`--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}'` allows one image per request.

    }
  ]
}

## Prerequisites

### Characteristic Matrix

- The following table shows the features supported by each version of the Llama model

| Model and parameter quantity | 800I A2 Tensor Parallelism | FP16 | BF16 | Flash Attention | Paged Attention | W8A8 quantization | W8A16 quantization | KV cache quantization | MOE quantization | MindIE Service | TGI | Long sequence | prefix_cache | FA3 Quantization | functioncall | Multi LoRA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B | Support world size 1,2,4,8 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

Note: The supported world size shown in the table is a configuration that can be run through the dialogue test. In actual operation, the video memory usage caused by the length of the input sequence must also be considered.

### Weight

**Weight download**

-[DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B/tree/main)

### Path variable explanation

| Variable name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| working_dir | The directory where the acceleration library and model library are placed after downloading (only used in source code download scenarios) |
| llm_path | ATB_Models The path where the model warehouse is located. If you use a mirror, the path is `/usr/local/Ascend/atb-models`; if you use the code downloaded by gitcode, the path is `${working_dir}/MindIE-LLM/examples/atb_models/` |
| script_path | The path where the script is located; the path where the working script of the Llama3 series is located is `${llm_path}/examples/models/llama3` |
| weight_path | Model weight path |

#### Atlas 800I A2 w8a8 Quantization

- Generate quantified weight dependency msModelSlim tool, see [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) for installation method

- The quantified weights are generated uniformly using the `${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}/examples/convert/model_slim/quantifier.py` script. The following provides a quick start command for Llama model quantified weight generation.
- Please use the following command to generate W8A8 quantified weights
  - Note that this quantization method only supports running on Atlas 800I A2 server
```shell
# 设置 CANN 包的环境变量
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
# 关闭虚拟内存
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False
# 进入 atb-models 目录
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B 量化，有回退层，antioutlier 使用 m1 算法配置，使用 min-max 量化方式，校准数据集使用 50 条 BoolQ 数据，在 NPU 上进行运算
bash examples/models/llama3/generate_quant_weight.sh -src {浮点权重路径} -dst {W8A8 量化权重路径} -type llama3.1_8b_w8a8
```

**Step 1 Generate W8A8S quantified weight**

- Modify the `torch_dtype` field in the model weight config.json to `float16`
- Generate quantified weight dependency msModelSlim tool, see [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) for installation method
- Enter the `msmodelslim/example/Llama` directory to execute the quantization script
```shell
# 运行量化转换脚本
python3 quant_llama.py --model_path {浮点权重路径} --save_directory {W8A8S 量化权重路径} --calib_file ../common/boolq.jsonl --w_bit 4 --a_bit 8 --fraction 0.011 --co_sparse True
```
**Step 2 Quantitative weight segmentation and compression**

```shell
# 执行"jq --version"查看是否安装 jq，若返回"bash：jq：command not found"，则依次执行"apt-get update"和"apt install jq"
jq --version
```

```shell
export IGNORE_INFER_ERROR=1
# 进入 atb-models 目录
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# 运行切分及压缩脚本
torchrun --nproc_per_node {TP 数} -m examples.convert.model_slim.sparse_compressor --model_path {W8A8S 量化权重路径} --save_directory {W8A8SC 量化权重路径}
```
- The number of TP is the number of tensor parallel parallels
- Note: If the weight is generated with TP=2 for segmentation, it also needs to be run with TP=2.
- Example
```shell
torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 -m examples.convert.model_slim.sparse_compressor --model_path /data1/weights/model_slim/Llama-8b_w8a8s --save_directory /data1/weights/model_slim/Llama-8b_w8a8sc
```

## Installation

Instruct users to install the MindIE container image. Please ensure that the server can connect to the network.

#### Prerequisite [](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#%E5%89%8D%E6%8F%90%E6%9D%A1%E4%BB%B6)

- The NPU driver and firmware have been installed on the host machine. If it is not installed, download [固件与驱动](https://hiascend.com/hardware/firmware-drivers/community) and select the corresponding community version or commercial version of firmware and driver according to the product series and model. Please refer to the following command to install:
```bash
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run
chmod +x Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-driver_<version>_linux-<arch>.run --full --force
./Ascend-hdk-<chip_type>-npu-firmware_<version>.run --full
```
- Users install Docker on the host machine by themselves (the version requirement is greater than or equal to 24.x.x). For the installation of Docker, see [安装Docker](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/docker_installation/).
- Before configuring the source, please ensure that the installation environment can connect to the network.

Description

For the Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module, the operating system compatibility requirements of the host and container image are as follows:

- Ubuntu 22.04 host supports running Ubuntu 24.04 container image
- openEuler 22.03 host supports running openEuler 24.03 container image

Please select a compatible container image version based on the host operating system.

#### Get MindIE image [](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#%E8%8E%B7%E5%8F%96mindie%E9%95%9C%E5%83%8F)

1. Click [昇腾镜像仓库链接](https://www.hiascend.com/developer/ascendhub/detail/af85b724a7e5469ebd7ea13c3439d48f) to enter the MindIE image download page.
2. Click the login button in the upper right corner of the page and log in with your Huawei account (if you have not registered yet, please register first).
3. On the "Image Version" tab of the MindIE image download page, click the "Download Now" button in the "**Operation**" column behind the corresponding image according to your device form.
4. Download the image according to the image download operation guide page that pops up, as shown in [图1](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#figure1). **Figure 1** Mirror download

#### Use image [](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E9%95%9C%E5%83%8F)
1. Execute the following corresponding commands according to the device form to start the container. The container startup command is for reference only and can be modified according to your needs. The command parameters are introduced as shown in [表1](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#table1). **Atlas 800I A2 Inference Server** `bash docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \ # 对于多模态理解模型，若业务最大并发数较高，--shm-size建议设置不小于100g --name <container-name> \ -w /home \ --device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \ --device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \ --device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \ -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \ -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \ -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \ -v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \ -v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \ {IMAGE_ID} bash` Description `{IMAGE_ID}` is the image ID. After the image is installed, execute the `docker images` command to view the corresponding ID. Just replace it in the above command. For the `--device` parameter, the mounting permission is set to `rwm` instead of `rw` or `r` with smaller permissions. information and run the MindIE business normallybut if the mounted If the npu (corresponding to `davinci_xxx_` in the mount option, for example, `npu0` corresponds to `davinci0`) is occupied by other tasks, using the `npu-smi` command will print an error and  if the mount permission is set to `rw`, after entering the container, an error will be printed when using the `npu-smi` command,the MindIE task cannot be run (`torch.npu.set_device()` will fail at this time). **Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module** When starting the container, you need to additionally mount some driver libraries and configuration files that npu-smi depends on. If it is not mounted, executing npu-smi related commands in the container may fail. The startup commands for different container image operating systems are as follows: Ubuntu 24.04 image: `docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=1g \ # 对于多模态理解模型，若业务最大并发数较高，若业务最大并发数较高，--shm-size建议设置不小于100g --name <container-name> \ --device=/dev/davinci0:/dev/davinci0 \ --device=/dev/davinci_manager \ --device=/dev/ascend_manager \ --device=/dev/user_config \ -v /etc/sys_version.conf:/etc/sys_version.conf \ -v /etc/ld.so.conf.d/mind_so.conf:/etc/ld.so.conf.d/mind_so.conf \ -v /etc/hdcBasic.cfg:/etc/hdcBasic.cfg \ -v /var/dmp_daemon:/var/dmp_daemon \ -v /usr/lib64/libsemanage.so.2:/usr/lib64/libsemanage.so.2 \ -v /usr/lib64/libmmpa.so:/usr/lib64/libmmpa.so \ -v /usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1:/usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1 \ -v /usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2.0.9:/usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2 \ -v /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi:/usr/local/sbin/npu-smi \ -v /usr/lib64/libstackcore.so:/usr/lib64/libstackcore.so \ -v /etc/slog.conf:/etc/slog.conf \ -v /var/slogd:/var/slogd \ -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64:/usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64 \ -v /path-to-weights:/path-to-weights:ro \ mindie:3.0.0-Atlas 800I A2 inference server uses the Alibaba Cloud Linux 3.2104 U10 operating system, this parameter must be used in the start container command to lift the limit on the number of processes. -it means starting an interactive terminal (-i) and connecting it to the standard input and output (-t) of the container, enabling interaction with the inside of the container, such as running command line operations. -d indicates that the container will run in background mode, that is, the container is started in the background. Using this parameter will not block the current terminal operation,you can continue to perform other operations after starting the container. --net indicates that the container will use the host's network configuration (network sharing), allowing the container to directly access the host's network interface, which is suitable for scenarios that require low latency and direct access to network resources. --shm-size indicates the shared memory (/dev/shm) size of the specified container, which can be set by the user. 1g is an example value. For multi-modal understanding models, if the maximum number of business concurrencies is high, it is recommended that --shm-size be set to no less than 100g. This value cannot exceed the total remaining physical memory of the host,can be viewed using the `free -h` command. When data parallelism is enabled (that is, when DP>1), the shared memory size needs to be adjusted as DP increases: When DP=2, shm-size is at least 2g. When DP=4, shm-size is at least 3g. When DP=8, shm-size is at least 5g. When DP=16, shm-size is at least 9g. --name means to specify a name for the container. \<container-name> is the identifier of the container, which can be set by yourself and is unique in the current system. If not set, Docker will automatically assign a random name. --device means mapping the host device to the container. Each --device parameter shares a host device (such as a hardware accelerator card or other hardware device) to the container so that the container can directly access it. /dev/davinci_manager: davinci related management equipment. /dev/hisi_hdc: hdc related management equipment. /dev/devmm_svm: Memory management related devices. /dev/ascend_manager: Ascend device management related devices. /dev/user_config: User configuration related equipment, which needs to be mounted when executing commands such as npu-smi in the Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module container. /dev/davinci*X*: NPU device, *X* is the ID number, such as: davinci0. You can query the device number and name according to the `ll /dev/ \| grep davinci` command, bind the device as needed,modify "--device=****" in the above command. -v indicates that the files or directories of the physical machine are mapped to the corresponding paths within the container,the ro parameter is used to set these directories to read-only permissions. /usr/local/Ascend/driver: This path contains hardware driver files. The driver is installed on the host and mapped to the container before it can be used in the container. Please modify it according to the actual path where the driver is located. /usr/local/sbin: This path contains NPU status viewing commands such as npu-smi. saved so that the container can access the weights. Please modify it according to the actual path. (The weight file and the data set file are placed in this path at the same time) For the Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module, additional files or directories that npu-smi related commands depend on need to be mounted according to the container image operating system: /etc/sys_version.conf: system version configuration file. /etc/ld.so.conf.d/mind_so.conf: dynamic library search path configuration file. /etc/hdcBasic.cfg: hdc basic configuration file. /var/dmp_daemon: Directory related to dmp_daemon running. /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi: npu-smi command. /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64: driver dynamic library directory. /etc/slog.conf, /var/slogd: log configuration file and log running directory. /usr/lib64/libmmpa.so, /usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1, /usr/lib64/libstackcore.so: general dynamic libraries that npu-smi depends on. /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libyaml-0.so.2: The libyaml dynamic library that npu-smi depends on under the Ubuntu 24.04 image. /usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2.0.9: The libyaml dynamic library that npu-smi depends on under the openEuler 24.03 image. /usr/lib64/libsemanage.so.2: The libsemanage dynamic library that npu-smi depends on under the openEuler 24.03 image.

| Model and parameter quantity | 800I A2 Tensor Parallelism | FP16 | BF16 | Flash Attention | Paged Attention | W8A8 quantization | W8A16 quantization | KV cache quantization | MOE quantization | MindIE Service | TGI | Long sequence | prefix_cache | FA3 Quantization | functioncall | Multi LoRA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B | Support world size 1,2,4,8 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

Note: The supported world size shown in the table is a configuration that can be run through the dialogue test. In actual operation, the video memory usage caused by the length of the input sequence must also be considered.

### Weight

**Weight download**

-[DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B/tree/main)

### Path variable explanation

| Variable name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| working_dir | The directory where the acceleration library and model library are placed after downloading (only used in source code download scenarios) |
| llm_path | ATB_Models The path where the model warehouse is located. If you use a mirror, the path is `/usr/local/Ascend/atb-models`; if you use the code downloaded by gitcode, the path is `${working_dir}/MindIE-LLM/examples/atb_models/` |
| script_path | The path where the script is located; the path where the working script of the Llama3 series is located is `${llm_path}/examples/models/llama3` |
| weight_path | Model weight path |

#### Atlas 800I A2 w8a8 Quantization

- Generate quantified weight dependency msModelSlim tool, see [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) for installation method

- The quantified weights are generated uniformly using the `${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}/examples/convert/model_slim/quantifier.py` script. The following provides a quick start command for Llama model quantified weight generation.
- Please use the following command to generate W8A8 quantified weights
  - Note that this quantization method only supports running on Atlas 800I A2 server
```shell
# 设置 CANN 包的环境变量
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
# 关闭虚拟内存
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False
# 进入 atb-models 目录
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B 量化，有回退层，antioutlier 使用 m1 算法配置，使用 min-max 量化方式，校准数据集使用 50 条 BoolQ 数据，在 NPU 上进行运算
bash examples/models/llama3/generate_quant_weight.sh -src {浮点权重路径} -dst {W8A8 量化权重路径} -type llama3.1_8b_w8a8
```

**Step 1 Generate W8A8S quantified weight**

- Modify the `torch_dtype` field in the model weight config.json to `float16`
- Generate quantified weight dependency msModelSlim tool, see [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) for installation method
- Enter the `msmodelslim/example/Llama` directory to execute the quantization script
```shell
# 运行量化转换脚本
python3 quant_llama.py --model_path {浮点权重路径} --save_directory {W8A8S 量化权重路径} --calib_file ../common/boolq.jsonl --w_bit 4 --a_bit 8 --fraction 0.011 --co_sparse True
```
**Step 2 Quantitative weight segmentation and compression**

```shell
# 执行"jq --version"查看是否安装 jq，若返回"bash：jq：command not found"，则依次执行"apt-get update"和"apt install jq"
jq --version
```

```shell
export IGNORE_INFER_ERROR=1
# 进入 atb-models 目录
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# 运行切分及压缩脚本
torchrun --nproc_per_node {TP 数} -m examples.convert.model_slim.sparse_compressor --model_path {W8A8S 量化权重路径} --save_directory {W8A8SC 量化权重路径}
```
- The number of TP is the number of tensor parallel parallels
- Note: If the weight is generated with TP=2 for segmentation, it also needs to be run with TP=2.
- Example
```shell
torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 -m examples.convert.model_slim.sparse_compressor --model_path /data1/weights/model_slim/Llama-8b_w8a8s --save_directory /data1/weights/model_slim/Llama-8b_w8a8sc
```

## Installation

Guide users to install MindIE on a physical machine. Please choose whl package or run package to install according to the actual situation.

This section introduces the steps to install MindIE through whl package. The following takes installing MindIE LLM as an example.

1. To ensure the security of file permissions after installation, please execute the following command to set permissions: `old_umask=$(umask) umask 027 `
2. Execute the following command to install the whl package. `pip install mindie_llm-{version}-{python_tag}-{platform_tag}.whl --no-deps `

```1. After the installation is completed, if the following information is printed, the software installation is successful: `Successfully installed xxx ` `xxx` represents the actual software package name installed.

```bash
若python版本是3.11，则默认安装路径为：`/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages`
```1. Execute the following command to restore permissions. `umask $old_umask `

This article introduces the steps to install MindIE through the run package method. This method will install the components of MindIE Motor, MindIE LLM and MindIE SD in sequence. The path of the component package is under the sub-path of MindIE.

1. Log in to the installation environment as the installation user of the CANN software package.
2. Upload the obtained MindIE software package to any path in the installation environment (such as /home/package).
3. Enter the path where the software package is located. `cd /home/package `
4. Add executable permissions to the software package. `chmod +x 软件包名.run ` **Software package name.run** indicates the development kit package Ascend-mindie_\_linux-\_\.run. Please replace it according to the actual package name.
5. Run the following command to add the environment variables of the ascend-toolkit package. (Take the root user as an example. The following is the default installation path for the root user.) `source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh `
6. Run the following command to verify the consistency and completeness of the software package installation file. `./软件包名.run --check `
7. Execute the following command to install the software (the following command supports parameters such as `--install-path=<path>`, please see [软件包参数说明](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/faq_and_appendixes/software_package_options/) for detailed parameter description). "/home/{current user name}/Ascend" The detailed log path of the software package installation is as follows. Root user: "/var/log/mindie_log/mindie_install.log" Non-root user: "/home/{current user name}/var/log/mindie_log/mindie_install.log" During the installation process, the aie_tmp_source folder will be temporarily generated in the current directory and will be deleted after the installation is completed. If there is currently a folder with the same name, it will be deleted after installation. By executing the above command, you agree to the terms and conditions of [华为企业业务最终用户许可协议（EULA）](https://e.huawei.com/cn/about/eula) by default. After the installation is completed, if the following information is printed, the software installation is successful: `xxx install success ` `xxx` represents the actual software package name installed.
8. (Optional) Run the following command to query the software version number. Take the default installation path as an example:
```bash
cat /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/version.info
```1. Configure environment variables Currently, a process-level environment variable setting script is provided for users to reference in the process to automatically complete environment variable settings. It will automatically expire after the user process ends. Examples are as follows: Configure environment variables in the default installation path of root users: `source /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh ` Configure environment variables in the default installation path of non-root users: `source /home/{当前用户名}/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh ` Users can also set permanent environment variables by modifying the ~/.bashrc file. The operation is as follows: `a. 以运行用户在任意目录下执行`vi \~/.bashrc`命令，打开.bashrc文件，在文件最后一行后面添加上述内容。 b. 执行`:wq!`命令保存文件并退出。 c. 执行`source \~/.bashrc`命令使其立即生效。 `

Please refer to the following command to install:

Description

For the Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module, the operating system compatibility requirements of the host and container image are as follows:

- Ubuntu 22.04 host supports running Ubuntu 24.04 container image
- openEuler 22.03 host supports running openEuler 24.03 container image

Please select a compatible container image version based on the host operating system.

#### Get MindIE image [](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#%E8%8E%B7%E5%8F%96mindie%E9%95%9C%E5%83%8F)

4. Download the image according to the image download operation guide page that pops up, as shown in [图1](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#figure1). **Figure 1** Mirror download

1. Execute the following corresponding commands according to the device form to start the container. The container startup command is for reference only and can be modified according to your needs. The command parameters are introduced as shown in [表1](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/image_usage_guide/#table1). **Atlas 800I A3 Inference Server** `bash docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=500g \ # 对于多模态理解模型，若业务最大并发数较高，--shm-size建议设置不小于100g --name <container-name> \ -w /home \ --device=/dev/davinci0:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci1:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci2:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci3:rwm \ --device=/dev/davinci_manager:rwm \ --device=/dev/hisi_hdc:rwm \ --device=/dev/devmm_svm:rwm \ -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver:ro \ -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi:ro \ -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi:ro \ -v /usr/local/sbin/:/usr/local/sbin:ro \ -v /home/weight:/home/weight:ro \ {IMAGE_ID} bash` Description `{IMAGE_ID}` is the image ID. After the image is installed, execute the `docker images` command to view the corresponding ID. Just replace it in the above command. For the `--device` parameter, the mounting permission is set to `rwm` instead of `rw` or `r` with smaller permissions. information and run the MindIE business normally but if the mounted If the npu (corresponding to `davinci_xxx_` in the mount option, for example, `npu0` corresponds to `davinci0`) is occupied by other tasks, using the `npu-smi` command will print an error and the MindIE task cannot be run (`torch.npu.set_device()` will fail at this time). >- For the Atlas 800I A3 super node server, if the mount permission is set to `rw`, after entering the container, an error will be printed when using the `npu-smi` command,the MindIE task cannot be run (`torch.npu.set_device()` will fail at this time). **Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module** When starting the container, you need to additionally mount some driver libraries and configuration files that npu-smi depends on. If it is not mounted, executing npu-smi related commands in the container may fail. The startup commands for different container image operating systems are as follows: Ubuntu 24.04 image: `docker run -it -d --net=host --shm-size=1g \ # 对于多模态理解模型，若业务最大并发数较高，若业务最大并发数较高， this parameter must be used in the start container command to lift the limit on the number of processes. -it means starting an interactive terminal (-i) and connecting it to the standard input and output (-t) of the container, enabling interaction with the inside of the container, such as running command line operations. -d indicates that the container will run in background mode, that is, the container is started in the background. Using this parameter will not block the current terminal operation,you can continue to perform other operations after starting the container. --net indicates that the container will use the host's network configuration (network sharing), allowing the container to directly access the host's network interface, which is suitable for scenarios that require low latency and direct access to network resources. --shm-size indicates the shared memory (/dev/shm) size of the specified container, which can be set by the user. 1g is an example value. For multi-modal understanding models, if the maximum number of business concurrencies is high, it is recommended that --shm-size be set to no less than 100g. This value cannot exceed the total remaining physical memory of the host,can be viewed using the `free -h` command. When data parallelism is enabled (that is, when DP>1), the shared memory size needs to be adjusted as DP increases: When DP=2, shm-size is at least 2g. When DP=4, shm-size is at least 3g. When DP=8, shm-size is at least 5g. When DP=16, shm-size is at least 9g. --name means to specify a name for the container. \<container-name> is the identifier of the container, which can be set by yourself and is unique in the current system. If not set, Docker will automatically assign a random name. --device means mapping the host device to the container. Each --device parameter shares a host device (such as a hardware accelerator card or other hardware device) to the container so that the container can directly access it. /dev/davinci_manager: davinci related management equipment. /dev/hisi_hdc: hdc related management equipment. /dev/devmm_svm: Memory management related devices. /dev/ascend_manager: Ascend device management related devices. /dev/user_config: User configuration related equipment, which needs to be mounted when executing commands such as npu-smi in the Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module container. /dev/davinci*X*: NPU device, *X* is the ID number, such as: davinci0. You can query the device number and name according to the `ll /dev/ \| grep davinci` command, bind the device as needed,modify "--device=****" in the above command. -v indicates that the files or directories of the physical machine are mapped to the corresponding paths within the container,the ro parameter is used to set these directories to read-only permissions. /usr/local/Ascend/driver: This path contains hardware driver files. The driver is installed on the host and mapped to the container before it can be used in the container. Please modify it according to the actual path where the driver is located. /usr/local/sbin: This path contains NPU status viewing commands such as npu-smi. saved so that the container can access the weights. Please modify it according to the actual path. (The weight file and the data set file are placed in this path at the same time) For the Atlas 200I Pro acceleration module, additional files or directories that npu-smi related commands depend on need to be mounted according to the container image operating system: /etc/sys_version.conf: system version configuration file. /etc/ld.so.conf.d/mind_so.conf: dynamic library search path configuration file. /etc/hdcBasic.cfg: hdc basic configuration file. /var/dmp_daemon: Directory related to dmp_daemon running. /usr/local/sbin/npu-smi: npu-smi command. /usr/local/Ascend/driver/lib64: driver dynamic library directory. /etc/slog.conf, /var/slogd: log configuration file and log running directory. /usr/lib64/libmmpa.so, /usr/lib64/libcrypto.so.1.1, /usr/lib64/libstackcore.so: general dynamic libraries that npu-smi depends on. /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libyaml-0.so.2: The libyaml dynamic library that npu-smi depends on under the Ubuntu 24.04 image. /usr/lib64/libyaml-0.so.2.0.9: The libyaml dynamic library that npu-smi depends on under the openEuler 24.03 image. /usr/lib64/libsemanage.so.2: The libsemanage dynamic library that npu-smi depends on under the openEuler 24.03 image.
2. Execute the following command to enter the container. `docker exec -it <container-name> bash `
3. Install dependencies. Before using the model for inference, you need to install the corresponding dependencies. The path of the dependency installation file (requirements_*xxx*.txt) of each model is /usr/local/Ascend/atb-models/requirements/models. Taking the LLaMA3 series model as an example, use the following command to install the dependencies. `cd /usr/local/Ascend/atb-models/requirements/models pip3 install -r requirements_llama3.txt `
4. Execute the following command to enable MindIE log printing. `export MINDIE_LOG_TO_STDOUT="true" `
5. Use models for inference. Take the LLaMA3 series model as an example. For details, please refer to the instructions in "$ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH/examples/models/llama3/README.md" in the container. For other models, please refer to [模型列表](https://www.hiascend.com/software/mindie/modellist). Neural networks are 2024-11-18 11:08:13,291 [INFO] [pid: 389497] logging.py-180: Generate[0] token num: (0, 20) ` If the user wants to customize the input question, he can use the "--input_texts" parameter setting, such as: `python examples/run_pa.py --model_path /path-to-weights --input_texts "What is deep learning?" # 请修改权重路径 ` Note "$ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH" has been set in ".bashrc", there is no need to set it yourself.
6. MindIE Motor is an inference service-oriented framework for general model scenarios. It provides inference service-oriented capabilities through an open and scalable inference service-oriented platform architecture, supports docking with the industry's mainstream inference framework interfaces,meets the high-performance inference requirements of large language models. For the method of connecting to Motor, please refer to [快速入门](https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/quick_start/quick_start/#%E6%A8%A1%E5%9E%8B%E6%8E%A8%E7%90%86).

## Prerequisites

### Characteristic Matrix

- The following table shows the features supported by each version of the Llama model

| Model and parameter quantity | FP16 | BF16 | Flash Attention | Paged Attention | W8A8 quantization | W8A16 quantization | KV cache quantization | MOE quantization | MindIE Service | TGI | Long sequence | prefix_cache | FA3 Quantization | functioncall | Multi LoRA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

Note: The supported world size shown in the table is a configuration that can be run through the dialogue test. In actual operation, the video memory usage caused by the length of the input sequence must also be considered.

### Weight

**Weight download**

-[DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B/tree/main)

### Path variable explanation

| Variable name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| working_dir | The directory where the acceleration library and model library are placed after downloading (only used in source code download scenarios) |
| llm_path | ATB_Models The path where the model warehouse is located. If you use a mirror, the path is `/usr/local/Ascend/atb-models`; if you use the code downloaded by gitcode, the path is `${working_dir}/MindIE-LLM/examples/atb_models/` |
| script_path | The path where the script is located; the path where the working script of the Llama3 series is located is `${llm_path}/examples/models/llama3` |
| weight_path | Model weight path |

- Generate quantified weight dependency msModelSlim tool, see [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) for installation method

- The quantified weights are generated uniformly using the `${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}/examples/convert/model_slim/quantifier.py` script. The following provides a quick start command for Llama model quantified weight generation.
- Please use the following command to generate W8A8 quantified weights
```shell
# 设置 CANN 包的环境变量
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
# 关闭虚拟内存
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False
# 进入 atb-models 目录
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B 量化，有回退层，antioutlier 使用 m1 算法配置，使用 min-max 量化方式，校准数据集使用 50 条 BoolQ 数据，在 NPU 上进行运算
bash examples/models/llama3/generate_quant_weight.sh -src {浮点权重路径} -dst {W8A8 量化权重路径} -type llama3.1_8b_w8a8
```

**Step 1 Generate W8A8S quantified weight**

- Modify the `torch_dtype` field in the model weight config.json to `float16`
- Generate quantified weight dependency msModelSlim tool, see [msmodelslim](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim) for installation method
- Enter the `msmodelslim/example/Llama` directory to execute the quantization script
```shell
# 运行量化转换脚本
python3 quant_llama.py --model_path {浮点权重路径} --save_directory {W8A8S 量化权重路径} --calib_file ../common/boolq.jsonl --w_bit 4 --a_bit 8 --fraction 0.011 --co_sparse True
```
**Step 2 Quantitative weight segmentation and compression**

```shell
# 执行"jq --version"查看是否安装 jq，若返回"bash：jq：command not found"，则依次执行"apt-get update"和"apt install jq"
jq --version
```

```shell
export IGNORE_INFER_ERROR=1
# 进入 atb-models 目录
cd ${ATB_SPEED_HOME_PATH}
# 运行切分及压缩脚本
torchrun --nproc_per_node {TP 数} -m examples.convert.model_slim.sparse_compressor --model_path {W8A8S 量化权重路径} --save_directory {W8A8SC 量化权重路径}
```
- The number of TP is the number of tensor parallel parallels
- Note: If the weight is generated with TP=2 for segmentation, it also needs to be run with TP=2.
- Example
```shell
torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 -m examples.convert.model_slim.sparse_compressor --model_path /data1/weights/model_slim/Llama-8b_w8a8s --save_directory /data1/weights/model_slim/Llama-8b_w8a8sc
```

2. Upload the obtained MindIE software package to any path in the installation environment (such as /home/package).
3. Enter the path where the software package is located. `cd /home/package `
4. Add executable permissions to the software package. `chmod +x 软件包名.run ` **Software package name.run** indicates the development kit package Ascend-mindie_\_linux-\_\.run. Please replace it according to the actual package name.

After the installation is completed, if the following information is printed, the software installation is successful: `xxx install success ` `xxx` represents the actual software package name installed.
8. (Optional) Run the following command to query the software version number. Take the default installation path as an example:
```bash
cat /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/latest/version.info
```1. Configure environment variables Currently, a process-level environment variable setting script is provided for users to reference in the process to automatically complete environment variable settings. It will automatically expire after the user process ends. Examples are as follows: Configure environment variables in the default installation path of root users: `source /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh ` Configure environment variables in the default installation path of non-root users: `source /home/{当前用户名}/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh ` Users can also set permanent environment variables by modifying the ~/.bashrc file.
